News.title: Mystery deepens into death of unnamed woman found in bin bag near Premier League ground as cops reveal cryptic new clue
News.content:
Next

THE mystery surrounding the death of a woman found in a bin bag has deepened as baffled cops reveal a new clue to help catch her killer.

The body of an unnamed woman was discovered in Stanley Park, Liverpool, near Liverpool FC’s Anfield and Everton‘s Hill Dickinson stadiums, on August 28.



Cops raced to the scene at around 5.25pm after a member of public reported a black bin bag in the bushes of a walled garden.

Police are yet to identify the victim and have ruled out more than 70 names given to them on the back of the grim discovery.



Officers have now reconstructed an image of the woman’s face as they urge anyone who recognises her to come forward.

She is described as white, about 5ft 2in tall, and of small build with strawberry-blonde hair, and wearing a “distinctive” cerise pink Nike T-shirt at the time of death.

Cops initially believed the victim to be in her 70s, but have now expanded their enquiries to probe reports of women aged between 60 and 80.

The woman had no teeth and no DNA match was found, making identification difficult.



She was malnourished, although it is yet to be confirmed whether this was due to neglect or ageing.

The victim is also said to have suffered from osteoporosis, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, and arthritis in her hands.

Police believe the first confirmed sighting of the bin bag was on July 13 – six weeks before her body was found.



Detectives from Merseyside Police’s Major Incident Team continue to probe how the tragedy unfolded.

Working with Face Lab at Liverpool’s John Moore’s University, an image of what police believe the deceased woman looked like has been released.

Detective Superintendent Rachel Wilson said: “I am grateful for the expert work that the team have done at Face Lab have done to develop this image.

“This work takes some time to complete but we believe that we have a representative image of the woman. Now we need to know who she is.

“Do you recognise her or think you have seen her prior to 13 July? Do you have any information which could assist our enquiries? Please come forward and speak to us or if you don’t want to speak to the police then contact Crimestoppers anonymously.



“It is vital that we identify this woman and get the answers as to who was responsible for her murder.”

She added: “We hope that the image of the woman combined with the physical description, clothing and ailments will jog someone’s memory. If you have information please get in touch with us as a matter of urgency.”

Professor Caroline Wilkinson, who is Director at Face Lab, said: “Face Lab is a centre of excellence relating to craniofacial identification and digital heritage.

“The Face Lab team have created a facial depiction to inspire recognition and assist the police in the identification of this woman and the forensic investigation into her death.

“The depiction was produced using our 3D computerised facial reconstruction system following anatomical and anthropometrical standards and the final image was created using photo-editing.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Anyone who recognises the woman in the image is urged to call 101 quoting reference number 26000706383.

If you do not feel comfortable speaking to police directly, you can contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Tragedy as body found in marshland during search for missing bride-to-be, 29, who vanished two weeks ago
News.content:
Next

A BODY has been found in marshland during the search for a missing bride-to-be who vanished two weeks ago.

Eren Wright, 29, was engaged when she went missing from her home in Lytham, Lancashire, on Tuesday, October 27.



Police said a body was discovered in marshland off the coast between Lytham and Warton on Thursday at around 3.30pm.

Formal identification is still yet to take place but officers believe it to be Eren and her loved ones have been informed.



The 29-year-old’s death is not being treated as suspicious and a file is due to be passed to HM Coroner.

Wright was first reported missing from her home on St David’s Road South in Lytham St Annes by her fiance Silas O’Carroll Pond on the day she disappeared.



Earlier that morning, she was seen at about 10.30am on Clifton Drive South, at its junction with St Anne’s Road West.

CCTV then suggested she travelled into Lytham town centre before taking a bus to St Annes.



Footage of her last known movements released by cops showed her walking by a road dressed in a light olive-green hoodie.

Officers believed Eren may then have travelled to the Fairhaven Lake area, between Lytham and St Annes, where she could have been from about 5.30pm.

Today, a police spokesperson said: “Many of you will have heard about missing Eren Wright, and our enquiries to locate her.

“At around 3:30pm yesterday police search teams located a body in marshland off the coast between Lytham and Warton.

“Whilst formal identification has not yet taken place, we do believe it to be Eren.



“Her loved ones have been informed and are being supported. Our thoughts are with them at this devastating time.

“Eren’s death is not being treated as suspicious and a file will be passed in due course to HM Coroner.”

They added: “We ask that you respect that Eren’s loved ones have just been given some of the worst news imaginable so please refrain from speculating online or otherwise.”

News.title: Moment driver hits 75mph before mowing down and killing boy, 12, in hit-and-run crash as he walked home from school
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a BMW driver hits 75mph before mowing down and killing a schoolboy as he walked home from school in a horror hit-and-run.

Aleksanders Dolars – also known as Dolars Aleksanders – ploughed into 12-year-old Keaton Slater in Coventry, West Midlands on June 14, 2024.



After leaving him for dead, the callous driver then sped off from the scene and abandoned his motor around six miles away.

Paramedics raced to the scene on Radford Road but the youngster had sustained fatal injuries and could not be saved.



Dolars then fled to Latvia where he was tracked down by police and extradited back to the UK to face justice.

He was arrested at Gatwick Airport in August and went on to admit causing death by dangerous driving.

Today, Dolars was jailed for nine years and four months and banned from driving for over 16 years at Warwick Crown Court.

After the case, Keaton’s family paid heartbreaking tributes to their “beautiful boy”.



The 12-year-old’s mum Louise said: “Keaton was our world. He was funny, caring, loving and full of life. He had the biggest smile and a heart full of kindness.

“He brought happiness into our home simply by being himself. The day Keaton was killed was the day our family stopped being whole.

“There are no words that can properly describe the pain of losing a child. It is heartbreak that never leaves you.

“When Keaton walked out of our door that day, we expected him to come home. We never imagined that we were watching him leave for the last time.

“It is not only Keaton who died that day. A part of all of us as a family died with him. Our lives changed forever, and nothing will ever be the same again.”



Louise added that the circumstances of her son’s death “have made our grief even harder to bear”.

“Knowing that the person responsible did not stop to help our son is something we will never understand. Keaton was left behind,” she continued.

“I cannot understand how anyone could leave a child who had just been struck and not stop to help him. That knowledge has added another layer of pain to an already unbearable loss.



“He should have had the chance to grow up, fall in love, have a career, make mistakes, achieve his dreams, watch football, play football, grow old and have a family of his own. All of those possibilities were taken away from him.

“I want Keaton to be remembered for the beautiful boy he was – for his smile, his kindness, his love of football, his laughter and the love he gave to everyone around him.”

Keaton’s father Clint said: “The bond I had with Keaton is something that is impossible to put fully into words.

“He was a huge part of my life, my heart and my world. He was someone I loved beyond measure, and I always believed that I would have a lifetime ahead of me to watch him grow, to guide him, to laugh with him, and to make more memories with him.

“Keaton was a passionate Coventry City supporter. He loved his football and followed his team with real passion.



“His untimely death has taken away the joy he would have had seeing his beloved team reach the Premier League.

“It is another future moment that he should have been here to experience, another thing that he will never get chance to celebrate.

“Keaton was loved. He mattered. He was more than what happened to him. He was my son, my best friend, my little mini me. I will miss him for the rest of my life.”

Detective Chief Inspector Sam Lewis, of West Midlands Police, said: “Keaton was a 12-year-old boy, making his way home from school, and he should have been able to arrive back safely.

“The driver was travelling at excessive speed and rather than stop and help Keaton he just left and tried to avoid capture.”



“We kept fighting for Keaton and through plenty of persistence, hard work and patience we finally got there,” he added.

“We’re grateful for all the support we received during this investigation, from members of the Coventry community who provided information to the other agencies who also worked tirelessly to ensure Aleksanders could be charged with his awful crime.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We’re especially grateful to Louise and Clint, Keaton’s brothers, and the wider family for their support during what has been a long and difficult process.

“This was always about getting justice for Keaton and together we’ve managed to do that.”

News.title: Driver and two horses killed after cars crash into loose animals on motorway
News.content:
HORROR SMASH Driver and two horses killed after cars crash into loose animals on motorway







Next

A DRIVER and two horses have been tragically killed after two cars hit the loose animals on a motorway.

Two Skodas smashed into the steeds on the M18 in Doncaster in the early hours of Friday November 13.



Police raced to the scene at 4.44am where a 50-year-old driver of one of the cars, a blue Skoda Superb, was sadly pronounced dead.

His family have been informed as cops probe how the tragedy unfolded.



A blue Skoda Octavia hit one of the horses before a Vauxhall Nivara crashed into the other, with both drivers suffering minor injuries.

Police are searching for the owners of the loose horses, one described as black and the other grey.

Any witnesses of the collision have been urged to come forward as cops appeal for dashcam footage.

A spokesperson for South Yorkshire Police said: “At 4.44am today (Friday 13 November) we were called to reports of a collision at junction four of the motorway.

“Officers responded to initial reports of two collisions involving two horses and two Skoda vehicles.

“Initial enquiries have led officers to understand that a Blue Skoda Octavia was in collision with one horse, and a blue Skoda Superb was in collision with a second horse who were loose in the carriageway.



“Following the collision involving the Skoda vehicles, a second collision has occurred involving a Vauxhall Vivaro and one of the horses.

“The driver of Skoda Superb, a 50-year-old man was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

“His family has been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this time.

“The driver of a Skoda Octavia and Vauxhall Vivaro suffered injuries that are not believed to be life threatening.

“Both horses also died at the scene.”



They added: “We are now asking for any witnesses, who have not yet spoken to police to come forward, and anyone with dashcam footage to share it.

“We would also like to speak to the owner of the horses, who has not yet come forward.

“One horse is black and one horse is grey in colour. Further enquiries are on-going around the horses and their owners, but anyone missing two horses or who may know who they belong to is asked to contact us.”

News.title: Girl, 4, dies after being caned, starved & forced to sleep in plant pot before body burned in oil drum
News.content:
TORTURED TO DEATH Girl, 4, dies after being caned, starved & forced to sleep in plant pot before body burned in oil drum







Next

A FOUR-YEAR-OLD girl has died after being caned, starved and forced to sleep in a plant pot – as adults filmed the horrific torture.

Megan Khun’s body was burned in an oil drum after she was beaten and humiliated during months of abuse.



Three people have been jailed for the vile torture of the child leading to her death.

Nouvelle Chua Ruoshi, 36, sobbed as she was sentenced to 13 years for conspiring to abuse Megan, disposing of her body and drug use.





Chua, who had a child of her own, watched as Megan was abused by her mum Foo Li Ping and Foo’s boyfriend Wong Shi Xiang, the court heard.

Instead of getting help for the little girl, she filmed the abuse, even helping to hide her injuries on at least six occasions.

Foo was jailed for 19 years and Xiang was put behind bars for 30 years for their roles in the torture of the child.

The court heard Megan had her head shaved and was made to sleep outside in a plant pot at the couple’s flat in Paya Lebar, Singapore.



Evil Chua suggested to her mum that the starving girl could eat mucus after she complained she was hungry, the court heard.

The evil abuser mum then blew her nose and smeared the snot onto her daughter’s tongue.

Chua even helped parade the screaming girl in public while she had red marks drawn across her face, as a punishment for playing with makeup.



She filmed the cruel torture to be used against the little girl in future, the court heard.

The girl died in February 2020 when her mum’s boyfriend Wong punched her in the stomach so violently that her back was sent slamming into a wall.

Chua came to the flat in the middle of the night to find Megan lying on the floor in pain.

When she told Foo and Wong about the little girl’s pain, the pair dismissed Megan’s suffering as attention-seeking.

But instead of taking the girl to the doctors, all three adults took drugs together in the living room.



The child was found unresponsive hours later.

Instead of reporting the death, the three conspired to keep Megan’s body in the flat for months, conjuring up an evil plan for how to get rid of it.

Chua bought vinegar and incense sticks to try and hide the smell of the decaying remains.

On 8 May 2020, she helped Wong and Foo transport the body to an open area in Ubi, Singapore.

While Boyfriend Wong burned the child’s body in a metal barrel, Foo and Chua threw paper offerings into the flames.



Justice S Mohan rejected Chua’s claims she had been no more than a passive witness to the torture, saying she had recorded Megan in “extreme states of deprivation”, including while naked.

He sentenced her to six years and six months for conspiring to abuse Megan, five years and six months for disposing of her body and another year for drug consumption.

The three sentences will run consecutively.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chua had pleaded guilty to the offences.

Megan’s prolonged abuse and death sparked a review of Singapore’s child protection system, which found serious shortcomings in the agencies responsible for her welfare.

News.title: ‘Unplanned day off’ memes flood the internet as workers celebrate the ‘Great Microsoft Outage of 2026’
News.content:
Next

MICROSOFT’S data outage caused major disruptions to thousands of users across the globe – with the issue now largely resolved.

But while services, including GPs, schools and police forces in the UK were affected, office workers instead revelled in the email-free day.

For the past 20 hours, Microsoft has experienced a major global outage, leading to communication platforms such as Microsoft Outlook to remain down.



But, office workers instead took to social media, appearing on the likes of Facebook, Instagram and X, to rejoice in the inability to send emails.



Users shared images on X of them holding bottles of wine, teasing that while they couldn’t work, they might as well drink.

Another quipped that with emails down, people have “rediscovered the long lost art of picking up the phone”.



Meanwhile, an X user shared an image of Clippy, the long-retired Microsoft Word mascot that was famously canned for its uselessness, captioned: “Clippy’s revenge.”

Another sarcastically joked “oh noo microsoft is down and I can’t do my work, nooooo”, alongside a picture of a crying mask – in front of a smiling one.



Others instead turned to the classic “intern” joke – with one Instagram user pretending to be Microsoft’s intern on their first day on the job and “accidentally” tripping on a wire.

“Hopefully nothing bad happens,” they wrote.

Some are even calling the incident “the Great Microsoft Outage of 2026“, alongside images of them using a fax machines.

But not all office workers could get in on the fun – although Microsoft Outlook was severely disrupted, Gmail services remained fully functional.



This led to some posting the iconic Squidward meme, as he looks out at Patrick and Spongebob enjoying themselves outside.

And some brands got in on the joke too, although of course Microsoft was too busy attempting to fix the problem to make light of the situation.

In the UAE, Emirates shared an Instagram post showing an A380 above the clouds and the caption: “Your email might be down, but the skies are always open.”



Meanwhile, KitKat joked that Outlook had taken a break, ending with a mock error message telling users to “Have a KIT KAT and please try again later.”

Major UK supermarkets also posted their versions of the meme, with Aldi UK posting on Facebook that “Microsoft being down is the equivalent of an adult snow day right?!”.

9 Source: X – @TylerJRodney

Domino’s also added a picture of their own pizza shop in chaos, with the caption: “live scenes at Microsoft head office”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the latest update from the tech giant, it confirmed the cause of “one of the biggest IT outages ever” as an “underlying bug” issue.

“Now, the underlying bug has been addressed and, due to a large volume of queued work, we are gradually bringing customers and regions back online,” it added.

News.title: Outrage as jailed husband, 32, who pushed pregnant wife to her death off 980ft cliff is FREED after six years
News.content:
WALKS FREE Outrage as jailed husband, 32, who pushed pregnant wife to her death off 980ft cliff is FREED after six years







Next

A HUSBAND jailed for life for pushing his seven-month pregnant wife to death off a 980ft cliff walked free after just six years behind bars.

Hakan Aysal was convicted of murdering his wife Semra, 32, after she plunged from a towering cliff at Turkey’s famous Butterfly Valley in June 2018.



But in a shock ruling, the country’s Supreme Court has ordered his release following a review of the case causing furious backlash.

Aysal spent six years locked up, including around four years in solitary confinement, according to his lawyer.



The case sparked widespread attention after it emerged he had taken out a £7,000 accident insurance policy naming himself as the beneficiary.

Prosecutors accused Aysal of luring his pregnant wife to the picturesque beauty spot under the guise of a romantic holiday before pushing her to her death.

They claimed he then attempted to cash in on the insurance policy following the fatal plunge, but his application was blocked.

Shocking footage captured by a tourist nearby shows the moments before the evil push.

Aysal was seen holding Semra’s hand as they headed down the cliff towards the sea.

The convict has always denied murdering his wife, insisting she had vanished when he turned his back.



He told the court: “When I turned back, my wife was not there.

“I looked down the cliff and ran around looking for her.

“I did not push my wife.”



The husband claimed the insurance policy had been taken out because the couple shared an interest in extreme sports.

But in February 2022, he was handed a 30-year life sentence, which he challenged with a last-minute insanity plea.

The court rejected his appeal and upheld the sentence.

His conviction came despite the presiding judge disagreeing with the verdict and arguing that Aysal should be acquitted.

The ruling was later challenged, with a Supreme Court prosecutor questioning the lack of direct evidence linking him to his wife’s death.



Concerns were also raised over the circumstances surrounding the insurance policy that had become central to the prosecution’s case.

Now, Turkey’s Supreme Court Criminal General Assembly has ordered Aysal’s release, bringing his six-year ordeal behind bars to an end.

His lawyer, Mehmet Buğra Çiçek, welcomed the decision as a “fair and correct ruling”.



He said: “The six years of unjust detention my client endured, approximately four of them alone in a cell, have come to an end today.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the dramatic decision does not mean Aysal has been cleared of his wife’s murder.

The case remains subject to further legal examination, leaving the circumstances surrounding Semra’s fatal plunge unresolved.

News.title: Coronation Street & Casualty star Eric Potts AVOIDS jail after being caught with sickening stash of child sex abuse pics
News.content:
WALKING FREE Coronation Street & Casualty star Eric Potts AVOIDS jail after being caught with sickening stash of child sex abuse pics







Next

FORMER Corrie actor Eric Potts dodged jail today after pleading guilty to child sex offences.

The married 61-year-old – best known as Diggory Compton on the Cobbles – admitted to being obsessed with 15-year-old boys.



Burnley Crown Court heard how he was caught with a total of 83 videos and pictures on his iPad when police raided his home in Bacup, Lancs, in October last year.

Potts, who also featured in Brookside and Casualty, was given a 26-month prison sentence, suspended for 30 months.



The disgraced star was also handed a Sexual Harm Prevention Order which includes banning him from being alone with any boy under the age of 16.

Judge Daniel Prowse told him: “Some of these images and videos featured children as young as 11 or 12.



“Each of these children in these videos is a real child somewhere in the world and each of them is either being required to abuse another child or is themselves being sexually abused.

“Make no mistake, these images that you have were of children being sexually abused and the impact on them is magnified when these images are shared.



“A conversation between you and another man on the application Telegram was also discovered and, in what is a sexually explicit conversation, you say you are attracted to teenage boys around the ages of 15 and 16.”

Potts pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing to three offences of making indecent images of a child and three offences of distributing indecent images of a child.

Seven of those are Category A, the most serious classification, which often displays penetrative sexual activity.

Another 16 images Potts hoarded were in Category B and 60 are Category C.

Prosecutors also said the married father-of-two shared five images on a single day on July 16, 2024.



Burnley crown court heard how Potts now walks with the help of a walking stick after two failed suicide attempts following his arrest.

His 38-year-long marriage has also broken down.

Scots-born appeared in Corries as Diggory for 50 episodes in 2005 and 2006.

Speaking about the role in 2019, he said: “It was just a joy being part of such an iconic show.”

Raised in Irvine, Ayrshire, he switched from studying law at Glasgow University to train at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School from 1984.



He landed a two-year run in the Channel 4 soap Brookside from 1998 as oddball Mr Moore, a character briefly suspected of being a serial killer.

Other TV credits include Heartbeat, The Royal, Last of the Summer Wine, and BBC Scotland sitcom Still Game.

In 2005 he also appeared in an episode of Doctor Who.

He later had roles in Emmerdale between 2012 and 2018, and a part in Hollywood film Oz the Great and Powerful in 2013.

Away from the screen, Potts built a career as a panto dame and writer.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

In December 2011 he starred alongside Dame Edna Everage in Dick Whittington at the New Wimbledon Theatre in London.

News.title: Police investigating David Walliams over reports alleging serious sexual offences
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".

It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.

The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".

When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".

"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.

Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.

"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."

Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.

Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.

One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.

He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.

The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.

Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."

He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."

Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

News.title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech
News.content:
A critical Microsoft outage lasting more than 22 hours has raised questions about how heavily vital services rely on a handful of major tech firms.

The disruption, which affected Microsoft 365 services such as Outlook, was caused by routine automated checks that took some servers offline, overloading the remaining ones with traffic.

The recovery took nearly a full day while engineers gradually restored services, highlighting how embedded the tech giant's services are in modern society.

Flora Hamilton, executive director of the Small Business Charter, said the outage was a "stark reminder" of how much firms "rely on digital systems" - like Microsoft Outlook - "to keep their operations running".

"For many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), access to email is fundamental to everything from communicating with customers and suppliers to generating income," she said.

The disruption was not just confined to businesses, but also affected organisations and public institutions around the world.

Around 430 million people globally use Microsoft 365, and issues were reported across more than 70 countries.

The fallout from the outage had a wide-ranging effect, knocking out email systems for the US House of Representatives and Australian intelligence agencies, as well as disrupting court systems in Singapore and airline support desks in India.

Microsoft has since apologised for the issue, which it said was due to a technical failure rather than a cyber-attack.

Walter Pasquarelli, an AI strategist, told the BBC that for governments, businesses and critical infrastructure, the outage had "put their vulnerabilities and dependence in plain sight".

"Looking ahead, as AI assistants are plugged into our email, calendars and files, a failure like this may spread even further," he said.

News.title: Former Hamas bodyguard guilty of UK knife attack
News.content:
A former Hamas bodyguard, wanted in Germany over an alleged plot to murder Jewish people, has been found guilty of a knife attack on a bailiff outside his UK home.

Mohammed Alfatih, previously known as Mohammed Naim, was regularly seen acting as a bodyguard for a former leader of Hamas in 2006. He was granted asylum in the UK in 2015 and British citizenship in 2020.

The 40-year-old was found guilty by majority verdict of unlawfully wounding a bailiff who had come to repossess his wife's car, possession of two knives and criminal damage. He was cleared of wounding with intent.

Alfatih was under surveillance by a counter-terror unit at the moment he attacked the bailiff in Birmingham last year.

The son of a senior Hamas official, he could not be named during his trial due to reporting restrictions.

During the trial, footage was shown of Alfatih brandishing two large kitchen knives outside his home in the suburb of Kings Heath and trying to stab the bailiff as he drove away.

He told the court he chased the victim across the street to scare him away after his wife was asked to settle her debts of more than Â£2,250 linked to unpaid parking fines.

Her car had been clamped by the enforcement officer, who was involved in a struggle inside Alfatih's terraced home.

News.title: Watch: BBC undercover reporter is offered fake art and awards for talent visa
News.content:
A BBC undercover investigation into abuse of a fast-track UK immigration scheme has found companies offering to help migrants pose as talented artists and tech experts to make fraudulent visa applications.

The UK government's Global Talent visa was launched in 2020 to attract the "brightest and best" scientists and researchers from around the world. It is also open to creative artists.

We found one company offering fake art portfolios to wealthy migrants looking to cheat the system - for a large fee - which could be passed off as their own work.

Our politics investigations correspondent Billy Kenber reports.

News.title: Reform and Tory spokesmen in angry clash over immigration at Piddington
News.content:
A press conference led by Piddington Parish Council chairman Tim McNally took place on Friday after Housing Secretary Angela Rayner approved the Home Office's application to change the use of the site for asylum accommodation.

The Home Office said this would allow it to continue developing the plan but that no final decision on the site had been taken.

There has been significant local opposition to the proposal and a legal challenge to the planning decision is expected from the parish council.

In September, Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK over the planned use for the site in Oxfordshire.

Politicians from the Conservatives and Reform have made several visits to Piddington, a village of about 350 people, to show their support for campaigners.

Speaking on Friday, Philp said a future Conservative government would shut the asylum accommodation "straight away" if it was opened by Labour.

Yusuf made clear Reform's opposition to the plans before his focus switched to the Conservatives.

He said: "It's obviously true that we would not be gathered here today and 1,200 men would not be being dumped into this beautiful village were it not for the actions of the Conservative government.

"So I actually want to ask you Chris, would you actually like to apologise for the things you did in government to bring hundreds of thousands of people into this country illegally?"

Philp, a former immigration minister, described Yusuf's remarks as "disingenuous" and argued the migrants who could be housed near Piddington will have arrived in the country while Labour has been in power.

He said the Conservatives are under new leadership and he hoped the politicians could "stand in solidarity with the residents" rather than "engage in point scoring".

Philp added: "Zia, read the room, listen to the people clapping and read the room."

Yusuf countered that it was "important that we hold everybody accountable for this situation" and said Philp had been "heavily involved in immigration and borders policy" for the Conservatives in government.

Philp repeated his "read the room" suggestion, adding: "The public here want you to pipe down on the cheap politics."

Yusuf dismissed the suggestion that he was engaging in "cheap politics" and repeated his criticism of the Conservatives' record, saying they "refused" to secure the country's borders when in power.

As Yusuf spoke, Philp could be heard saying: "Buddy, I'm not here to give you comms advice, mate, you're in a hole stop digging."

Philp told Yusuf he should "calm down", with the Reform politician repeating his request for the Conservative MP to "apologise to the British people".

McNally thanked the pair for attending the press conference, adding: "I understand this is a passionate discussion and I respect you both for what you've got to do and what you represent."

While the two parties are on the right of politics, it is unusual for them to share a platform to campaign and both are keen to stress their differences to voters.

Reform leader Nigel Farage has pitched the party as replacing the "old, fuddy-duddy" Conservatives, and Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has said she would rather have another general election than do a deal with Reform to secure power.

News.title: Man jailed for grooming at least 70 girls online
News.content:
A man who groomed at least 70 girls and manipulated them into sending sexually explicit videos and images of themselves has been sentenced to 30 years in prison.

Bilal Kazi, 27, targeted his victims - aged between 10 and 17 - using apps including Snapchat, Wink and Roblox between August 2021 and August 2025.

Kazi, a student from India who was studying at the University of Chester, posed as a 14-year-old white British teenage boy and made his victims believe they were in a relationship with him.

He was jailed after pleading guilty to 37 charges including making indecent images, blackmail and inciting a child to engage in sexual activity.

Warning: This article contains distressing information

Kazi must serve a minimum of 20 years in prison before being eligible for parole and will be on the sex offenders register for life.

Once eligible for parole he will be on licence for eight years.

In a personal impact statement read out at Chester Crown Court earlier, one victim said she had struggled with anxiety as Kazi, who later moved to Birmingham, had "taken away a sense of privacy and security".

"I am doing my best to move forward but the effects are still with me," she said.

"The harm caused is not limited to the time events took place - they continue to affect my daily life."

The court heard that some of the victims had attempted suicide, struggled with anxiety and developed eating disorders.

One victim, who was 13 years old when Kazi first contacted her, said he took her "innocence away".

"I hope one day I can get on with my life," she said.

News.title: More women make allegations against Russell Brand
News.content:
Warning - this story contains graphic content

More women have come forward to make allegations about disgraced entertainer Russell Brand, in interviews with the Times and a new Netflix documentary.

Brand was jailed earlier this week after being found guilty of one count of rape and three of sexual assault at a trial in London.

Allegations against him first emerged after an investigation by the Times, the Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches in 2023.

The Times has now reported, external accusations of what it called sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by a further six women, which the newspaper said could not be reported until the criminal case had ended. He has denied non-consensual sexual activity.

The Times report was published on Thursday evening, and a Netflix documentary, titled Russell Brand: Open Secret, was made available on Friday morning.

The programme included an interview with a woman referred to as Emily, not her real name, who said she was in a relationship with Brand when she was in her twenties.

On one occasion, she said she "literally begged" Brand to stop after he refused to wear a condom during sex.

Emily, who was portrayed by an actress in the documentary, said: "I said to him, 'No, Russell, please, let's just use protection.' I kept saying 'No'. I said, 'Stop Russell, stop, please don't, please.'

"I begged him. I literally begged him. I tried to kick him off, I tried to draw my knees back, to kick him in his belly, but he was too strong for me."

But he "just pinned my hands back behind my head" before forcing himself upon her, she alleged.

"When it happens you just feel like, is this... is this rape? Because I'm with this guy [in a relationship]," she said, according to the documentary.

"I know I said 'No', but you question yourself and you think, did I do something wrong?"

She "left his as quickly as I could" and told one friend what had happened, but "back then women felt shamed", she said.

"You didn't talk about it. I just felt completely violated and unseen and unheard. I was saying 'No'. I kept saying, 'No, stop, please, stop, stop, no'."

News.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
News.content:
How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang?

The answer is very.

The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China.

Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China.

Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities.

But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country.

Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits.

But that relationship now looks rather more complicated.

News.title: NHS, schools and police forces hit by Microsoft outage
News.content:
Key services across the UK, including the NHS, GPs and schools, have been affected by a global Microsoft outage.

Pharmacies and businesses have also been hit after email and messaging services went down.

NHS England said patients should still attend appointments unless told otherwise, while several large police forces are urging the public to call if they want to report a crime.

Microsoft said services were now gradually being restored globally after a problem caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers, but users could still experience disruption.

The government said it was working closely with the firm to assess any impact on its services, while local authorities warned that some council services were being affected.

The full extent of the impact of the outage - which is affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot - and the time it will take to restore the systems remains unclear hours after users first reported issues.

Some 430 million people use the online tools worldwide.

The chief executive of the NHS Alliance, which represents the healthcare system in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, said the outage was affecting some services including emails.

NHS trusts in England were enacting measures to minimise disruption to critical services, a spokesperson said.

Patients have been told to continue to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111 by phone or online, or their local pharmacy.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains. Practices in Hampshire and Shropshire have told patients to phone them or come into the surgery if they have an urgent need.

News.title: Eleanor Donaldson given supervision order and placed on sex offenders' register
News.content:
The wife of former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader and convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Donaldson has been placed under a supervision order for three years.

Appearing before Newry Crown Court, via video link, for the first time since 2025, a tearful Eleanor Donaldson was also told she would be placed on the sex offenders' register for five years.

When Judge Paul Ramsey asked if she understood that she would be subjected to a supervision treatment order (STO), she nodded her head and said "yes".

Eleanor Donaldson could not be given a prison sentence as she faced a 'trial of the facts' as it was determined she was medically unfit for a criminal trial.

She was found to have done the acts in relation to five charges, including four of aiding and abetting her husband's offending.

Last month Jeffrey Donaldson was sentenced to 15 years in prison for a series of child sex offences against two victims, including one count of rape, which took place between 1985 and 2008. He is seeking to appeal against his convictions.

News.title: 'Hardest challenge of my life' - Owain Wyn Evans completes Children in Need ride
News.content:
Presenter Owain Wyn Evans has completed his challenge of cycling through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.

The Welsh host of BBC Radio 2's Early Breakfast Show rode almost 400 miles, setting off from Glasgow and finishing in Cardiff on Friday.

The challenge started on 9 November in Scotland and over the next five days, Owain rode through Northern Ireland, England and Wales and raised Â£3,853,530 in the process.

Reflecting on his journey, he said: "This has been the hardest challenge of my life, 100%.

"I can't believe I'm here. It's overwhelming, all the love and passion and commitment people have shown."

The BBC said Owain's challenge would be the "greatest-ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.

He crossed the finish line in Cardiff's Central Square just after 11:00 GMT, and was greeted by a crowd cheering him on before he was met by his husband, Arran Rees.

Owain, 42, whose bike was named Shania Chain, and decked out in Children in Need colours - Pudsey's favourite yellow with coloured spots - said: "Thank you so much everyone, from me and Shania.

"Honestly, this has felt so far away for such a long time. I can't believe that I'm here with this welcome and the sun's out."

Hollywood actor Luke Evans announced the route to Owain each day on BBC Radio 2.

During the 640km feat, he was also surprised with the premiere of Steps' brand-new version of their debut hit 5, 6, 7, 8, retitled 5, 6, 7, donate, which featured new lyrics and extra vocals.

It was recorded to help boost Owain's spirits on the longest day of his challenge.

News.title: Tories pay artist for Burnham images after legal threat
News.content:
The Conservatives have agreed to pay an artist who threatened to sue the party after it used his illustration of Andy Burnham to mock the prime minister.

Stanley Chow posted on Facebook that the party had used the picture - which Burnham has used on social media - without permission.

He had sought legal advice and threatened to take action against the party. It is understood the Tories agreed to pay a Â£1,000 fee for use of the image - and contributed an unknown sum to Chow's legal fees.

The Conservatives had distributed water bottles with the image on them - accusing Burnham of being a "bottler".

Chow posted on Facebook: "The Conservative Party have settled after their recent indiscretion of using my image without my permission."

He added: "Maybe ask firstâ¦ admittedly I would have said no, but it would have been a damn sight cheaper for the Tory Party if they just hired any illustrator to do their take on a cartoon of Burnhamâ¦ hopefully this a lesson learned. Copyright matters."

A Conservative spokesman said: "The Conservative Party values the importance of intellectual property in the creative industries. We consider this matter closed."

News.title: Man dies after being seriously injured at Edinburgh film studio
News.content:
A man has died after being seriously injured at a film studio in Edinburgh.

Emergency crews were called to FirstStage studio in Leith at about 15:00 on Thursday.

The man, who has not been named, was pronounced dead a short time later.

Police Scotland said the death was not being treated as suspicious but inquiries into the circumstances were ongoing. The Health and Safety Executive said it was "aware" of the incident.

FirstStage is the studio behind popular dramas including Netflix's Department Q and the Amazon Prime exclusive, The Rig.

BBC Scotland News understands filming of the latest series of Department Q wrapped up at the facility last month.

News.title: Mother whose newborn died after failed hospital checks was 'terrified and alone'
News.content:
A mother whose newborn baby died after hospital staff failed to wake her for checks before he was born told an inquest she felt "terrified and alone".

Eve Taylor, 29, was admitted to Ysbyty Gwynedd, Bangor, after her waters broke early at 36 weeks and was identified as having signs of potential infection.

She was due to be monitored again later that night, but a midwife decided not to wake her up. Taylor awoke hours later and was rushed for an emergency C-section.

Sonny Taylor died of a brain injury three days after being born on 3 October 2022, with a coroner saying his death was preventable.

Betsi Cadwaladwr University Health Board has apologised and admitted failings in care.

During a full inquest hearing at Caernarfon, the coroner's court heard how initial monitoring showed both mother and child were well, with antibiotics given in case of an infection.

In a statement read out in the hearing, the mother said she later woke up "feeling an intense fear".

"Instinctively, I felt that something was wrong and I needed help," she said.

Taylor told a midwife that her baby did not appear to be moving as usual.

The maternity team discovered the baby's heartbeat was very low, and an emergency C-section was carried out.

"Everything seemed rushed and out of control. I felt that the staff were frantic with little organisation," she said.

The hospital then moved the mother to the labour ward rather than directly to an operating theatre, leading to a further delay in delivering the infant.

Taylor said there was "panic" with staff arguing with each other and her son was born in "poor condition" just after 02:00 in the morning.

She was told he was very unwell with a possible brain injury.

Sonny was then transferred to the special care baby unit at Glan Clwyd Hospital, but despite intensive care, he died three days later.

News.title: Man who transported Omagh bomb was an MI5 and Garda agent, inquiry told
News.content:
The detective who led the Omagh bombing investigation has told an inquiry that he believes the man who transported the bomb was an agent for both the UK security services agency MI5 and the gardaÃ­ (Irish police).

Retired Ch Supt Norman Baxter gave evidence to the Omagh Bombing Inquiry on Friday.

He said: "As I went through the investigation it became very apparent that an individual was a Garda agent. It became apparent that in one operation there was a high potential that he was jointly handled by the security services."

Baxter said he also believed that intelligence services were aware of the bombers' activity before they carried out the Omagh bombing.

Twenty-nine people, including a woman pregnant with twins, died in the Real IRA bombing in the County Tyrone town on 15 August 1998 - the biggest single atrocity in the Troubles.

Baxter said he "formed the view that Special Branch, the security service and GCHQ (Government Communications Headquarters) knew prior to 15 August 1998 the identities of some if not all of the suspects involved in the Omagh bomb".

"The amount of information they knew I can't assess but yes, they knew."

Baxter told the hearing that there was "significant effort by the Garda to prevent their activities being uncovered".

"The Irish government and particularly the Ministry of Justice, have failed to investigate the Garda operations in the period leading up to Omagh, he added saying he was "saddened" by the "absolute failure" of the police investigation.

"It is very sad. I am very proud of my time in the police but this was a failure at leadership, a failure at government level.

"It just should not have happened."

News.title: Water firm pleads guilty after four killed in blast
News.content:
A water firm has pleaded guilty to health and safety charges after an explosion at one of its sites killed four workers, including a teenage apprentice.

Luke Wheaton, 16, Ray White, 57, Brian Vickery, 63, and Mike James, 64, died in the blast in a silo at Wessex Water's treatment site in Avonmouth, Bristol, in December 2020.

An Avon and Somerset Police investigation into manslaughter was dropped in 2024 but the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) undertook its own investigation to determine if criminal offences had been committed under health and safety laws.

At a hearing at Bristol Magistrates' Court earlier, Wessex Water pleaded guilty to three charges under the Health and Safety at Work Act.

The charges were failing, between 2013 and 2020, to ensure the health, safety and welfare of its employees, failing to ensure the health, safety and welfare of someone other than an employee and failing to comply with a health and safety notice issued in 2021.

The explosion took place in a silo containing biosolids â recycled organic matter used by farmers as agricultural fertiliser.

The four workers who died were on the roof of the silo when the explosion happened.

News.title: Here is why you should be eating more dark chocolate to improve your health
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Dark chocolate has been served as a delicacy for thousands of years with origins dating back to the ancient Mayans - and comes with some surprising health benefits.

A whole bar of dark chocolate has 200 calories and 22 grams of sugar - close to the recommended daily limits for men and women. Excess sugar in our diet converts to fat, leading to a heightened risk of chronic disease, such as cardiovascular disease.

But dark chocolate also contains beneficial properties that lead researchers to recommend the treat in moderation, including for heart, gut and brain health.

“Eating chocolate is healthy when it is dark chocolate,” Dr. Poulina Uddin, a cardiologist at Scripps Clinic, said in a statement. “Studies show that eating a small amount of dark chocolate regularly can benefit your health.”

open image in gallery Eating dark chocolate can be healthy if you pick the right kind, according to experts ( AFP via Getty Images )

Powerful plant compounds

For one, dark chocolate contains plant-based compounds that help reduce inflammation and protect cells from disease, known as polyphenols and flavonoids. These compounds help the body to produce nitric oxide, a molecule that supports healthy blood pressure by relaxing blood vessels and improving circulation, according to Northwestern Medicine.

“Nitric oxide is a very powerful stimulator of good things in the arteries and a protector against plaque,” Dr. John P. Higgins, a sports cardiologist and professor at UTHealth Houston, explained.

Better blood flow is also tied to fewer dental issues and improved memory, he said.

Flavonoids increase insulin sensitivity, which may eventually reduce the risk of diabetes, according to the Mayo Clinic.

There is even some research showing flavonoids can prevent skin damage from UV radiation, which is a precursor for skin cancer.

open image in gallery TV host and actor Mario Lopez reacts to a dark chocolate statue of himself on August 1, 2013, in Los Angeles. Dark chocolate contains antioxidants that help reduce harmful inflammation ( Getty Images for DOVE )

Truly essential minerals and hormones

Dark chocolate also contains essential minerals.

It has magnesium, which supports muscle and nerve function, controls blood sugar and pressure and helps keep our bones healthy. There’s also copper and iron, which support our energy levels and help to carry oxygen throughout the body.

Beyond minerals, it’s a good source of the happy hormone serotonin, Higgins said. High serotonin levels can reduce blood pressure and regulate gut and sleep health.

“When you’re happy, your blood pressure is lower, and you release other happy chemicals, which are also heart-healthy,” he said.

open image in gallery The key to a healthy diet is to indulge on occasion - and not to overeat ( ANP/AFP via Getty Images )

The takeaway

The most benefits from dark chocolate are seen in bars with higher percentages of cacao and the least amount of added sugar.

Aim for eating just one and three squares of dark chocolate with 70 percent or more cacao per day, Northwestern Medicine says.

“I think a key to long-term success with a healthy diet is to indulge on occasion – whether it’s a small dessert or a great piece of dark chocolate,” registered dietitian Haley Dockrey told U.C. Davis Health.

News.title: Supreme Court will consider Trump’s executive order suspending asylum access at the southern border
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Supreme Court agreed Friday to consider President Donald Trump’s ban on asylum at the southern border, a pillar of the Republican president’s far-reaching crackdown on immigration.

The Trump administration wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the executive order banning asylum applications is illegal.

Federal law gives people the right to seek asylum if they fear persecution in their home countries, no matter how they arrived in the U.S.

At the same time, it also allows the executive branch to decide whether people are granted asylum. The Trump administration argues it can categorically deny asylum to migrants covered by the order and should not have to accept applications destined to be rejected.

Federal attorneys say long yearslong processing times had previously contributed to a major influx of migrants at the southern border as many were released into the country while awaiting a decision.

But immigration attorneys at the American Civil Liberties Union and National Immigrant Justice Center counter that border crossings were already falling before Trump took office.

They say his executive order is an attempt to unilaterally “eviscerate” legal protections aimed at protecting people fleeing danger in their home countries.

The executive branch does decide whether to grant asylum, which allows people to live and work legally in the U.S. But those decisions are supposed to be made on an individual basis and the law doesn’t allow the president to unilaterally stop people from even applying, those attorneys argue.

The asylum ban was one of a series of immigration restrictions Trump rolled out upon his return to office in 2025. It has remained in place during the litigation.

News.title: Ohio restaurant reeling after hosting Vivek Ramaswamy during campaign: ‘Never dining there’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

An Ohio restaurant is picking up the pieces after hosting Republican Vivek Ramaswamy on the midterms campaign trail — a move that alienated some longtime customers.

Ramaswamy was defeated in Ohio’s gubernatorial race by Democrat Amy Acton, in part, thanks to an attack ad his campaign ran featuring his opponent’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur. Acton was sexually abused as a child by Arthur’s late husband, and the mom sided with him over her own daughter, smearing her as a “liar” in the ad.

The ad received bipartisan backlash as Republicans warned it would come back to bite Ramaswamy come Election Day.

His campaign announced a stop at P.J. Marley’s in the city of Medina on October 31, which the owners, Patty and Jon Stahl - described as small-business Republicans - claimed was arranged before the controversial ad was released, according to The New York Times.

They reportedly believed the attack ad was in bad taste, but hoped Ramaswamy would fulfill his campaign pledge to lower property taxes and tackle rising electric costs.

open image in gallery PJ Marley’s in Media, Ohio, where Republican Vivek Ramaswamy made a campaign stop in Ohio’s governor’s race (pictured) has been on the receiving end of backlash ever since ( Getty )

The couple added that they would have hosted a Democrat in their restaurant too, and the opportunity was not about taking sides.

But since announcing the visit, their staff has been subjected to aggressive phone calls calling them “pedophile supporters” and dozens of negative reviews on social media.

“Makes me sad that they are complicit of MAGA behavior,” one person wrote in a Facebook review.

“They love supporting candidates who use child s*xual abuse against the victim,” another posted.

“Never dining there, vile pedophile supporters,” a Facebook user wrote.

“PJ Marley's has great food, which makes this all the more disappointing,” someone else wrote.

The Independent has contacted the restaurant for comment.

open image in gallery County Democrats announced they were holding a protest outside the restaurant on the day of Ramaswamy’s visit, where demonstrators yelled at people going inside ( Getty )

The Stahls began deleting negative comments on their Facebook page at the height of the onslaught, they told the Times. But the couple said they don’t regret the decision to host Ramaswamy.

“People were saying, ‘Oh, you’re giving Vivek a platform,’” Jon Stahl told the newspaper. “I looked at it as he was giving us a platform.”

County Democrats announced they were holding a protest outside the restaurant on the day of Ramaswamy’s visit. A neighbor of the Stalhs, Kellie Biegel, attended the protest and reportedly yelled at people going inside, “There they are, pedophile supporters!”

One of the restaurant’s bartenders, Anthony Buchanan, told the Times that one protester kept shouting at him, “How can you work for them?”

He didn’t respond, but told the newspaper that he could have told the protester that he was a third-grade teacher working two jobs. “I’m just trying to get my money,” he said.

Acton comfortably beat Ramaswamy in the race for governor with 52.3 percent of the vote. He received 44.4 percent of the vote. The Democrat, who became the first woman elected governor in the state, reportedly let Ramaswamy’s concession call go to voicemail on Election Night.

“We left her a message,” Ramaswamy said. “It’s a tough night for us here in Ohio.”

The victory ends 16 years of Republican leadership in the state.

News.title: UN chief says 'immediate and drastic' emissions cuts needed to avert climate change catastrophe
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The world must immediately and drastically cut fossil fuel emissions to avert the most catastrophic effects of climate change, United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said Friday at his final climate summit, urging the world to “follow the science” and face hard facts.

“You cannot build peace on a burning planet," Guterres told reporters, stressing that climate change is central to the U.N.'s work because it contributes to geopolitical instability by driving hunger and displacement, pushing countries into debt and fueling competition for land and water.

“You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it,” he added. “You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends. And you cannot speak seriously about justice when those who did least to cause this crisis suffer first and worst.”

World leaders meeting in Turkey for the annual U.N. climate talks are trying to reach consensus on concrete actions to address climate change — which is fueling more intense and deadly heat waves, droughts, floods and other disasters — and help countries at greatest risk, including island nations that also are losing land to rising seas.

Electrification goals emerge as point of contention

Achieving reductions in emissions is setting up a point of contention at the climate talks, especially around electrification. A goal introduced this year would increase the share of electricity in total global energy consumption from roughly 21% to 35% by 2035, preferably from renewable energy such as solar and wind.

But it does not require that electricity be generated by renewable sources — something Guterres said is essential — meaning coal and other fossil fuels could be used, at least initially. Climate TRACE, which tracks global emissions via satellites, found that prioritizing clean energy would cut global emissions 14% compared to 7% if fossil fuels also are used for electrification.

International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said it's more important that as many countries as possible sign on to the pledge, which works best without a clean energy requirement.

But environmental groups say that electrification will only have a real impact if fossil fuels are omitted.

“Electrification must end fossil fuel dependence, not be an end in itself,” said Jasmin Duregger, from Greenpeace's Global Gas Campaign.

Vulnerable nations seek more compensation as warming takes a toll

Leaders from countries ravaged by climate change — mostly poorer, vulnerable countries that contributed little to the problem — also are calling for more money to deal with climate disasters and adapt to a warming world. Leaders of small island nations, who say climate change is a life-or-death matter for their people because rising seas are engulfing their lands, have been the most vocal at this year’s summit, COP31, saying a U.N. fund created for compensating vulnerable nations must be urgently strengthened.

Guterres said wealthier countries that have contributed most to climate change “must deliver the finance they have promised” at past summits — but also contribute much more.

“Let us be clear about the scale of the gap,” he said. “Even tripling adaptation finance would meet less than 30 percent of what is needed.”

Progress stalls, top-emitting countries skip summit

Progress is difficult without the cooperation of all nations, “particularly the biggest emitters,” Guterres said.

A report released Thursday by the independent Climate Action Tracker found that progress in slowing global warming has essentially stalled for the past five years. That means the world is sure to overshoot the goal set in the 2015 Paris Agreement of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial temperatures.

Climate change is caused primarily by greenhouse gases emitted by burning gas, oil and coal, and countries have established plans to reduce those emissions. But even if they fulfill all their promises — a big if — the globe will end the century 2.6 degrees Celsius (4.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warmer than pre-industrial times, the report said.

“Our responsibility is to keep it as small as possible, for as short a time as possible and bring temperatures back below 1.5 degrees as quickly as we can,” by cutting emissions about 6% per year for several years, Guterres said, calling the overshoot “a recipe for catastrophe.”

But some of the top-polluting countries stayed away from this year's summit, most notably the United States — the world’s second-largest polluter after China and the largest historical polluter.

It's the second year in a row the U.S. skipped the summit, after President Donald Trump withdrew the U.S. from climate negotiations.

“Facts are facts,” Guterres said. “No country can protect itself from climate change alone. We share one planet, and whether we like it or not, we share one fate.”

___

Webber reported from Fenton, Michigan; Borenstein from Kensington, Maryland; and Delgado from Bangkok.
