News.title: David Walliams investigated by police over new ‘serious’ sexual offence allegations
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation after the force received a number of allegations of “non-recent serious sexual offences” against David Walliams.

The complaints to police came after the comedian and children’s author was unmasked as the celebrity who failed to gag reports accusing him of grooming teenage girls as young as 15.

Multiple women accused the Little Britain star of sexual misconduct in an investigation published by The Guardian and ITV News on Tuesday, alleging he used his fame to prey on them for sexual purposes.

Mr Walliams, 55, denies any wrongdoing and his lawyers took a case to the High Court to try to stop the accusations being published.

Several allegations have been made to police in the aftermath of the reporting but they are separate to those uncovered by the news outlets, the Met confirmed.

open image in gallery Walliams tried to get an injunction to prevent allegations of sexual misconduct being reported ( Getty )

A statement from the force said: “In recent days, the Met has received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his fifties.

“Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers.

“The allegations are separate from those reported by ITN and The Guardian. However, as part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences.”

The Met is yet to confirm how many alleged offences have been reported, what the accusations are and when or where the incidents are alleged to have taken place.

Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney, the head of the team leading the investigation, said: “We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.

“We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process.”

open image in gallery The author denied any wrongdoing in statements to ITV News and The Guardian ( AFP/Getty )

One woman, named by ITV News and The Guardian as Jade, claimed she was 15 when Mr Walliams contacted her out of the blue on MySpace in 2007. The comic, then 36, later invited her to his £3.2m London townhouse where he sexually assaulted her, she alleged.

She claimed what happened to her there was “sexual assault” and “grooming”, adding: “It’s completely wrong in every way.”

Mr Walliams strongly denied to the publications that he had any sexual contact with Jade, adding that he rejects any allegations of criminal activity and he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

Another woman, named by the news organisations as Alex, alleged she was 15 and studying for her GCSEs when Mr Walliams telephoned her in 2004 after she had shared some of her scripts with him at a fan event a few days earlier. They stayed in contact and she started having sex with Mr Walliams when she was 17, she claimed.

Asked how she feels about him now, she said: “I think I was groomed. 100 per cent.”

Mr Walliams told the publications he believed she was 18 at the time they had sex. His lawyers say the suggestion he groomed Alex is false and has caused him significant distress.

In an emphatic denial, Mr Walliams told the publications he is “devastated” that allegations have been brought against him. He added: “I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.”

open image in gallery Walliams was dropped by his publisher HarperCollins last year ( Reuters )

Mr Walliams had brought legal action against the news outlets’ publishers, Independent Television News (ITN) and Guardian News and Media (GNM), but failed to get an injunction to stop the reporting because of the risk he would take his own life, after two previous suicide attempts.

Judge Mr Justice Nicklin refused the bid for an injunction, ruling it would be an “exceptionally serious interference” with freedom of expression.

After the allegations were published, the former Britain’s Got Talent judge was dropped by his literary agency, Independent Talent Group, and the BBC began removing his shows, including Little Britain, from iPlayer. His Labour Party membership was also suspended.

His publisher HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025 after an investigation into allegations that he had “harassed” young women, which Mr Walliams denied. The Alton Towers attraction inspired by his bestselling children’s books was permanently closed earlier this month.

Mr Walliams did not respond to The Independent’s request for comment following the publication of his name on Tuesday. We have attempted to contact him again.

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.

News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

News.title: Bird flu viruses ‘gaining function’ through natural mixing, warn scientists
News.content:
The bird flu virus’ resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead.

Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn’t reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over. Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent.

Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again. The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed?

Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues.

Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as “reassortment”.

News.title: The country where diabetes is more feared than HIV
News.content:
Furthermore, even when antiretrovirals suppress the virus, the immune system can stay chronically activated, causing a low-grade inflammation that damages organs and blood vessels. The Lancet HIV Commission reported that, by one measure of biological ageing, people with HIV appeared about five years older on average than peers without the virus.

HIV also makes other infections more dangerous. For example, those living with the virus are more likely to contract human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer, and they are less able to clear HPV from their bodies.

“With HIV, you don’t channel your mind into dying,” Ms Shongwe said. “But when I got to know that I have cervical cancer, I thought it was the end of the world.”

In 2018, Ms Ginindza moved from the Ministry of Health’s HIV programme to its NCD programme, but almost immediately, she asked to go back to her old job. “There is nothing here,” she recalled, “no tools, no data collection system, no guidelines”.

Even today, the ministry doesn’t have any dedicated NCD posts. While there are hundreds of people working on HIV, there are just 10 NCD staff, all borrowed from other programmes, Ms Ginindza said.

Although latest figures show that NCDs account for almost half of Eswatini’s deaths the government’s programme for NCDs, injuries and mental health received about one million emalangeni - roughly £45,000 - or 0.03 per cent of the health budget.

Foreign aid hasn’t filled the gap: international partners cover about five per cent of NCD spending, Ms Ginindza said, compared with 60 per cent of the HIV response. Donors “cannot give you money when they also need that money to address their own NCDs”, she added.

So, when it comes to these chronic diseases, patients struggle to get diagnosed, obtain their medicines or see a specialist for complications. In a 2024 government survey, fewer than 30 per cent of people with high blood pressure were on medication, and only 14 per cent had their hypertension under control.

The government’s own NCD report puts the stock-out rate for key medicines at 79 per cent, and the public system has no nephrologists, endocrinologists or cardiologists, Ms Ginindza said, relying instead on private specialists and Taiwanese medical missions to provide these services.

Faced with one of the worst HIV epidemics, Eswatini poured almost everything into fighting it. “The focus was HIV,” Ms Ginindza said, “so we forgot about the other conditions.”

Fighting on two fronts



Now, Eswatini is trying to turn its HIV machinery towards chronic diseases.

Since 2020, a government-led scheme has delivered NCD medication refills, blood pressure checks and glucose tests in hundreds of community settings, integrating this with existing HIV services. As it once did with antiretrovirals, the ministry is also shifting NCD care from hospitals to local clinics, Ms Ginindza said, aiming to train at least two nurses at each.

For Mr Mamba, that means he sees the same clinician for his HIV, diabetes and blood pressure. It saves time, he said, since he can get everything under one roof.

The challenge is not just extending HIV services to NCD patients but finding the money to sustain both. The Eswatini government aims to increase NCD funding to 20 million emalangeni, or £900,000, by 2028.

But last year, the Trump administration gutted the US President’s Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar), the backbone of Eswatini’s HIV response.

In December, Eswatini signed a five-year deal with the US to restore some HIV funding - on the condition that the government shoulders more of the cost itself. So, as the country scrambles to protect its HIV gains, NCDs risk remaining a secondary priority.

With his diabetes and blood pressure medicines so often out of stock, Mr Mamba has come to dread his check-ups, convinced each one will show his numbers have climbed again - and that his luck is running out.

Many of his neighbours have the same conditions and probably share these fears, he said, but much as people once kept quiet about HIV, they rarely discuss such things.

Over 30 years ago, Ms Gwebu contemplated suicide after being diagnosed with HIV. But today, she hopes Eswatini can sustain its hard-won progress against the virus without leaving those with other diseases behind. “What is going to kill our people,” she said, “is not going to be HIV.”

News.title: Ebola could be raging in DRC for another year, expert warns
News.content:
The Ebola epidemic currently raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo could last at least another year, a leading UK epidemiologist has warned.

Experts have struggled to contain the current outbreak since the first cases of the rare Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May.

There have so far been almost 11,000 cases including 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history, after the devastating West Africa epidemic of 2014-16. Cases have also been reported in Nigeria and Kenya, although transmission has not been widespread.

The outbreak is taking place across a vast area of DRC - North Kivu and Ituri - where conflict and widespread mistrust of authorities, including health workers, have hampered the response.

Neil Ferguson, professor of epidemiology at Imperial College, London, told a press briefing that at the current rate of disease spread that the epidemic could still be ongoing at the end of next year.

“Controlling Ebola outbreaks takes a long time so it is highly likely we’ll still be seeing transmission in a year’s time,” he said.

“We’re ticking over at about 70 confirmed cases a day at the moment and that’s almost certainly quite a significant underestimate of the true number of infections,” said Prof Ferguson, who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Covid pandemic when he advised government on the likely trajectory of the outbreak.

SCOTT PARKER is the right man to spearhead West Ham to promotion despite making a woeful start in the hotseat, according to former England team-mate Darren Bent.

The Hammers handed their iconic midfielder the managerial reins after their push for a return to the Premier League faltered.



But Parker, 46, is still searching for his first win in charge and saw fans vent their fury following a 2-1 loss to Blackburn last week.

The setback, which came after a thrilling 3-3 draw with Cardiff, resulted in the Hammers heading into the international break outside the Championship play-off places.



Bent still reckons Parker is set to spark an upturn in form as West Ham aim to bounce back from last season’s relegation.

Bent, 42, told SunSport: “He deserves the West Ham job with his track record of getting teams promoted from the Championship.

“He has got three promotions already, which is incredible, so he’s definitely the right man for the job.

“I know the start has been a bit more rocky than he would have thought, but I’ve got no doubt that he’ll get it right.

“If West Ham have got any aspirations of getting themselves out of the Championship, they’ve definitely got one of the best men out there because he’s done it so often before.”

FRANCE supremo Zinedine Zidane leapt to Malo Gusto’s defence after he suffered a Nations League nightmare.

The Chelsea right-back, 23, came in for fierce criticism as Les Bleus were consigned to a 3-1 defeat by Italy on Thursday.



Gusto, who was valued at £75million when Manchester City showed interest in the summer, gave away a second half spot-kick.

The former Lyon youngster brought down Nicolo Cambiaghi with a reckless lunge and the penalty was converted by Pio Esposito.



But Zidane refused to pin the blame on Gusto after suffering his first defeat since being appointed as France’s boss in July.

The three-time Champions League-winning boss, 54, said: “He was called up, he played his part, he conceded the penalty, these things happen.

“I don’t think we can say that he had a bad game. There you have it, now I’m doing the analysis as a whole anyway. I’m not talking about individuals.”

Gusto, who has only made three Premier League starts for Chelsea this season, was hauled off by Zidane seconds after gifting Italy a two-goal advantage.

And the Azzurri completed a stunning fightback after a blunder from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowed France to bag an early lead.

Manchester City fans slammed their first-choice keeper when he sensationally passed the ball straight to Michael Olise, who grabbed the opener.

But Italy came out on top in the Nations League showdown thanks to a brace from Esposito – whose brother Sebastiano missed a penalty – and a clinical finish from Davide Frattesi.

Zidane, who has seen Dayot Upamecano pull out of the squad for personal reasons ahead of a clash with Turkey on Sunday, still reckons there were positives to take after throwing away an early lead at the San Siro.

The Real Madrid legend added: “There were some good things, especially in the first half, where we should have focused on what we did well. After that, we did some less good things.

“We lost the match, so naturally there were some more complicated situations.

“Particularly in duels and one-on-one situations, we weren’t quite as good. It’s all part of the learning process.



“When we were in difficulty, we didn’t know how to react and stay within the game plan we had put in place.

“We did it in the first half, but when they took the lead, we became a little scattered, especially defensively.

“It wasn’t a bad game. There’s room for improvement. I told the players we shouldn’t panic.

“We became more fragile as the match went on. What I told them is that it was a defeat, but not entirely deserved.

“We did some good things and some not-so-good things. We’ll analyse it when we’re in Bordeaux to prepare for our match. We just need to rest and focus on the game we have left.”

Sports.title: How Spurs icon Dele Alli amassed £8.3million from image rights company, including amazing deals and property portfolio
Sports.content:
Next

DELE ALLI is closing his image rights company with £8.3million in the bank.

The former England ace, 30, will pocket £7.6million of that staggering amount after paying £685,362 corporation tax bill.



Details of the closure of Dele Alli Promotions were in a Declaration of Solvency as he put the business into liquidation.

But how did Alli amass his £8.3million fortune from his image rights company?



SunSport crunches the numbers, from how he caught a tax break to Alli’s impressive sponsorship deals during his peak years.

Making plans for his future

Modern footballers know that they have a limited shelf life.



For Alli, his career has stalled in recent years. His most recent spell came at Como in 2025, although he is still working hard on his fitness and hopeful of a return to football in the near future.

But, he smartly invested money earned during his peak years at Tottenham and with England, which should make him financially sound for the rest of his life.

Clever Alli funnelled sponsorship fees and commercial bonuses into his company rather than taking them as standard salary, building an £8.3million asset pile.

Then, came the tax play. By keeping his earnings inside a limited company, Alli avoided paying a 45 per cent personal income tax rate.



That meant he owed just £685,362 in corporation tax.

Alli has also gone down the bricks and mortar route, slowly building a property portfolio.

He has two other companies — Future Homes Investments, which owns six rental properties worth more than £1.5million, and Dele Investments, which is worth £336,267.



His commercial peak

Between 2016 to 2019, Alli was arguably the most marketable young footballer in the UK.

For Spurs, he led the club to a title challenge and the Champions League final.

With England, he was an integral part of a team that reached the World Cup semi-final in Russia in 2018.

That success made him a poster boy for aspiring kids around the country who dreamed of becoming footballers.

On a personal level, he won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in consecutive seasons.



Major brands wanted to buy a piece of the “Dele” brand.

Adidas reportedly signed him up on a five-year boot deal worth around £8million.



He designed a line with menswear brand boohooMAN and became one of their ambassadors.

Alli also secured a global fragrance campaign with Paco Rabanne.

Being repped by CAA Sports placed the midfielder in the same commercial stable as Cristiano Ronaldo.

During his brief window at the top, Alli was able to bottle lightning and set himself up for life.



What’s next for Alli?

When a sports star shuts down an image rights company, traditionally it signals the end of their commercial life.

But that doesn’t mean that Ali isn’t relevant anymore. Far from it.

This could be a pivot move for him at this stage in his life, moving from traditional corporate endorsements to becoming a very bankable digital creator.



Rather than fading away after leaving Como, Alli has leaned into gaming and live-streaming – catching the eye of the Gen-Z audience.

Early partnerships with EXCEL ESPORTS and Secretlab laid the groundwork for his post-football digital identity.

He’s now a regular live-streamer on his recently launched Twitch channel, and has already created some viral moments.

Most recently, he recorded content with influencer iShowSpeed playing EAFC 27.

After losing two games against the YouTuber, Alli was forced into a forfeit – having to wear the shirt of Tottenham’s fiercest rivals, Arsenal and posting the image on social media.



He captioned the Instagram Story: “Sorry Spurs fans, but a bet is a bet.”

Later, Alli appeared on his Twitch livestream wearing white overalls and attempting to set fire to the top.

This was followed with another Instagram Story of the Arsenal shirt appearing ripped up next to a fire extinguisher.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



Alli posted: “Speed, a bet is a bet! But this is what you call the aftermath.”

Whatever the future holds for Alli, he will still have a substantial nest egg to fall back on.

Sports.title: Johan Cruyff’s grandson called up for completely different country after making own way in football
Sports.content:
Next

JOHAN CRUYFF’S footballing legacy will continue after his grandson earned an international call-up – but not with Holland.

Shae Cruyff-Beane will link up with the United States Under-18s for their matches against Norway and Portugal at their training camp in Santarem.



The 18-year-old has pledged his allegiance to the Stars and Stripes for now, but could be the subject of an international tug of war, with the midfielder also eligible to play for Spain and the Netherlands.

Cruyff-Beane was born in Spain, and qualifies for the Netherlands via his maternal family background.



He is the youngest son of Chantal Cruyff, while his grandfather is widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of all time.

Cruyff’s impact on the sport is unquestionable, after captaining the Netherlands to the 1974 World Cup final and winning three consecutive European Cups with Ajax between 1971 and 1973.

He also won the Ballon d’Or three times – twice as an Ajax player in 1971 and 1973, and once during his spell with Barcelona in 1974.

The Dutchman would go on to win a La Liga title and the Spanish Cup during his spell as a player in Spain, but his impact as a head coach at the Camp Nou was arguably even greater.

Cruyff led the Catalans to four successive domestic titles between 1991 and 1994, and managed the Barca side which won their first European Cup in 1992.

His possession-based style style of play had a lasting influence on Barcelona’s philopsophy, and the tactics of modern-day great Pep Guardiola.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Cruyff-Beane’s uncle, Jordi, also had a distinguished career, despite not reaching the heights of his father.

He won a Spanish Super Cup with Barcelona, but his main haul of silverware came at Manchester United.

The midfielder won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup and the Uefa Champions League at Old Trafford, before returning to Spain in spells for Alaves and Espanyol.

He now plies his trade at Ajax, having served as their technical director since February.

Cruyff-Beane’s father, Todd Beane, also played football in the NCAA first division for Dartmouth College.

Sports.title: USA drop major hint over ambitious Pep Guardiola approach after Mauricio Pochettino’s tearful exit for Man Utd
Sports.content:
Next

USA chiefs have revealed money will not be an issue when it comes to appointing Mauricio Pochettino’s successor.

The Argentine, 54, is preparing to leave his role following a Concacaf Nations League double-header against Haiti after being confirmed as Manchester United’s new boss.



USA have been linked with preparing an ambitious approach to make Pep Guardiola their next boss.

And it now appears meeting the former Manchester City chief’s hefty demands will not be a stumbling block.



United have agreed to trigger Pochettino’s huge release clause after sacking Michael Carrick.

US Soccer chief executive JT Batson has confirmed the federation will be pocketing the compensation fee instead of billionaires who contributed to paying their outgoing supremo’s salary.

Scott Goodwin, who co-founded £30billion asset management firm Diameter, and Citadel chief executive Kenneth C. Griffin helped to fund the USA’s appointment of Pochettino.

They put cash towards the contracts handed to the former Tottenham boss and his coaching staff.

But Batson said: “The agreement with United, those funds, US Soccer is a non-profit.

“Those funds will be used to help hire coaches, run coaching sessions and referee courses. Those funds are available for us to invest in our goals.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Our supporters, sponsors and donors are very supportive around making sure we have the resources to achieve our goals, including having a world-class coach. Our ambition is high.”

It is a major hint that Guardiola, 55, will not be out of their reach as they aim to bring in a big-name Pochettino replacement.

The Spaniard has allegedly been discussed internally across multiple levels in the early stages of the USA hiring process.

And Guardiola has been out of work since ending his trophy-laden stint in the Man City hotseat at the end of last season.



Roberto Martinez has been mooted as another possible candidate to head into the USA dugout.

The former Everton boss, 53, quit the Portugal job after their World Cup hopes were ended by eventual winners Spain during the summer.

Martinez had already earned his stripes in international management with Belgium.

Pochettino broke down in tears during his farewell press conference after being handed the United reins.

Sports.title: Footballers with strange hobbies, like Cristiano Ronaldo’s love of bingo, after Alisson Becker shows passion for fishing
Sports.content:
Next

AS the international break kicks in, some footballers will be enjoying their time off.

Many will be enjoying sinking themselves into a new hobby.



Liverpool shotstopper Alisson Becker is the latest pro to show a love for fishing in his downtime.

The Brazil keeper took to Instagram to share a snap of his latest catch, as well as a picture by a scenic lake.



That’s prompted SunSport to uncover the most unusual hobbies we’ve seen footballers enjoy, starting with something usually reserved for seniors around the country.

Cristiano Ronaldo – Bingo

In between sculpting his physique in the gym, Ronaldo’s developed a love of bingo.

Imagine him rocking up at the Mecca in Sale?

Ronaldo said in 2008: “Playing bingo can be very exciting.

“It can be very exciting because you can be there waiting for a long time for just the one number to make the game complete.



“Then you see one of your friends you are playing against get his lucky number before you.”

Paul Pogba – Camel racing

The France World Cup winner took his obsession with camel racing to another level.

In 2025, Pogba invested in Saudi Arabia-based team Al Haboob.



“I’ve watched my fair share of [camel] races on YouTube and spent time doing research in my spare time trying to understand the techniques and strategies,” Pogba told the BBC.

“And what stood out to me is how much dedication it takes from everyone involved. At the end of the day, sport is sport. It demands heart, sacrifice and teamwork.”

Eberechi Eze – Chess

The Arsenal No10 is used to facing the tightest defences to break down at the Emirates.

So, it’s no surprise he knows a thing or two about strategy, which has led him to playing chess.



The week before he downed Man City in the 2025 FA Cup final, he won £15,000 at a four-day chess tournament and is ranked in the top 15 per cent of players on Chess.com.

He has even lined up his pawns to face off against Sir Richard Branson.

Axel Tuanzebe – Hungry Hippos

When your hobby is a kids’ game and you hold a world record in it, does that mean you’ve taken it too far?

Not if you’re former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe, who is a Hungry Hippos whizz.



“We have had a great day adjudicating a range of record attempts with the Manchester United football team as part of their collaboration with Guinness World Records,” said adjudicator Adam Brown.

“Axel Tuanzebe, was the bigger winner of the day and bagged himself the record for fastest time to clear a game of Hungry Hippos in a time of 17.36 seconds, beating competition from his fellow team-mates.”

Beat that, kids.



Xavi – Mushroom hunting

The Spain legend has an eye for a pass and a mushroom, unbelievably. But not THEM ones, before you get too clever.

Xavi is a mycology nut, which means he regularly hunts for mushrooms.

Former team-mate Gerard Pique and his ex-wife Shakira used to reportedly joined Xavi on a trek for some rare shrooms.



“Someone who picks mushrooms can’t be a bad bloke,” his former boss Pep Guardiola once said.

Phil Foden – Fishing

From Xavi, we go to the ‘Stockport Iniesta’ – better known as Phil Foden.

To take himself away from the stresses of Premier League football, the playmaker props himself up next to a lake and dangles out his rod – just like his Premier League rival Alisson.

Foden has even trekked to Spain, where he once caught a 130lb catfish.



“I was probably about six or seven and my dad had a fishing rod of his dad’s and said we should go and try it out,” he recalled.

“I fell in love with it and we ended up going every weekend. I still remember my first catch.”

Aaron Ramsdale – Dog training

Former Gunners star Ramsdale enjoys spending his downtime training dogs.

In the past, the goalie said he finds it relaxing to connect with pets and it’s how he finds peace away from the pitch.



He is the proud doggy dad to Chow Chow, Patrick. We don’t know if it was named after Vieira.

Sadly, Ramsdale ‘slove of dogs wasn’t enough to keep him at Arsenal, if Mikel Arteta’s pooch Win is to be trusted.

Matt Oakley – Piranha collecting

We’ll keep this one snappy.



Former Leicester City star Oakley’s strange and frankly dangerous hobby involved collecting South American red-bellied piranha.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I wanted something unusual,” he said. “They certainly make feeding time interesting.”

You don’t say.

Sports.title: Dream Team managers overlooking Yeremy Pino, Luka Vuskovic and others — 3 underrated players from each position
Sports.content:
Next

THE very best Dream Team managers are using this international break to broaden their knowledge of the season so far.

In hope of providing a helping hand, we have identified three underrated players from each position worthy of wider attention.

GOALKEEPERS

We start with perhaps the most obviously underappreciated performer of the lot, Bart Verbruggen (£4.8m).



Brighton’s No1 is the outright leader in terms of clean sheets with 10 and has matched David Raya (£5.2m) all the way this season — the pair are currently level on 88 points as the joint-best keepers.



However, while Arsenal’s custodian is by far and away the most popular asset in his position with a massive ownership of 31.3%, Verbruggen features in just 4.5% of teams.

The Dutchman is less popular than Manchester United’s Senne Lammens (£3.6m), who has mustered a measly 38 points in comparison.

Zion Suzuki (£4.1m) ranks fifth among keepers having earned 61 points since he replaced Emi Martinez (£4.1m) at Aston Villa.



The 3.9%-owned Japan international will want more protection as the campaign develops but the Villains’ porous defence has actually helped him accumulate points.

He’s made 52 saves in total, 10 more than anyone else.

Alisson’s (£4.4m) tally of 51 points is underwhelming but there’s every chance he climbs the rankings in the run-up to Christmas.

Liverpool are due to fulfil eight fixtures across the next four Gameweeks and while it’s possible Giorgi Mamardashvili (£3m) will be called upon once or twice, the Brazilian will take the bulk of the load.



Alisson reminded everyone of his pedigree with an excellent performance at Selhurst Park in Gameweek 10.

He appears in 2.7% of teams at the time of writing.

DEFENDERS

There’s been so much focus on Maxim De Cuyper (£4.1m) that many gaffers have failed to note Luka Vuskovic’s (£4m) efforts for high-flying Brighton.

The teenage centre-back is mature beyond his years and has chipped in with three goal involvements on top of seven clean sheets.



A total of 85 points puts him fourth among defenders, one place above Ezri Konsa (£4.5m), who is more than twice as popular as Vuskovic (7% ownership).

We feel compelled to mention another of Fabian Hurzeler’s troops here as Olivier Boscagli (£3.6m) is within touching distance of Vuskovic and Konsa on 80 points and yet just 2.2% of gaffers have the Frenchman in their back line.

He has contributed to nine clean sheets this season, the joint-most among defenders alongside Gabriel (£5.7m).

The Seagulls are due to face Hull (a) and Universitatea Craiova (h) in Gameweek 11.

James Hill (£3.7m) surely deserves a greater ownership than 2.7% given Bournemouth have won eight games in a row, including six clean sheets.



Thomas Tuchel has evidently been impressed as the German tactician has included the 24-year-old in his latest England squad.

Hill has 73 points at this stage and will be hopeful of more success when the campaign resumes as the Cherries have some favourable fixtures in their near future.

MIDFIELDERS

The top six midfielders in Dream Team right now all feature in over 19% of teams but the man at number seven, Matheus Cunha (£4.9m), has an ownership of just 5.4%.

Dream Team bosses may be reluctant to go shopping at Old Trafford while the Red Devils are in the relegation zone but the numbers don’t lie, their No10 is the most in-form player in his position.



Despite some farcical efforts from his team-mates, the Brazil international has taken 33 points from his last three outings via two goals and two assists.

Similarly, Yeremy Pino (£4.1m) can hold his head high while surrounded by incompetence.

Aided by Europa League commitments, the Crystal Palace playmaker has registered seven goal involvements and ranks joint-fourth among all players for big chances created.

The World Cup winner is doing his best to drag the Eagles out of the mire, as evidenced by his impressive tally of 88 points — he features in 1.5% of teams.

Dream Team managers are spoiled for choice in midfield and so it’s understandable why only 5.1% are backing Elliot Anderson (£5.1m) at this moment time.



That being said, Manchester City’s big-money acquisition is a reliable performer who ticks over nicely and offers peace of mind.

He leads the way for both bonus points (22) and tackles (36) in his position.

Anderson’s all-action style has yielded 82 points at an average of 5.9 per game, plus he’s more immune to rotation than most other City midfielders.

STRIKERS

With an ownership of 11.6%, Thierno Barry (£3.6m) is the most popular player on this list but it’s remarkable that 88.4% of gaffers are ignoring the second-best performer this season.



Erling Haaland (£9m), the most selected asset of all, is the only man keeping Everton’s charismatic forward off the throne.

Barry has amassed 120 points via 10 goals without European fixtures to pad out his schedule.

He’s missed a fair few big chances too!

Managers brave to pick Barry have been handsomely rewarded across the first quarter of the season — extra kudos to the tiny minority who owned him from Gameweek 1.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Truth be told, it would be disingenuous of us to recommend any other strikers as viable differentials at this juncture because it’s difficult to look past popular options such as Evanilson (£4.6m), Nicolas Jackson (£4.3m) and Alexander Isak (£6.5m) when trying to remain competitive.



However, 0.7%-owned Georginio Rutter (£3.8m) and 0.9%-owned Jorgen Strand Larsen (£3.1m) are worthy of mentions as the seventh and ninth ranked performers in their position respectively.

MAURICIO POCHETTINO will replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach.

Carrick was sacked on November 12, with the club in the relegation zone after their woeful start to the season.



United are 18th in the Premier League table, their lowest position ten games into a top-flight campaign since 1986/87.

Old Trafford chiefs quickly decided that USMNT boss Pochettino is the man they want to replace Carrick.



Other names such as Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann were also under consideration, but the club opted for the former Tottenham manager.

USMNT have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, with the games on Saturday and Tuesday coming.

When will Mauricio Pochettino take charge of Man Utd?

Pochettino will take charge of both legs of the USA‘s Concacaf Nations League quarter-final.

The first leg at Sabina Park in Kingston, Jamaica, is on Saturday, before the return leg in Cincinnati three days later.



Pochettino will arrive in Manchester to take his first training session on November 18.

This will give the former Tottenham boss and his staff a matter of days to assess the squad before taking charge of his first game at rivals Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

Sports.title: Tearful Pochettino admits he 'couldn't say no to Man Utd'
Sports.content:
An emotional Mauricio Pochettino said that leaving his role with the United States was the "toughest decision of his career" but admitted he couldn't turn down the chance to become head coach of Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as Michael Carrick's replacement at Old Trafford having signed a deal until the summer of 2029. It comes mere months after extending his stay with the USMNT until the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentine will begin his new role on November 18, after taking charge of the USA's two fixtures against Haiti.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference before his penultimate game, Pochettino broke down in tears as he explained his decision.

"In some part, this is a very sad decision. In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true," the former Spurs and Chelsea boss said.

"It all happened so quickly. By Sunday afternoon there was contact. You always were transparent and always tried to build something together. We learned a lot from you all, this amazing country and you amazing people. This is one of the most difficult decisions of my career. Thank you so much."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett explains why Pochettino could be set for a busy January transfer window

Pochettino last held a club role in Europe during his one-season stint at Chelsea, which came to an end in 2024. When asked why he had opted to leave his post to return to the Premier League, Pochettino didn't hide the fact that taking the Old Trafford hot seat was a once in a lifetime opportunity.

"It's obvious," Pochettino added. "They [US Soccer Federation] know that not many opportunities can happen in your career like a side the size of Manchester United.

"When that arrives, it's difficult to turn down."

Liverpool

Manchester United Sunday 22nd November 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Pochettino explains why he is staying for two more games

Pochettino will start life at Carrington following the international break, and will have three training sessions with the players before the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

The new head coach admitted that he would have started sooner if asked to, but explained why he wanted to see out the remainder of this camp.

"I am a professional person and the emotional link between us we have built in this two years is to show the commitment and respect and care and love," Pochettino said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports's Rob Dorsett explains why Pochettino has a VERY busy few days ahead of him

"Even if we take a decision which is not the best for one part, we've always been open. We have the respect of the players and staff, they understand the situation.

"Of course, if Manchester United and the federation agreed different terms, I would have respected between both. But this happened and of course, all the games are important.

"The last four games were important. We gave debuts to 13 players, before the cup I thought everyone had different ideas about it but we believe in the programme and are brave enough to go ahead. We're always optimistic and positive.

"After this camp, with four victories, we've been consistent in the same way, win or lose. We believe in the programme. It's an honour for us to be here, defend our patch and our players.

"We need to play tomorrow and the next game. We're not thinking in the future, it's about performing. We're very optimistic and it's a natural way to finish our partnership."

Emotional Poch rediscovered motivation in USA

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"We've always known Mauricio Pochettino is an emotional person. He wears his heart on his sleeve. But I don't think you would normally expect a manager to break down and be so emotional in a press conference when he was leaving the USA to manage Manchester United.

"But that just tells you about the kind of guy he is because he's all about personal relationships. And obviously, he's made some very good friends in the US.

"He also said: 'We recovered our motivation here'. He was quite hurt and bruised by what happened to him at PSG and at Chelsea. It's almost like he's rediscovered his motivation by working in the US. And now he's ready to come back to the Premier League."

Carrick’s unintentional advice to Pochettino

In the wake of the announcement of Pochettino as the new head coach at Old Trafford, his predecessor Michael Carrick penned an emotional farewell off the back of his sacking on Wednesday.

Carrick took to social media to thank supporters saying, “you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way".

In his post, the former Red Devils midfielder also lent an inadvertent word of advice for his replacement, giving an insight into what life is like at the club.

Sports.title: Riley determined to prove himself a world champion in waiting
Sports.content:
Viddal Riley will put himself on a path to a cruiserweight world title shot, if he can defend the European championship against Seydi Coupe on Saturday.

Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship.

The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe.

"I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports.

"I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at Viddal Riley's best knockouts.

The IBF belt is currently vacant with Riley and New Zealand's David Nyika ranked one and two. Sooner or later a world title fight would surely lie ahead of Riley, if he's victorious.

"He's in the way. We can't worry about the other side of the door until we get past the doorman," Riley said of Coupe.

"I'm trying to get in the club, Seydi's asking for my ID at the door, I have to show him my ID or pull him out the way and get into the club."

It's a fight Riley is determined to dominate.

"I believe this will be a stoppage victory," the Londoner said. "You can't stop everybody, I'm aware of that as well. I won't be disappointed per se if I don't stop him. I'll be disappointed if I don't batter him.

"I just want to show for 12 rounds at least, it's not the level. We're completely different levels and I do, contrary to belief, possess good punch power."

Sports.title: Jonbon records Shloer Chase hat-trick at Cheltenham
Sports.content:
Harry Cobden made his first ride on Jonbon in public a successful one as the odds-on favourite landed a third Shloer Chase in gritty fashion at Cheltenham.

Never out of the first two in 29 races, Nicky Henderson's charge is approaching veteran status at the age of 10 and was winning for the 21st time in his stellar career.

His task was made easier with the late withdrawal of Gidleigh Park, but Mighty Bandit kept him honest after the last, with the 1-2 favourite pulling away again towards to line to win by two and a quarter lengths.

Cobden said: "I'm so fortunate to be in this position riding all of these great horses and there's so many in the camp to look forward to, you do have to pinch yourself a little bit.

"I was really looking forward to it and pressure is just something you put on yourself isn't it. There was no point having a sleepless night over a Shloer Chase though as what would I be like in March!"

He went on: "I really enjoyed that. He pinged from fence to fence and loved that ground, he did well.

"I didn't want to ask him too many questions too early today as ultimately he is a 10-year-old now, but he's been round everywhere and doesn't need me telling him what to do.

"It was a lovely starting point for me to ride him in. If it was a Champion Chase with 10 others around going championship pace then it wouldn't be as easy, but it was pretty uncomplicated and straightforward there. I just let him enjoy himself."

The man who made the call to employ Cobden was owner JP McManus who has never made any secret of the esteem he holds the veteran in.

McManus said: "Nicky had him looking great and he was up for it today, he gave a little blow but hardly put a foot wrong and got the job done.

"This horse has stood the test of time and he's been going from four to now rising 11 and to run as many times as he has and still be performing, it's fair play to Nicky as he knows this horse to a tee."

He added: "I don't have to worry about Harry, he knows every horse. He was good on him there."

Henderson was equally as delighted as the new green and gold pilot, stating the intention to follow the tried and tested route to Sandown's Tingle Creek on December 5.

"Some say this isn't his favourite place but that's his third win in this race and it's lovely to see him back," said the Seven Barrows handler.

"He is exactly where we want him to be and we have three weeks until the Tingle Creek and that will be the plan.

"I'm always so proud he has never been out of the first two which is going to be a hard record to maintain, but we've kept it intact today and it's a remarkable record.

"I thought he was more forward this year than last year and this was the perfect race for him. He's had a lovely time and Harry looks like he enjoyed it. There was never any anxiety and I think he always had enough in his pocket.

"He'll never run away from them at his age over two miles and we know we can go further. But for now we'll stick to two miles and then review. I could see him doing two and a half at some stage and maybe after the Clarence House like last year, but we'll see."

D Art D Art delivers for rising star Daniel King

Rising weighing-room star Daniel King timed his run to perfection aboard the Tom Cooper-trained D Art D Art in the Mucking Brilliant Paddy Power Novices Chase.

The winning jockey, who landed a famous double at the Galway Festival in the Plate and Hurdle for Willie Mullins and Tony Martin respectively in the summer, delivered aboard the 7-2 shot.

Given time to close on the leaders from a patient position in the five-runner field, King closed on the leaders at the turn into the straight and stayed on well to deny the strong-finishing Intosomethinggood at 100-30 by a neck.

Image: D Art D Art struck gold at Cheltenham

Cooper said: "This is very emotional and if you saw this horse on August 13, 2025 he got an awful bad doing. He bled profusely internally and they did a wonderful job at the vets.

"It was terrible, he was gone, dead. But they brought him back to life and it was amazing. He crashed into a wall and got loose in the box and out of his stable overnight and what he did to himself was horrific.

"We gave him a couple of runs to get over the accident and he's taken well to the fences. He can come back here in March, what for I don't know what, but he's obviously going absolutely the right way.

"He's a different horse this year and he's been a little hot before, but he's so chilled out now and changed his tune completely, he's loving life."

He added: "I was always confident as he jumps for fun and this rider is absolutely top drawer - you're going to hear a lot about this kid!

"He doesn't know how to lose this horse and he will stick his head out, grind and wants to win."

Sports.title: July Flower fancied for Handicap gold at Cheltenham
Sports.content:
Ahead of the start of Cheltenham's November meeting, the Weekend Winners panel offered their top tips for a potentially informative Saturday at Prestbury Park.

The panel of Kate Tracey, Declan Rix and Sam Boswell paid particular attention to the feature Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase, which sees Meetmebythesea head the market for Ben Pauling.

Blueking d'Oroux will be looking to rediscover the winning thread having finished second the last twice, whilst Cheltenham Festival hero Madara also represents the formidable Skelton operation. Quebecois and July Flower could also have a say, alongside the likes of Norn Iron, O'Moore Park and Zurich.

Declan Rix...

"A mare won this last year, and I am hoping the girls can do the same here with July Flower. I feel like we haven't seen the best of her yet but she won at this meeting last year when winning the Arkle Trial. She's a lovely, big mare and maybe we could see the best of her this season.

Image: July Flower goes for glory at Cheltenham on Saturday

"When she won at Cheltenham last year, she beat the Dan Skelton-trained horse Be Aware, who franked the form in Grade One Company with Lulamba. The De Bromhead team have targeted this from early in the season and despite her trainer being in Bahrain, I think she has a big chance here."

Host Kate Tracey...

"I can't resist Blueking d'Oroux, who has switched stables from Paul Nicholls to Dan Skelton. We ran the figures of the stable switches, and it's definitely been a positive moving to Skelton. He has been a slow burner when early up he was beaten at 1-2 on chasing debut when with Paul Nicholls.

"He's going to be tuned up for this today and has been his target, back into a handicap off a mark that isn't his career high, I think he is fascinating at 11-2."

Sam Boswell…

"There were bullish comments around Meetmebythesea and ante-post movements around him for the King George at Christmas. I will be joining the Ben Pauling fan club and think he will go well here but the price is on the sharp side. He won the Jack Richards last year impressively and fits the right profile for the race.

"He's a second season chaser who could progress more - it's unoriginal but I am sticking with the favourite here."

Watch Weekend Winners in full on the At The Races YouTube channel...

Sports.title: Tearful Pochettino says leaving USA for Manchester United ‘most difficult decision’ of career: football – live
Sports.content:
From 7h ago 07.01 EST Manchester United confirm Pochettino appointment Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from the US men’s national team to Manchester United has been confirmed. Pochettino will guide the US through a pair of Concacaf Nations League matches on Saturday and Tuesday before joining United, for whom his first game will come at Liverpool next Sunday. The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton manager has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal to replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after leading United to their worst start to a season in four decades. More to follow. Mauricio Pochettino’s switch from USA to Manchester United confirmed Read more Share

37s ago 13.34 EST Richard Hirst has something to add. “With Carrick, and presumably his assistants, gone and the new management, sorry coaches, not arriving till the middle of next week, is this the moment when the traffic cones have actually taken over training at Utd? You really couldn’t make it up. Carry on SJR/Jason, you’re doing a great job.” Share

5m ago 13.30 EST Joshua Keeling mails in with his thoughts on United’s new ePoch (sorry). “Pochettino will probably fail, given the mess United are in. But I desperately hope he succeeds. He’s a club builder, hopefully the club give him the tools he needs.” Share

7m ago 13.28 EST In other news, the Aberdeen chair, Dave Cormack, has admitted the club’s financial performance “falls short of the standards we set ourselves” after their latest accounts showed an operating loss of £6.2m. Aberdeen reported a record turnover of £24.4m for the year up to 30 June 2026, which the club attributed to participation in the Conference League last season alongside “strong performances across commercial, retail, ticketing and hospitality operations”. But they posted an Ebitda (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) loss of £4m and an operating loss of £6.2m, compared with a loss of £1.5m in the previous financial year. The club finished ninth in the Scottish Premiership last term after sacking their manager, Jimmy Thelin, in January and put their financial losses down to increased investment in football operations, a “disappointing” season on the pitch, increased operating costs and lower gains from player sales. “While we are pleased to report record turnover, the overall financial outcome falls short of the standards we set ourselves and reflects the significant challenges experienced during the 2025-26 season,” Cormack said. “The board made a conscious decision to invest heavily in the football department with the aim of driving success on the pitch. Unfortunately, the performances and results achieved did not deliver the return we expected from that investment, and that is reflected in these results. “That said, the underlying strength of the club’s revenue streams continues to be encouraging. Achieving record turnover and record partnership revenue demonstrates the continued loyalty of our supporters, the commitment of our commercial partners, and the hard work of our staff across all areas of the business.” Press Association Share

19m ago 13.16 EST What do you make of Pochettino’s chances at United, readers? Email me with your thoughts, ideally publishable ones. Share

27m ago 13.08 EST Well, hello there. As the blog heads into injury time, we’ve got an email from Peter Oh. “I’m trying really hard not to have a major tissue, I mean issue with Poch’s tears,” he writes. “But let’s be honest. It’s all a bit performative, isn’t it?” Share

33m ago 13.02 EST Tonight’s schedule is mainly Nations League stuff. Netherlands v Greece, Serbia v Germany, Scotland v North Macedonia and Slovenia v Switzerland are all 7.45pm (GMT) kick-offs in Leagues A and B, while Moldova are 1-0 up versus Kazakhstan at half-time of their League C game. That’s all from me. Will Magee will guide you through till closing time. Share Updated at 13.05 EST

45m ago 12.50 EST Pep Guardiola to become Pochettino’s successor at the USMNT? That’s what the swirling rumours are already suggesting at this very early stage. We shall see … Share

1h ago 12.38 EST Nations League: Konrad Laimer is convinced Austria can beat the Republic of Ireland in Linz in their Saturday night clash despite the absence of key personnel. Austria are in control of their own destiny, leading the group by three points heading into their final two fixtures, and would earn automatic promotion to League A with victory over the Republic. Ralf Rangnick has been dealt a double blow, adding Xaver Schlager and Alexander Prass to an ever-growing list of injured players ahead of the Ireland match and Tuesday’s group-stage closer against Israel. “We have to exert some pressure,” said Laimer. “We have to look to see if we can get some chances to score goals. The Republic of Ireland have a good team, but I think if we perform well we can win the game tomorrow.” PA Share

1h ago 12.31 EST Transfer rumour: It has not taken long for Manchester United to be linked with a Pochettino-coded player. Reports suggest United are taking an interest in Como and Argentina attacker Nico Paz, who terrorised Michael Carrick’s side in their recent 4-1 Champions League defeat in Italy. Paz is the son of former Argentina international Pablo Paz, an old teammate of Pochettino’s with Newell’s Old Boys. Share

1h ago 12.23 EST Is Pochettino tough enough for the United job? I received this email during my earlier stint on the blog about the new head coach, via reader Ronnie. I’ve not seen a whole heap of anti-Poch stuff today – the bile/anger has mainly been directed at those above him at United – but it’s an interesting argument. double quotation mark United need a big personality and, to be frank, the meanness in Deschamps or Tuchel. Very surprised at the Poch appointment. He seems a good guy, perhaps too nice, with a positive playing style and the players, in good times, loved him. But in bad times it’s been a disaster. PSG? Couldn’t deal with the big characters. Spurs? Falling to pieces when they should have been kicking on after losing the Champions League final. Shipping 7 against Munich at home in 2019? The players wanted him gone. Yes he has a temper to scold but, in the end, he’s too soft and cannot deal with strong or turbulent characters. It’s simply not a quality in his bag and that’s not going to change. The players will walk all over him like a doormat. Meanwhile, the execs won’t leave him and the dressing room alone to do the job. And poor Poch simply has not got the wherewithal in those narrow shoulders to deal with the bullies, the melodrama, nor the size of United. Share

1h ago 12.11 EST Simon was too modest to plug it too much, but I enjoyed his illuminating passage in the latest Football Daily newsletter (are you subscribed yet?) on Pierre Sage’s ill-fated stint as Crystal Palace manager: double quotation mark His supporters, such as they are, would argue he was hobbled by knack, suspensions and poor transfer dealings, and approximately nothing went to plan for the man who just six months ago was revelling in being named Ligue 1 coach of the year. His philosophy just never quite translated. “There are two types of teams: one with the ball, and the other chasing it,” he said last year. “I prefer to be the first of those.” And it is true that in Ligue 1 last season only Paris St-Germain and Marseille had, on average, more of the ball than his Lens side. But it turned out that Crystal Palace players were quite happy chasing it thank you, whichever of them he picked – and he picked most of them, fielding more players than any other club this season. Share

1h ago 12.05 EST Very kind of you Simon. Maybe Pochettino’s tears were simply a result of thinking about the huge undertaking he’s about to tackle at Old Trafford? It seems to be he’s starting from the very very bottom, with no guarantee that things will automatically improve. More Poch/United stuff in the next hour? You bet! Share

2h ago 12.02 EST And with that, I’m going to make a tearful farewell. And the good news is, Dominic Booth is back! Share

2h ago 11.57 EST Here’s the definitive update from Pablo Iglesias Maurier at Mauricio Pochettino’s press conference in Fayetteville, Georgia. View image in fullscreen USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino: “It’s a tough decision but at the same time we are excited for the next step forward.” Photograph: Press Association/PA There were always going to be tears at Mauricio Pochettino’s news conference at US Soccer’s national training center on Friday. It was only a matter of when. Pochettino is famously emotional, and nobody in attendance had to wait long for the waterworks – they came during his introductory remarks, as he thanked the US Soccer executives flanking him for the opportunity to guide the US men. He grew emotional again as he addressed his impending departure for Manchester United, one announced just hours earlier. “I think [the decision was],” Pochettino said, pausing to compose himself, “one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.” The news conference read very much as a farewell to Pochettino, but there is still work to be done. The Argentinian will guide the USMNT through a pair of Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti on Saturday and Tuesday. In the meantime, the future United coach did his best to address questions about his departure and what comes next. Much more here: Tearful Pochettino says United job was ‘difficult to turn down’ in USMNT farewell Read more Share Updated at 12.01 EST

2h ago 11.30 EST Laura Cochrane has written about Jude Bellingham’s commercial savvy. Warning: this article contains photos of Bellingham’s naked torso. As one public relations consultant tells her: double quotation mark Bellingham is an exceptional sporting talent, and his brand value is understandably enormous. But fashion doesn’t create that value, football does. Fashion merely provides another means of exploiting it. There’s very, very much more here: Branding it like Beckham: how Jude Bellingham is future-proofing his fame Read more Share

2h ago 11.23 EST “I am a very emotional guy,” said Mauricio Pochettino as he dabbed at the tears during his press conference today. You don’t say? View image in fullscreen Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino celebrates after their stunning victory over Ajax in the 2019 Champions League semi-final. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino, Manager of Tottenham Hotspur, during a game against Arsenal in April 2017. Photograph: Shaun Botterill/Getty Images Share

2h ago 11.10 EST Pablo Maurer, who covers USMNT for us, was at training today to see Mauricio Pochettino saying a few (almost) farewells, including this embrace with Christian Pulisic. The two are not believed to have a close relationship, though last year Pulisic said this: double quotation mark We have good conversations. Honestly. Probably what you guys experience and what the media sees is a bit not exactly what we experience. Things are good. We spoke. We had a normal camp and everything is good between us, good between the team. There’s probably not as much drama as you guys think there is. Allow content provided by a third party?
