To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'. Allow and continue Share

3h ago 10.47 EST Don’t worry, human rights, Uefa’s got your back. Here’s Reuters: Uefa has established a Human Rights ⁠Advisory Board to provide independent oversight and advice ⁠during the ⁠planning ​and delivery of Euro 2028, the governing body said ⁠on Friday. The board will serve as a platform ⁠for constructive dialogue, external scrutiny ​and specialist guidance ‌on identifying, ‌preventing and mitigating human rights risks ‌linked to the tournament. The initiative builds on Uefa’s previous work with Human Rights Advisory Boards established for Euro 2024 ‌in Germany and Women’s Euro 2025 in Switzerland. “The Human Rights ​Advisory Board brings valuable independent perspectives and constructive challenge, helping us stay proactive as preparations progress ⁠and ensuring our commitments translate into ​meaningful ​action,” Uefa’s vice-president ​and board chair Laura ​McAllister said. Euro 2028 ​will ​be jointly hosted by England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales. Share

3h ago 10.35 EST We’ve been sent some photos of England’s players hard at work at Tottenham’s training ground today. I liked them, so here they are. Or some of them, anyway: View image in fullscreen James Hill, Morgan Gibbs-White and teammates stretch during an England recovery session at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Myles Lewis-Skelly of England and teammates do a stretch during a recovery session at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground. Looks like they’re punting. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane on stationary bicycles during an England recovery session at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images Share

3h ago 10.14 EST Hello everyone! I begin my time at the helm with some reaction to, yes, Pochettino’s appointment by Manchester United. Here are the thoughts of Henry James “Harry” Redknapp: double quotation mark Someone said to me today, ‘What a bad time to take the job’, I said, ‘I could never think of a better time to take over the Man United job’. They are rock-bottom. There’s only one way, it’s up. It isn’t like David Moyes following Alex Ferguson. David Moyes is a great manager, but following Fergie was impossible. Now he [Pochettino] takes over a club that is in a real mess at the moment, and he can only take one take them one way, and that is going to be up. I like him. He’s a great character, very clever manager, knows the game, and I’m sure he’ll do a good job. But it’s going to be two or three years before you see Man United anywhere near what you’d hope they would be. And here are the thoughts of Harry’s son, Jamie Redknapp: double quotation mark He’s an elite manager. I’m sure that [sporting director] Jason Wilcox, [chief executive] Omar Barada are probably thinking to themselves, ‘Are we lucky to keep our jobs?’. I think the answer to that would be yes, if they are to stay with that structure and regime. He’s coming into an environment now that’s going to be so difficult, he’s probably going to think after a few months, ‘Wow, have I made the right decision here?’. One of the biggest clubs in the world, but for the last few years has been so poorly run. I regret to report that the thoughts of Jamie’s children Charley, Beau and Raphael are currently unknown. View image in fullscreen An emotional Mauricio Pochettino speaking earlier on Friday. Photograph: Press Association/PA Share Updated at 10.20 EST

4h ago 10.01 EST Time to hand the blog to Simon Burnton for further Pochettino reflections and more. Here he is… Share

4h ago 09.55 EST Pochettino is doing his best not to talk about Manchester United – yet. But he does finally give away something. double quotation mark I think we will have time next week to talk about Manchester United, but now I think it is much better to talk about us, about USA Soccer, and of course, USA Men National Team, and we have two games ahead, and now it is focus complete on this. However, when pressed about why he’s leaving after just signing a new deal with the USMNT, he does throw us a little nugget. double quotation mark There’s not too many opportunities that happen in your career like a side of Manchester United and, of course, when that arrives it is difficult to turn down. Share

4h ago 09.47 EST Pochettino is asked if he’s satisfied about what he achieved during his time at USMNT. double quotation mark I think it’s difficult in that business, always you want more, and then you are a critic, and you say, ‘oh, I could be better, I should do better things, do better things’. Always it’s being brave, take the best decision, to get the experience from that decision, what happened, and try to adapt again, and to try to make better decisions for the future. I don’t like to use satisfaction, being satisfied of what happened in the past. That’s always, I think, in our mindset, it’s always we try to do better, and do better and try to find a way to, maybe in this similar situation, act in the always best way. Share

4h ago 09.40 EST Pochettino composes himself. Aware that this is U.S. Soccer goodbye rather than a Manchester United hello, his focus is on his time in charge of USMNT. He dodges the question on what appealed about the United job. double quotation mark I want to thank the fans for the support, for everything. And of course, always, it was a tough moment. Like I said before, it’s a really tough decision. But at the same time, we are excited for that step forward. But now it’s not the moment to talk, it’s the moment to be committed, like always we are. And care, because we really care. And always we are going to care about the federation and the players and all the people that are here. It’s to be focused in the next game because it’s really important for the federation. The players are amazing and they know how to manage this type of situation. It’s true that it’s not ideal, but it’s never an ideal situation when this type of thing happens. But in life, football is quick to move. That is why we need to move forward, I think. To keep that relationship and all the memories that we share. I think we were amazing. Share

4h ago 09.31 EST Pochettino bids tearful farewell to USA Mauricio Pochettino is giving a surprisingly emotional press conference as he officially announces his departure from the USMNT for Manchester United following their next two games. When thanking officials for the opportunity he was given, his voice cracks and out comes a tissue to wipe away the tears. “We learned a lot from you all, from this amazing country,” Pochettino said. “I think this was one of the most difficult decisions of [my] career.” View image in fullscreen A tearful Mauricio Pochettino speaks to reporters as he confirms his impending departure as USA head coach. Photograph: Colin Hubbard/AP Share Updated at 10.42 EST

4h ago 09.29 EST If you want your Football Weekly in video form, this is the link for you. 57:07 Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United and record breaker Kane | Football Weekly video Share

4h ago 09.14 EST We’re all aware now that Pochettino’s first game in charge is at Anfield. But what comes after that? His first six matches comprise four in the Premier League and two in the Champions League. 22 Nov: Liverpool v Man Utd

25 Nov: Sporting v Man Utd

28 Nov: Man Utd v Brentford

2 Dec: Newcastle v Man Utd

5 Dec: Man Utd v Coventry

8 Dec: Man Utd v RB Leipzig Three away games in the first four isn’t ideal or perhaps it is. Poch can start to bed in on the road where the away fans will perhaps give him more leeway. Sporting away is tough given that the Portuguese side have won three of their first four Champions League matches in the group phase. But Leipzig are down in 29th while Coventry and Newcastle are in the bottom half of the Premier League. Brentford sit 12th in the six-match EPL form table after two wins, two draws and two defeats. In other words, there are opportunities to turn the ship around. Share

4h ago 09.05 EST Cheers Dom. That seems a fair summation of my plans. I’ll start with some Poch… Share

5h ago 09.00 EST Right, I shall hand back to David Tindall who will no doubt provide much more United/Pochettino chat, with the occasional post about something else. Share

5h ago 08.52 EST Valérien Ismaël has been appointed as Le Havre coach until the end of the season, with the club sitting rock bottom in the Ligue 1 standings. The 51-year-old former defender, who was hired as a replacement for Didier Digard, will face a huge task to keep Le Havre in the French top tier. Still winless in Ligue 1, Le Havre have two points from 10 matches. The much-traveled Ismaël has coached teams in Germany, Greece, Austria, Turkey and England, and was most recently at Blackburn. Le Havre said in a statement yesterday that he has handled “emergency situations” in the past, “which could prove very useful in the coming weeks.” AP Share

5h ago 08.47 EST Will Carlos Baleba become a key man for United under Pochettino? Much has been made of the Argentinian’s desire to see his teams run, run, and then run some more. In the space of one season at Chelsea, Pochettino improved their running stats. Baleba looks to be the only current United midfielder with the legs to cover large spaces. Pochettino often prefers a 4-2-3-1, so surely it stands to reason that the former Brighton player will fit in as one of two deep-lying midfielders? Kobbie Mainoo would appear to be the ideal partner for Baleba – and we know Pochettino likes to promote young homegrown talent. What that means for summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, it remains to be seen. But the news that Bruno Fernandes probably won’t sign a new contract, could mean a shift in the structure of United’s midfield. Santos was loaned out by Chelsea to Nottingham Forest and Strasbourg during Pochettino’s sole campaign at Stamford Bridge. United may well look to recruit more hard-running midfielders in January or the summer to suit Pochettino’s preferences. Share

5h ago 08.26 EST Just watching Carrick’s end-of-season speech on the Old Trafford turf from May, after a 3-2 win over Nottingham Forest. I suspect he won’t be repeating his praise of the United playing staff, but that connection with the Stretford End is most certainly evident. Share

5h ago 08.16 EST Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu will step down next week, the country’s football association revealed today, cutting short his tenure in the wake of the 2027 Asian Cup’s postponement. Moriyasu, Japan’s longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa. But the Asian Football Confederation announced last week that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to “exceptional circumstances” in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country. That left Moriyasu in limbo, with Japan Football Association (JFA) chiefs last week declining to clarify when the coaching handover would take place. They said that Japan’s friendlies in Singapore against Brazil on Saturday and Paraguay on Tuesday would be Moriyasu’s last games in charge. AFP Share

6h ago 08.03 EST Reports are already emerging suggesting Pochettino will bring Jesús Pérez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jiménez, Sebastiano Pochettino (his son) and Sílvia Tuyà with him to Manchester United. Coaching squad, assemble! Share

6h ago 07.56 EST Wow, that’s quite the emotional and heartfelt message from Carrick, speaking directly to the United supporters. That’s a bond that will not be broken, despite the events of the past few months. He may not have been up to the job, but Carrick remained classy and dignified until the end. Share

6h ago 07.53 EST Michael Carrick statement on Manchester United exit The former head coach has taken to Instagram to address United fans and his departure from the club. double quotation mark Dear United fans, I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love. There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I am incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time … I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special rare breed … I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies. I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing … would be to turn the other way. That means more than a win or two … I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on. Sports.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
GONE IN SOIXANTE SECONDS

So farewell then, Pierre Sage. Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate. The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug.

His supporters, such as they are, would argue he was hobbled by knack, suspensions and poor transfer dealings, and approximately nothing went to plan for the man who just six months ago was revelling in being named Ligue 1 coach of the year. His philosophy just never quite translated. “There are two types of teams: one with the ball, and the other chasing it,” he said last year. “I prefer to be the first of those.” And it is true that in Ligue 1 last season only Paris St-Germain and Marseille had, on average, more of the ball than his Lens side. But it turned out that Crystal Palace players were quite happy chasing it thank you, whichever of them he picked – and he picked most of them, fielding more players than any other club this season.

They are averaging 43.2% possession, more than only Coventry and Hull. Against Tottenham at the end of October – when, to be fair, they were hobbled by a 13th-minute red card – they had the ball just 20.8% of the time – which, at least since 2013-14, they’ve never come close to equalling – and ended with an xG of 0.14 – not as bad as the 0.12 they registered against Manchester City in August 2022 (a game which, somehow, they ended with two goals), but worse than all their other ones. “It is,” Sage sighed after the Spurs match, “a disaster.” In that interview Sage said his “main principles” included “to look to get behind the opposition defence non-stop; and to press your opponents hard so you can win the ball back quickly,” Again, lovely ideas.

But Sage’s Palace were absolutely rubbish at pressing – on Opta’s pressed sequences metric, measuring “the number of open-play sequences starting in their defensive third where the opposition has three or fewer passes and the sequence ends in their own half”, they are currently bottom of the league, and what high turnovers they have managed have led to just eight shots (second-bottom) and no goals (bottom). As for getting behind the opposition defence non-stop, Opta has recorded 24 through-balls this season, which actually is the fifth-highest total in the league. They have also recorded 23 offsides. Still, we should take a minute (but no more) to mark another coach’s departure. Farewell, Pierre, and good luck. You certainly had none of it over here.

Sports.title: Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think
Sports.content:
There was a time when the games between the top three – traditionally Chelsea, Manchester City and Arsenal – were title-deciders. Where every point taken off a title rival was key. Such was the gap in investment and quality between those teams and the rest of the Women’s Super League, it was extremely rare that points would be dropped to teams outside that elite clique.

As the WSL has grown in investment, profile and size, that narrative has started to shift a little. The investment gap is still large from the top to the bottom of the league. But increased investment among the best of the rest and even among those teams further down the table, as well as an increase in high-quality coaches with the tactical and technical vision to get more from players, is having an impact.

That’s a roundabout way of saying that when Chelsea welcome the title holders and current league leaders to Stamford Bridge on Saturday lunchtime, counterintuitively, the three points isn’t the most important takeaway. Instead, based on the state of play, it’s the momentum, confidence, belief and bragging rights that are critical.

Naturally, should Chelsea win and thus leapfrog Manchester City, then the title race will be considered wide open. If Andrée Jeglertz’s City extend their lead over Chelsea from two points to five, even at this early stage, they will be considered favourites for the title in May, but it will be said with a little less confidence than it might have been in previous years.

The WSL is more and more competitive year on year. There have been only two occasions, in the 15 years since the first WSL season was played (after it was launched to replace the FA Women’s Premier League National Division), when the title winners have lost more than two games in a season. Both of those have come in the last three years, with Chelsea the first to do so in 2023-24 and then Manchester City last season.

You could say that because wins are less consequential in the games between title rivals, those games are less thrilling, but the reality is that the growing unpredictability of almost every match across the WSL means that every game becomes a must-watch.

At Stamford Bridge on Saturday, the remaining two unbeaten teams have the opportunity to inflict a first defeat. Neither side has looked infallible this season. City have kept just two clean sheets in their 13 games in all competitions, while Chelsea stuttered last weekend, with their second draw of the season allowing City to move above them.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City leapfrogged Chelsea at the top of the WSL after beating West Ham last weekend. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

Arguably, there has been a momentum shift between Sonia Bompastor’s and Jeglertz’s teams, with the former having dropped points against Everton before a 0-0 draw with the Swedish side Häcken in the Champions League while City earned a 5-0 win over West Ham and picked up a first win in Europe, after three draws, with a 4-1 defeat of Inter.

Jeglertz said that moving top had changed nothing before this clash. “We’re still early in the season. We want to win all games. That’s our focus this weekend,” he said. “Nothing has changed from that point of view and I don’t think it will have for them either.”

Chelsea have been defensively strong, and are the only WSL team to still be in single figures for goals conceded, on five to City’s 10, and they have kept nine clean sheets in their 13 games in all competitions (not including Champions League qualifying).

However, the key to the west London side’s ambition of drawing first blood between the two teams this season will probably centre around how well they cope without Lauren James.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

They may lead the way in goals scored too, 28 to City’s 27, but against Everton the absence of the England forward’s creativity was keenly felt and Chelsea’s attack looked a little predictable. Everton nullified the impact of the wide players Ellie Carpenter and Sandy Baltimore and Chelsea struggled to find another way through.

“My job is to make sure I find solutions when some players are not available and not playing for the team,” Bompastor said last week.

While Chelsea have to cope with the absence of James, who has a hamstring injury that Bompastor says means they “won’t see her until the end of this block” – up until at least the international break at the end of the month – City have players returning.

Rebecca Knaak is fine after a knock to the head against Inter and Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead and Niamh Charles are on their way back. “All three of them, actually, were in the session today and I hope that they will be available for Saturday,” said Jeglertz. Advantage City then, just.

In a way, that it is unlikely that this result decides either team’s season makes it a more interesting and exciting contest, because players are free to play uninhibited by the pressure of how catastrophic a loss could be and, with the two dominant teams going head to head, we’re in for a show.

Sports.title: It’s Happy Harry Kane day as England’s finest seizes his moment in style | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
Happy Harry Kane day! And many happy Harry returns. There is a process in clinical psychology known as semantic satiation. Subjects are asked to repeat a word or phrase so many times that it loses any kind of meaning. Suddenly “daffodils” is just an absurd, empty set of sounds. So it was in the buildup to Harry Kane’s record-breaking 126th cap, at the end of Harry Kane Ballon d’Or fortnight, as Harry Kane’s England were led out by top scorer Harry Kane, climax to a week of Harry Kane tributes, Harry Kane montages, 26-page Harry Kane … wait. Where were we?

This was that kind of occasion from start to finish, a night where you expected to look up from your desk mid-match to see Kane’s head looming helpfully over your shoulder, to enter the Wembley toilets at half-time and find him silently offering you a breath mint and a scented tissue.

Football loves its rankings and ratings. England loves a formal march-past. The Harry Kane moment was always going to come at Wembley. And it duly arrived with 61 minutes gone and the score 1-1 in a meandering game of mid-November England product.

There may be less satisfying ways to decide a game of football than a VAR-screen penalty awarded for an overly prolonged grab of the collar on a player who wasn’t going to get the ball. But it’s hard to think of many right now.

View image in fullscreen Kane calmly strokes his penalty beyond Dominik Livakovic. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

It was enough here. There was a gathering roar from the Wembley crowd, luxuriating in the prospect of a Kane penalty sequence: the pre-kick close-up, the jaw, the stare, the iconic hairline. Kane delivered, rolling the ball into the centre of the goal. There was a leap, a punch of the air, an embrace in front of a billowing George Cross flag.

At times like these it is hard to remember a time when Kane wasn’t exactly here doing exactly this, to accept that he won’t just be out there doing it for ever. Although the good news is he now gets to re-break the caps record every time he plays, thereby ensuring more ceremony, more pomp, more of that sweet, sweet, neural fatigue.

No doubt the haters will say: typical Kane. A low-key Wembley. A cheapish penalty kick. The numbers ticking over. But that’s the haters for you, as relentless in their own way as Kane himself. The goal made it 92 in 126 games, which really is mind-boggling in its focus and longevity, the sheer will to keep doing this. Imagine not thinking Kane is England’s best player since Bobby Charlton. What else are you supposed to do out there?

Wembley had been cold and crisp at kick-off, gripped with the familiar echoey, midweek chill, the booming PA, the thin air, like being present at a vast corporate presentation or the opening of a mega-sale in the world’s largest out-of-town DIY warehouse.

The military personnel wobbled the massive flag. Tongues of fire leapt around the perimeter. And as the teams lined up there was a surprise appearance from the real star of this stage, the Ballon d’Or itself, wreathed in event glamour and star-flash.

Kane drew the ballon from its stone in Arthurian fashion, then held it a little sheepishly in one hand. Prince William walked out and gave him a massive framed shirt, which seemed weird in the moment, like the chief area sales manager presenting the prize from the Christmas raffle. Has Prince William ever been asked to carry anything before?

A little earlier a vast Harry Kane tifo had appeared at one end, showing Kane in full roaring lion mode. It carried the tagline “England’s finest”, which sounds like a type of cheddar cheese you can buy at the airport gift shop. But it’s also a good compromise. He is indeed very fine.

It was a striking coronation for a player who made his debut here 11 years ago as a promising other-guy under Roy Hodgson. There is still a similar element of double-take about that Ballon d’Or. Kane has always seemed like one of those sports people destined to be reaching for something, constantly in search of a final validation. This has been his strength and his energy. Well, we’re here now. Kane has his notch on the forever tree. Ultimacy arrived on a London stage dressed in a shiny tuxedo.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane is captured with a huge England flag in the background. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

This does change something. Kane’s entire professional life is now divided into two parts. Everything up to 26 October 2026. And then the last 17 days. How does it feel now? Is the air pressure different, the noise in his head, the tension in his ears?

Here the whole team started slowly. In the opening four and a half minutes Croatia had 92 per cent possession and England made one pass. Thomas Tuchel was up early in his puffy winter coat, tight black slacks and black business shoes, like an actuary going sledging. Kane lurked in some strange deep position and played one or two overambitious passes.

Is this something new? Arrogant Kane. Big-shot Kane. Has he become our Ronaldo? Maybe he should have angrily retired straight after the game and promised to speak his truth on a YouTube chatshow.

Instead Kane helped to make the opening goal for Morgan Rogers, set up with a lovely floated diagonal pass and an expert cutback from Jude Bellingham. England faded a little and were pegged back around the hour. Lewis Hall played well. Trent Alexander-Arnold was fun to watch. They have now definitively qualified for the Nations League knockouts, which is certainly a thing. But in the end this was always going to be Harry’s day.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers says ‘it’s a lie’ that Cole Palmer does not want to play for England
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers has said accusations that his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer is not committed to playing for England are “a lie”.

Palmer, who was left out of the squad for this week’s Nations League ties against Croatia and Spain, has faced questions over his desire to play international football since withdrawing from last month’s camp with a groin injury. Thomas Tuchel, who did not take the 24-year-old to last summer’s World Cup, expressed irritation at the time, saying the Chelsea attacker “misses too many opportunities” to play for his country.

Tuchel last week insisted Palmer’s latest exclusion was “not personal” but he has placed plenty of store in players showing up to camp. The German has previously said it was “hard to argue” when it was put to him that Palmer does not want to play for the national team after his fourth withdrawal from a squad. But Rogers, who scored in England’s 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday, delivered a strong rebuttal to claims his friend and teammate is not dedicated to the national team.

“It’s a lie,” Rogers said. “He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done. People just see it as news and say the easy thing.

“We all know he had a difficult year last year with injuries and I know personally he’s been managing them injuries ever since. He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn’t feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself. Of course he does, who wouldn’t? But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 to 15 years, he also has to manage himself.

“If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it. It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It’s a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don’t get it and he doesn’t get it. But it’s something he has to deal with but I can assure you he wants to be here and he wants to play for his country.”

Tuchel had no issue with Rogers’s defence of Palmer. “It’s totally fine, it’s his teammate and friend,” England’s manager said. “I was very happy with the emotional commitment and physical commitment of Morgan. He was our standout player today.”

Tuchel is not short of options at No 10 and has selected Eberechi Eze, Rogers and Josh King as cover for Jude Bellingham. Rogers played on the right against Croatia and opened the scoring as England secured the win that secured England’s place in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

England were pegged back by Petar Sucic’s equaliser but they restored their lead thanks to Harry Kane converting a penalty on the night when the captain became his country’s most capped player. Tuchel’s side will win Group A3 if they beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday. But the occasion was slightly overshadowed by Ben White being booed when he came on in the second half. Some fans are yet to forgive White for his self-imposed exile after his early departure from the camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“I didn’t hear the boos,” Tuchel said. “I thought we were past it. I hope it doesn’t happen again. He is a player for us. Since I came in he is desperate to be in the group. He hasn’t put a foot wrong since I am in charge. He is part of our group and I will protect our group. He deserved to be with us and I hope to open a new chapter for him.”

Sports.title: Robertson pays tribute to Dalglish as he matches Scotland cap record
Sports.content:
Andy Robertson insists his matching of Kenny Dalglish’s Scotland cap record by no means brings reputational parity. Four decades after Dalglish, widely regarded as the country’s finest player, ended his international run at 102 games Robertson will hit the same figure with the visit of North Macedonia to Hampden Park on Friday.

The Tottenham full-back is understandably delighted by his own tally – and should surpass Dalglish in Switzerland on Monday – but paid glowing tribute to the man he got to know well during nine years at Liverpool.

“For how long the record stood, for starters, for what he achieved in his career, for the person he is,” Robertson said.

“Tomorrow is another reason for our country to honour one of the greatest players that has played a game. He’s definitely the greatest from Scotland. I think it’s another reason for everyone to speak about him and realise his achievements in his footballing career. And also the person that he has been throughout his whole life.

“Obviously, in terms of number, I will stand side by side with him but I don’t want people to forget how important this man has been to our country.”

The Liverpool connection between Robertson and Dalglish adds an endearing, personal element. “He reminds me all the time that getting into the 100 caps back then was a lot harder than it is now,” said Robertson with a smile. “I never set myself personal goals. For me it’s always about the team and how I best deal with the team and things like that.

“When I overtook Darren Fletcher, when I was in the 80s, it felt like it took ages for me to get to Jim Leighton [at 91]. Then I thought: ‘I’ve only got one more to go.’

That’s when I started thinking about it a little bit more, starting to believe that it might happen a little bit more, starting to wind-up Kenny a bit more that it was going to happen. Sat here today, if it happens, it’s something I couldn’t be more proud of.’’

Sébastien Pocognoli, the Scotland manager, has said the country is stepping up efforts to convince eligible players born in England to commit their international futures to Scotland. Archie Gray and Hayden Hackney are among those who qualify to play for Scotland but have, thus far, resisted overtures. In conjunction with others at the Scottish Football Association, Pocognoli would like that to change. Gray’s position as a club-mate of Robertson’s may be significant in this context.

“We are on it,” Pocognoli said. “We are always proactive in all of these situations. What is very exciting about those two names [Gray and Hackney] is that they are young players.

“That’s interesting. We have to look and manage the situation. But it won’t be a definitive choice from them because we weren’t proactive. That has to be clear. We are proactive.”

Sports.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
Sports.content:
It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player. You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball.

These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.

Reader, it did not. But it did set a precedent that is being enthusiastically revived. It’s even possible that, after several decades of hurt, the world’s favourite sport may finally be getting its artistic due. There have been three iterations of the Football Art Prize in the past 20 years, and the latest arrives at the National Football Museum this month (from the Sheffield Millennium Gallery) with a breadth of entries that demonstrate how resonant the subject can be.

View image in fullscreen Felix Higham’s Newcastle 2 Barcelona 7, one of many exhibits that focus on football culture rather than the game itself. Photograph: Courtesy of the National Football Museum

Meticulous still lives – of battered balls, or boots mid-clean – ache with memory. There’s haunting photo-documentary: Bangladeshi youths playing a pickup game in the middle of a rubbish dump, pitches affected by climate change. “You see the whole gamut of footballing experience on display,” says the museum’s exhibitions director, Pip Diment. Her assumptions – she initially imagined herself hanging portraits of famous moments and iconic players – were overturned. “Pretty much every one of the artists is expressing how football matters to them, but they’re responding and reacting in such different ways.”

There are a few famous faces nevertheless. One artist worked in charcoals to create a hyper-realist bust of N’Golo Kanté. Roy Keane appears twice, once proffering a plate of prawn sandwiches to his viewer, another time in a diptych with Micah Richards. The latter is the work of Conor Rogers, whose satirical series of paintings on abandoned betting slips took second prize. They include a poignant image of Sheffield United’s manager, Chris Wilder, head in hands, next to a repurposed bookmaker’s logo asking: “Lad r u ok?”

Diment says football and art are still perceived as almost entirely separate spheres, so it’s interesting that this year’s winning work – a video by Alina Akbar – explores the connection between “high” and “popular” culture. In Footwork, the multimedia artist segues between keepy-uppy skills and the choreographed movements of Kathak, an Indian classical dance style. The combined rhythms and sounds create a mesmerising meditation on identity, related to the northern South Asian community in which she grew up.

View image in fullscreen Kyle King-Jagger ‘s Roy’s Rolls riffs on Roy Keane’s famous ‘prawn sandwich brigade’ comment. Photograph: Courtesy of the National Football Museum

Football, she says, is a post-migration culture whose value is sometimes overlooked by the very people who adopted it. “Whenever I went to my great-grandparents’ house, football was on TV all the time and I’d be on their street, trying out tricks,” says Akbar. “My grandad and his brothers were really excited when I started playing, because they’d gone through the more racist era of the 70s, and they never went to games.”

For all its social themes, Akbar’s work still expresses the balletic movement and poise that Picasso once pursued in the flowing form of his ceramic sculpture Footballeur. It’s interesting how so much of the art in the show reflects football culture rather than the game itself – watching from the sofa, in the pub, on the touchline of a recreational game. Perhaps it’s hard for artists to compete with the volume of visual content that the games already provide. And we have moved a long way from a classically inspired fascination with athletes’ physiques (for comparison, check out the leaping goalkeeper in Cecil Beaton’s mid-20th-century painting Footballers, with his unashamedly pert buttocks).

Tim Marlow, the director of the Design Museum and chair of the judging panel, points out that “artists today have unashamedly adopted the position of the spectator or the fan” and that it’s rare to find works that try to get inside the experience of the footballer themselves. One of his favourite exceptions is the 2006 film, Zidane: A 21st Century Portrait, which he calls “a great piece of conceptual art”. “It’s a really intimate study of the game, which in the current era, when you’ve got referees with head cams, might feel old hat, but nothing like it had been done before.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Keith Bird’s Full-time at Maine Road depicts Manchester City’s former home. Photograph: Courtesy of the National Football Museum

And then there’s Tottenham’s stadium gallery, OOF, where exhibitions of football-related work have ranged from Roger Mayne’s 1950s street photography to AC Larsen’s polemic on the FA’s trans ban. This month brought the opening of Trackie McLeod’s celebration of Wag culture. Historic football art, meanwhile, is rocketing in value. Four years ago Lowry’s Going To The Match went for £7.8m at auction, a record price for the Salford artist’s work, and in 2022 one of Nicholas de Staël’s Parc des Princes 1952 abstract series – based on a friendly he watched between France and Sweden – became the most expensive football artwork when it sold for £16.7m.

Money has always been a key element in the art world, and there are notable collectors within the footballing world today, from billionaire club owners to cultured former players. Fabio Capello has a well documented passion for Kandinsky; David Beckham’s collection is said to include Andy Warhol, Banksy and Yayoi Kusama; Michael Ballack is spotted at major art fairs around the world. The whimsically named J St John, who organised Football and Fine Arts, told the Liverpool Daily Post 70 years ago that art needed a new form of patronage, to help people appreciate the painted canvas in the same they understood the artistry of Joe Mercer, Ferenc Puskas and Stanley Matthews. Could his dream finally be coming to pass?

Sports.title: Arsenal dig deep to earn WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance
Sports.content:
Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, and they dug deep to hold on to a draw at the Camp Nou on Thursday night. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared.

Barcelona have been formidable when playing at the club’s main stadium, winning nine and drawing twice, against Chelsea in the semi-finals in 2023 and now Arsenal.

“Grit, resilience, discipline, clarity, communication, leadership, bravery – that’s a lot of words,” said Renée Slegers, whose side now lie fourth in the standings. “There’s a lot of really good things in this performance that we definitely want to build on.”

The last time these two teams met, Arsenal lifted the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect defensive performance and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time but Arsenal showed the guts they have been missing at times this season, against the team that retook their crown last season, and showed they can play ugly when needed.

There was one change to the team that earned a 2-1 win against Liverpool on Sunday, but it was a significant one. Olivia Smith was replaced by Maanum and the Norwegian slotted into the No 10 role with Alessia Russo, who has scored 12 goals in nine games for club and country, moving into the centre-forward position.

It was the England forward’s play on the left that set up the shock first-half goal that temporarily silenced the crowd. She beat two and worked the ball to Maanum. Barcelona got the ball away but Russo was there again and delivered a perfect cross across the face of goal for Caitlin Foord. The Australian forced a close-range save from Cata Coll only for Maanum to power in the loose ball.

The pocket of travelling fans behind plexiglass in the upper tier were jubilant. About 1,000 had travelled despite the late switch of the match to Thursday due to a 24-hour general strike in Spain on Wednesday.

Quick Guide Benfica bounce back to see off Austria Vienna Show Benfica rebounded from their humbling defeat by Arsenal last time out to claim a second Women’s Champions League victory of the season by seeing off struggling Austria Vienna 3-1. Beaten 3-0 at Meadow Park a fortnight ago following Alessia Russo’s hat-trick, Benfica had the ideal opportunity to get back to winning ways against a Vienna side who had picked up one point in three games. They went ahead at Lisbon’s Estadio da Luz through Andreia Norton in the fifth minute before Carina Wenninger levelled after half-time when Valentina Potzl was upended in the area by Lena Pauels. But Vienna goalkeeper Jasmin Pal’s 73rd-minute red card proved a turning point as Caroline Møller headed home before she teed up Nycole Raysla to score in time added on. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

The goal came decidedly against the run of play but Barcelona struggled to capitalise on their first-half dominance. Ewa Pajor and Graham Hansen were particularly threatening as Barcelona targeted Arsenal’s left, made up of the less experienced Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum.

The scoreline at the break was a little unfathomable based on the run of play and the domestic fortunes of both sides. While Arsenal languish in sixth in the WSL, 12 points behind the league leaders, Manchester City, Barcelona have won nine of their 10 games in Liga F, having scored 41 goals and built a five-point lead over their nearest rivals, Real Madrid.

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s Alessia Russo shows her dismay after a missed chance. Photograph: Álex Caparrós/Uefa/Getty Images

Arsenal’s gameplan felt familiar. It was as if they had studied the blueprint religiously followed by teams that have sat back in a low block and frustrated them week-in, week-out in the WSL this season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Aitana Bonmatí, the three-time Ballon d’Or winner, was surprisingly relegated to the bench but her arrival shortly before the hour elevated Barcelona’s threat, causing Arsenal’s defending to look even more calamitous at times, and lifted the mood in a frustrated stadium.

Three minutes after her arrival they were level. Esmee Brugts found an unmarked Graham Hansen on the right and she cut inside and swept in past Misa Rodríguez.

It was no surprise that Baum and Hinds, who had been run ragged, were removed soon after, with former Barcelona player Ona Batlle and Smith, Arsenal’s record signing, replacing them.

Arsenal were better after the goal and the changes, occasionally breaking free of their prison of a final third. At the end they were clinging on, but cling on they did.

“If we were to do it again, we’d try to stay on the ball for longer and play our game even more,” said Slegers. “Definitely there were moments in the first half and in the second half where we were really, really dangerous and created big chances, open chances. I’m just really pleased with the way we played the game tonight because it’s a very different game to what we usually play and that we can do it this way is a big boost for us as a team and that’s what we’re going to take with us going forward.”

Sports.title: Two Manchester United players can thrive under Mauricio Pochettino – look what he did with Dele Alli
Sports.content:
Two Manchester United players can thrive under Mauricio Pochettino – look what he did with Dele Alli

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to get the best out of Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo at Manchester United.

The new Red Devils boss will officially take charge at Old Trafford next week after being announced as Michael Carrick's successor.



4 Rashford and Mainoo have struggled for consistency so far this season - but that could soon change Credit: Getty

Pochettino, who will leave after USA's upcoming fixtures against Haiti, has signed a two-and-a-half year deal with the club as he looks to turn around their fortunes.

United are currently winless in their last eight Premier League matches, a run of form which resulted in Carrick's sacking on Thursday.

As a result, the Red Devils find themselves 18th in the table ahead of Pochettino's first match in charge against Liverpool on November 22.



Amongst those struggling for form is Rashford, who has yet to score or assist in eight appearances across all competitions this term.

Rashford and Mainoo tipped to 'thrive'

According to former Premier League goalkeeper and USA icon Brad Friedel, the forward can thrive under Pochettino this season.



The Argentinian has also been backed to take Mainoo to a new level thanks to his history of working with high potential players.

Speaking to Sam Matterface, Gabby Agbonlahor and Scott Minto live on talkSPORT, Friedel explained: "I think as opposed to trying to get a senior player on board, I think he’ll put his arm around some of the younger players that have incredible potential.



"Somebody like Marcus Rashford could really thrive under him if that’s one of the players that Mauricio pinpoints, Mainoo as well, players like that.

"If you look at what he did with Dele Alli at Spurs when he came in, kind of a similar situation.

"He’s very good at making players that he wants in his system, in his culture at the club, making them feel a million bucks.

4 Pochettino's success with Alli should give United's young stars confidence, says Friedel Credit: Getty



"He’s excellent at that and his whole staff is very good at that, being compassionate and making you feel wanted, making you feel possibly better than you are while making sure that you’re working hard.

"We’ve watched many Manchester United games and some of the games we’ve actually watched and we’ve come away saying, 'They’re just getting outworked at times,' you can’t have that.

"That’s one part of the game he won’t tolerate at all and it really has no meaning to him what your name is on the back of the shirt at all."

Pochettino signed Dele Alli for Tottenham Hotspur back in 2015 when the midfielder was aged just 18.



He would go on to score 55 goals and provide 48 assists in 194 appearances for Spurs under Pochettino.

Alli was also named PFA Young Player of the Year for the 2015/16 and 2016/17 seasons.

4 Here is how Pochettino compares to former United candidates Emery and Howe

Those campaigns also saw him included in the PFA Team of the Year as recognition for his performances.



During his time as Spurs boss, Pochettino secured a second place in the Premier League as well as two third place finishes and a run to the club's first-ever Champions League final.

Fernandes' future under Pochettino

Friedel was also questioned on whether Pochettino will want to keep Bruno Fernandes around the first-team squad.

The United captain has rejected a second new contract offer, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the season.

He added: "I think he’ll want his talent at the football club, but he won’t tolerate it if he does have an ego.



"I don’t know Bruno personally at all. I think Mauricio’s not a fool. He’ll want the best players on the pitch, but he’ll want them fully committed.

4 Fernandes' future will be an early hurdle for Pochettino to overcome Credit: Getty

"If they’re not he will work very quickly to get them out the door. I would imagine he will try to work with him at first and if he doesn’t think he’s going to fit then I don’t think it’ll be an issue for him to change him.

"He is a top quality player, we all know that. Mauricio builds a culture at the club. If he’s not going to buy into that then you’ll be out the door."

Sports.title: Manchester United handed perfect Bruno Fernandes replacement for Mauricio Pochettino to sign
Sports.content:
Nico Paz could be the signing to kickstart the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United - if they move on from Bruno Fernandes.

That's the view of talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who has named the Como starlet as a potential solution to one of the first dilemmas facing Pochettino following his appointment as Red Devils boss.



4 Como starlet Paz has been tipped to become Lionel Messi's long-term heir for Argentina Credit: Getty

After days of speculation, Pochettino was confirmed as Man United's new manager on Friday following Michael Carrick's sacking.

But with his new side sitting 18th in the Premier League, the ex-Tottenham and Chelsea boss inherits a less than ideal set of circumstances - made worse by recent news surrounding captain Fernandes.

The United talisman, whose current contract runs out at the end of the season, turned down a second offer from the club.



As it stands, Fernandes is free to negotiate with foreign clubs regarding a free transfer from January.

While United do have the option to trigger an automatic 12-month extension, the 32-year-old's latest decision makes it increasingly likely the club could consider moving him on next summer.



Having been inspirational since his arrival at Old Trafford in 2019 - scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists for United - Fernandes' departure would leave a gaping hole at the club.

However, former Aston Villa hero Agbonlahor believes Pochettino could look to rebuild his team with a face United are familiar with.



Is Paz the solution?

Discussing Pochettino's possible response to Fernandes' contract saga, Agbonlahor tipped him to consider signing Como sensation Paz - who starred with two stunning goals in his side 4-1 thrashing of United in October.

He told talkSPORT: “Maybe Pochettino comes in and says, ‘You know what? I don't like his attitude. I don’t like the way he throws his arms up at his teammates, the way he threw Michael Carrick under the bus. Can I go and get my own players?’

“Nico Paz - how good has he been? He's the next star for Argentina.

4 Bruno Fernandes is at a crossroads in his Man United career Credit: Getty

4 Pochettino arrives at Old Trafford with plenty to sort, including Fernandes' future at the club Credit: AFP



“Does he say, ‘You know what? I want him next summer from Como, make it happen’. Save the money on wages that maybe Bruno Fernandes wants.

“So he might have his own ideas to get all these players out that maybe have been a little bit of a problem [like], 'I want to refresh the whole squad.'”

Paz would certainly be a popular arrival at Old Trafford, given how he put United to the sword recently in the Champions League.

The 21-year-old is widely regarded as one of the most promising young talents in Europe after impressing in Italy.



A Real Madrid youth product, the Argentina international has starred under Cesc Fabregas at Como since his arrival in 2024, and boasts six goals and eight assists in 14 games altogether this term.

His exploits include three Champions League goals, firing the Italian side to three wins out of their first four European games.

4 Paz has earned 14 senior caps for Argentina, where he has been tipped for a bright future Credit: Getty

This follows a strong 2025/26 campaign, where Paz's 12 goals and seven assists in Serie A helped his team qualify for the Champions League for the first time in their history.



And the youngster is so highly thought of that he has even been touted as the eventual heir to Lionel Messi with his national team.

With Paz into the final 18 months of his Como contract, he won't be short of offers as he weighs up his next move.

And United could certainly prove a tempting option, with the appointment of fellow Argentine Pochettino meaning he would have a clear connection if he did move to Manchester.

Sports.title: New Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in tears over ‘most difficult decision of his career’
Sports.content:
New Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in tears over ‘most difficult decision of his career’

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears during his first press conference since being named Manchester United manager.

The Argentinian has been announced as Michael Carrick's successor on a two-and-a-half year deal.

4 Pochettino broke down in tears as he reflected on leaving his USA role Credit: YouTube/U.S. Soccer

Carrick was sacked on Thursday following an eight-match winless run in the Premier League.

Pochettino will officially begin his United tenure on November 19 following the USA's upcoming fixtures.

As a result, his first match as manager will be away against Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

Ahead of taking charge at Old Trafford, he will oversee the USA's matches against Haiti before stepping down as head coach.

The national team boss spoke to reporters on Friday prior to their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final first leg.

Emotional Pochettino on USA exit

A visibly emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he admitted the decision to leave his role for the United job was 'one of the most difficult' of his career.

Discussing his exit, he joked: "Normally it's the opposite. You're sacked and you cry because you want to stay.

"For this case it's the opposite. It's a really tough decision, but at the same time I'm excited for that step."

Pochettino added: "The staff and the players, I want to say thank you so much for the last two years.

"You made me feel really happy sharing an amazing project. It's difficult now for me to finish.

4 Pochettino's decision to leave the USA was 'one of the most difficult' of his career Credit: AFP

4 Pochettino's record compared to fellow United contenders Unai Emery and Eddie Howe

"We were very excited to share a project which we really believe in and are evolving together, it makes the decision harder.

"It's a sad decision but we are professionals, and we need to try to find the next step to make your dreams come true."

As he continued, Pochettino was in tears whilst admitting: "We increased the federation and around the world too.

"I didn't prepare a speech; I am talking from the heart. We recovered our motivation and the capacity to dig deep.

"I want to recognise the value from us and me. Big thank you. You respect your work. You never lie to us. That is a difficult decision but we need to move forward."

The 54-year-old was first appointed as USA boss in September 2024, signing a deal through to this summer's World Cup.

4 Pochettino guided the USA to the last 16 of this summer's World Cup Credit: AFP

Following the Stars and Stripes' run to the last 16, he was handed a four-year extension until the end of the 2030 finals.

Prior to facing Haiti this week, Pochettino has won 22 of his 35 matches in charge.

Sports.title: Scotland eye two Premier League stars for international switch from England
Sports.content:
Sebastien Pocognoli has revealed Scotland are stepping up their pursuit of recruiting Archie Gray and Hayden Hackney for international duty.

Tottenham star Gray and Everton summer signing Hackney were both born in England, but have strong ties to the Tartan Army through family heritage.



4 Still just 20, Archie Gray has been a Premier League regular for the last two years with Tottenham Credit: Getty

Gray is the son of former Scotland striker Andy and related to Leeds legends Frank and Eddie Gray, who both won caps for Scotland.

Despite this, the 20-year-old has represented England at every age group, except the senior team.

Meanwhile, ex-Middlesbrough star Hackney previously played for Scotland’s Under-21s side, before switching allegiances to play for the Three Lions' Under-21s.



Scotland make 'direct contact' with duo

Scotland boss Pocognoli has revealed he is ‘proactive’ in his hunt for players eligible to represent his team, and said moves have been made to persuade both stars to pledge their allegiances.

Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes is also still on the SFA’s radar, despite previously appearing to rule out donning a dark blue jersey.



Pocognoli said: “I am busy with everything. We know which players are eligible to represent the country one day.

“It won’t come from me, it has to come from them to show that one day they maybe represent the country. We will see in the future.



Asked if he has spoken to players who could play for Scotland, Pocognoli said: “Yeah, I have had direct contact or indirect contact.

"When I go to the direct contact it’s because I feel it’s a first positive approach. I’ve done it with many players. I’ll do my best to bring them.

“With Barnes it was different. I knew before my first camp that he was different. The two other lads [Gray and Hackney] are young lads. It’s a long way. But if you wait too long, it might not be the right moment. In a year’s time, we will see.

4 Hayden Hackney joined Everton in the summer after being named Championship Player of the Year with Middlesbrough last term Credit: Getty



4 Sebastien Pocognoli is actively looking to add more Premier League stars to his team Credit: Getty

“Right now, we have players in the squad who are performing well. It will always be up to them (current players) to be the priority. Because we’ve built things and we’ve had time with the ones who are here right now.

“But we are on it. We are always proactive in all of these situations.

"What is very exciting about those two names is that they are young players. That’s interesting. We have to look and manage the situation.”



Pocognoli - who succeeded Steve Clarke in the Scotland dugout in August - insisted producing a successful national team is the best way to convince Gray and Hackney to play for them.

He added: “The best way to convince players is to show good football, show them they can come to us, enjoy it and be successful.

“They have to feel when they leave a top club that they arrive here into top conditions and a top environment. That’s the best publicity we can offer, to show good football.”

4 English-born Scott McTominay has become a national hero with his heroics for Scotland Credit: Getty



Having qualified for three major tournaments under former boss Clarke, Pocognoli has been tasked with taking the Tartan Army further after all campaigns ended in group stage exits.

However, after an unconvincing start to life in the hotseat, the Belgian is in need of two big results in the upcoming double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

In last month's extended international break, Scotland managed to win just once, losing twice and drawing one of their four matches, prompting talkSPORT's Ally McCoist to label the national team's form a concern.

Sports.title: Man City to avoid imminent sanctions hearing with appeal to conclude first
Sports.content:
Man City to avoid imminent sanctions hearing with appeal to conclude first

Manchester City are unlikely to be sanctioned for their breaches of Premier League rules until their appeal has concluded.

The club's appeal against an independent commission's ruling takes place in December.

3 City will be handed sanctions in the new year if their appeal fails Credit: Getty

City were found guilty in September of all charges against them relating to alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.

Having first been charged in February 2023, the verdict was announced by the Premier League almost two years after a hearing was held.

The hearing saw the independent commission find that the club had inflated its financial position by more than £900million over a nine-year period.

With City appealing against the decision, a further hearing is now set to determine whether the ruling will stand.

When could City be sanctioned?

According to the Financial Times, any potential sanctions will be handed down to City in 2027 if their appeal proves to be unsuccessful.

An independent commission will give their verdict in the new year, with sanctions to follow if the verdict is upheld.

It means that City have successfully managed to avoid the sanctions hearing from taking place concurrently with their appeal.

Such a process had previously been a possibility following the initial guilty verdict.

Instead, City will now discover the outcome of their appeal before any hearing into possible sanctions takes place.

talkSPORT understands most lawyers believe this to be the most sensible approach.

3 Premier League rules allow for City to be expelled from the top-flight in 2027 Credit: Getty

The FT report adds that the Premier League rule book gives the independent commission permission to hand out a range of punishments.

Those include fines, points deductions and even expulsion from the top-flight.

However, it remains unclear when those sanctions could ultimately take effect.

City would once again have the right to appeal against any punishments put in place against them.

It subsequently raises the possibility of the process stretching beyond the end of the current season.

The Premier League campaign is scheduled to conclude on Sunday, May 30, 2027

3 Maresca's side currently sit third in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Next month's appeal hearing against the initial ruling is taking place three months after the verdict was announced.

Therefore it remains a possibility that any appeal against potential sanctions may not take place before April 2027.

City latest

City won three Premier League titles during the period in which their offences took place.

Meanwhile, the club have not played outside the top-flight since winning promotion in 2002.

Enzo Maresca's side are currently third in the table, six points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

It follows back-to-back defeats to Brighton and Nottingham Forest prior to the international break.

City also find themselves 13 points above the relegation zone 10 matches into the season.

Sports.title: Where to watch Spain v England as rivals battle to top Nations League group
Sports.content:
Where to watch Spain v England as rivals battle to top Nations League group

England are preparing for their final Nations League match against Spain and both sides can still finish top of Group A3.

Both sides have already secured their ticket to the quarter-finals and world champions Spain only need to avoid defeat to the Three Lions to ensure they finish first.



3 Kane became England's all-time most capped player in midweek, surpassing Peter Shilton Credit: Getty

England demolished Croatia 7-0 in October but Thursday night was a different tale after they secured an underwhelming 2-1 win over Slaven Bilic's side.

Thomas Tuchel's men won thanks to a strike by Morgan Rogers and a penalty from Harry Kane with the Bayern Munich striker making history as he was honoured as England's new record appearance maker on his 126th cap.

Spain will be favourites heading into the match after being victorious over England in the 2024 Euros final and in their Nations League group opener, where they triumphed 3-2 at Wembley.



The last time England were successful over La Roja came on Spanish soil in 2018, when Raheem Sterling and Marcus Rashford scored.

Where to watch Spain vs England

The fixture will kick-off at 7:45pm on Sunday, November 15 at Atletico Madrid's home, the Metropolitano Stadium.



It will be shown on free-to-air television and will be live on ITV1, with build-up starting from 7pm.

Mark Pougatch, Roy Keane and Ian Wright present the action before commentary from Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.



Fans can listen to live commentary of the match on talkSPORT, with Adrian Durham, Jim Proudfoot and former England striker Dean Ashton.

3 Yamal missed out on the action against Czechia, and is hopeful to return against the Three Lions Credit: Getty

Spain vs England team news

Ezri Konsa should be back in contention after missing the Croatia game on Thursday.

The Arsenal defender and Djed Spence have spent the majority of the England camp training separately.



However, Tuchel has been hopeful that the pair can return before they travel to Madrid.

Both will compete as options for Jarell Quansah's place following his mistake which led to Croatia's equaliser.

3 Tuchel felt his side were messy yet admitted they 'desperately' wanted to win the game still Credit: Getty

Tuchel wants England to end their 2026 campaign on a high with a victory over world champions Spain.



The German said: "The winner takes it all. Even like you see today like in the last 10 minutes, where it gets nervous and a bit tense and Croatia is pushing, these are important moments for us to overcome and to learn from them.

"We need exactly these games. Now it's a final for the group victory. We want we wanted exactly this kind of match, and we want the victory in Spain."

Luis de la Fuente's side will also hope to strengthen ahead of the highly anticipated match as they expect Lamine Yamal and Oyarzabal to return.

Sports.title: Premier League club caught up in worldwide Microsoft outage chaos
Sports.content:
Chelsea have provided an update after the club were impacted by Friday's global Microsoft outage.

Microsoft 365 services around the world have been hit with 'connectivity problems'.



3 Chelsea have been affected by the global Microsoft outage Credit: Getty

Efforts to fix the issues, which have affected more than 430million people, have so far been unsuccessful.

It has not been caused by a cyber-security incident, though, Microsoft have confirmed.

Amongst the services impacted by the outage are emails and AI products.



Schools and business are amongst those to have been affected, with football clubs also facing issues.

Chelsea statement

Those include Chelsea, who have confirmed there have been disruptions to the club's email services.



However, the Blues' ticketing system currently remains unaffected, with fans still able to access to portal.

In a statement, Chelsea said: "Due to the worldwide Microsoft outage, we are currently experiencing disruption to our email services.



"We thank you for your patience and hope to be able to respond to all enquiries as soon as possible.

"Please note that our ticketing system is unaffected and supporters can continue to access it as normal."

It comes ahead of their women's fixture against Manchester City this weekend.

3 Ticket purchases for Chelsea Women's match against City are unaffected by the outage Credit: Getty



The two sides meet at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with kick-off at 1.30pm, live on talkSPORT 2.

City head to west London as league leaders, with the match marking a meeting of the top two in this season's Women's Super League.

Both sides remain unbeaten after nine matches, with the visitors just two points clear of their opponents.

A home win for Chelsea would see them leapfrog City into first place, though.



When do Chelsea play next?

As for the men's first-team, they do not return to Premier League action for over a week.

Due to the ongoing international break, Xabi Alonso's side's next match comes on Saturday, November 21 against Leeds United.

3 Alonso's side return to action against Leeds next weekend Credit: Getty

The Blues were held to a 2-2 draw in the fixture last season when the sides met in February.



However, they have since beaten Leeds in both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup, with the former coming in the semi-finals at Wembley Stadium.

Chelsea are currently fifth in the Premier League following their away defeat to Sunderland last weekend.

Sports.title: UFC chief Dana White opens up on 'crazy 48 hours' after Trump's bombshell press secretary plea
Sports.content:
UFC chief Dana White opens up on 'crazy 48 hours' after Trump's bombshell press secretary plea

UFC supremo Dana White has lifted the lid on his 'crazy 48 hours' after Donald Trump jokingly offered him the White House press secretary role over the weekend.

Trump sparked mayhem on Saturday afternoon after announcing on Truth Social that White had been offered the job of press secretary, pleading 'please take the job!'

White fueled rumors by sharing an AI-generated image of him standing behind the briefing room lectern, captioned 'On to the next chapter.'

He was then whisked over to Washington, following a boxing event in London, to be paraded in front of the White House press corps amid the chaos on Monday.

Trump later revealed that the offer was simply a joke, while White distanced himself from ever getting directly involved in politics, putting an end to the rumor mill.

Now, in the wake of his whirlwind weekend, the UFC chief has spoken out.

UFC supremo Dana White has lifted the lid on his 'crazy 48 hours' after Donald Trump jokingly offered him the White House press secretary role over the weekend

Trump invited the UFC boss to address the White House press corps on Monday afternoon

In an interview with FOX's Lara Trump that is set to air in full this weekend, White was asked how it felt to actually stand at the podium in front of the press corps.

He said: 'It was incredible. What an amazing experience. Literally when I was pulling in the gates of the White House, his assistant called and said, hey, we're going to take you right down to the press room, he wants you.

'I was like, what. This is crazy. It was a very unique and crazy 48 hours for me.'

Following on from that, White was asked whether he feared 'ending up in the crosshairs' of Democrats who said that they want to 'target the president' in the wake of their midterm win.

The UFC boss continued: 'Well, I mean, we kind of expected that. If you didn't do anything illegal or anything wrong, I don't know why you'd have to be worried.

'I've never done anything, you know, in the political world that would be illegal, where anybody should come after me or anything that we have to hide.

'So yeah. I expect it, but no, I'm not worried about it.'

Moments before his White House trip on Monday, White spoke with TMZ and revealed the real reason why his meeting with Trump had been arranged.

White admitted it was an 'incredible' experience to join Trump in the Press Briefing Room

Trump made the decision on Saturday to jokingly offer White the role of Press Secretary

White explained that trading card company Topps had created a 1-of-1 collectible commemorating the UFC Freedom 250 event held on the White House South Lawn.

'Me and the president wore patches that night for Freedom 250, and the cards are done so he's going to sign the card tonight. That's one of the reasons why I'm here,' White explained to TMZ.

When asked about the press secretary rumors, the fight promoter insisted he had nothing to do with the viral stunt and was completely caught off guard by the post.

'He put that out! The press secretary thing was him. Everyone has been blowing me up, asking me questions. I'm not going to be disrespectful and say anything. It's his thing!' White said.

Trump later clarified his shock job offer was simply a joke, but White revealed the president actually phoned him just moments after making the public declaration to give him a quick heads-up.

'Yeah, he called me,' White revealed, noting that he was already scheduled to travel to DC before the political rumor mill went completely into overdrive.

Sports.title: Egypt sack their manager for 'negative impact on team image' after he fainted when fight broke out between his TWO wives with punches and hair-pulling in a bar
Sports.content:
Egypt will begin their African Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches with a new manager after their previous head coach was sacked amid a torrid breakdown of both of his marriages. Hossam Hassan was handed his marching orders on Saturday after an incident in August which saw his two wives embroiled in a vicious fight, captured and shared on social media. Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel bar in the upscale Porto Marina resort on Egypt's north coast. El-Gharbawy and Mustafa were videoed arguing with Hassan in the middle attempting to cool tensions, but the duo came to blows, with punches thrown and hair pulled as screams filled the air. Such was the stress of the incident that Hassan is believed to have fainted as he tried to separate the two women. Horrified public onlookers watched as the physical fight grew with relatives of the trio getting involved, and security was called before Hassan was taken to hospital. En Égypte, un violent différend a éclaté entre... les deux femmes du sélectionneur égyptien, Hossam Hassan. 🇪🇬😳 Le conflit a dégénéré en échauffourée avec coups et tirage de cheveux, avant que des jeunes et des passages n'interviennent dans la bagarre. pic.twitter.com/pvRUSMtAsD — Instant Foot ⚽️ (@lnstantFoot) August 15, 2026 Egypt head coach Hossam Hassan was sacked this week after a fight broke out between his two wives Hassan's first wife Howaida El-Gharbawy and his second Dina 'Dan Adam' Mustafa started the argument while at a hotel in the upscale Porto Marina resort The 60-year-old is believed to have fainted while trying to separate the two women Both women are believed to have been left with cuts and bruises following the vicious scrap, while Hassan, despite briefly losing consciousness, was left unharmed. His lawyers later told Sky News Arabia, via the Sun, that he was not suffering a health crisis during the incident, and that he remained in good health. But in the days that followed, Hassan started proceedings to divorce El-Gharbawy, who he has been married to for decades. The couple also share three children. The 60-year-old has a further two children with second wife Mustafa, who Le Parisien alleges also filed for divorce in the days after the footage went viral on social media. The Egyptian Football Association ensured that Hassan's professional life took a similar nosedive, sharing in a statement that his dismissal was due in part to reputational damage the scandal might be doing to the national team. 'After analysing all the circumstances and events of the past few days, as well as their consequences and the negative impact they have had on the positive image and stability of our national team, the Board of Directors has decided, within the framework of its responsibilities, to dismiss coach Hossam Hassan and his entire technical staff and to end his tenure,' their statement read. Mustafa's lawyer Mohamed Shams gave an interview on Sky News Arabia claiming that his client had been the victim of a 'premeditated attack'. 'We hoped it wouldn't come to divorce, but things escalated to this level.' Hassan married his second wife in 2015, with Egyptian law allowing Muslim men to marry up to four women, providing that any wives have been formally informed that another marriage is to take place. The law mandates that the husband is also obligated to treat all of his wives equally with regard to housing, financial support and standard of living. Hassan had been married to his first wife El-Gharbawy for decades, with the pair sharing three of his five children Hassan and Mustafa briefly separated four years ago before recoupling before the spat that ended both of his marriages. As well as being relieved of his duties, Hassan was also sanctioned by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation, leaving him unable to publicly address the media following his sacking. Mohamed Salah and Co will now play their first qualifier of the international break against Malawi under new head coach Ali Maher. The former Liverpool star could be among those Pharaohs stars privately pleased with the departure of Hassan, after he was benched by his ex-manager for the last two international clashes. When asked why the superstar and national team captain had been left on the sidelines for the ties, Hassan had said: 'It is not right for a country of 120 million people for the national team to depend on one player.'
