Sports.title: Former England star Dele Alli in line for huge £8.3m payday after selling his image rights company
Sports.content:
Former England star Dele Alli in line for huge £8.3m payday after selling his image rights company

Former Tottenham star Dele Alli is set for a mammoth £8.3million payday as he plans to close down his image rights company, Dele Alli Promotions.

The now 30-year-old may be without a club but was not so foolish as to not prepare for life without a bumper contract, with his company boasting the sizeable sum in assets.

However, Alli will have to hand over £685,362 to the tax man - but this is a drop in the ocean in relation to the eyewatering £7.6million he is set to receive.

The former England international has been without a club for over 19 months, having last been in action for Cesc Fabregas' Como side in Serie A but only played one game, coming on as an 81st minute sub against AC Milan and receiving a red card just nine minutes later.

But Alli has several projects alongside Dele Alli Promotions keeping him busy while he is attempting to get back to full fitness and find a new club.

He owns and manages a private residential real estate holding company named Future Homes Investments, which owns and rents six properties worth more than £1.5million.

Dele Alli is looking at a very healthy payday after closing down his image rights company

The Englishman has played just ten minutes of professional football since February 2023

The Former Spurs man was forced to wear an Arsenal shirt on his Instagram story after losing a game of EAFC 27 to a fellow streamer

And his smallest company, Dele Investments still holds £336,267 in assets.

Most recently the former English international has branched out into livestreaming on Twitch with a skateboard, an array of expensive designer bags, and at least 48 pairs of shoes providing his backdrop.

He has already picked up traction on his channel by calling up old teammates such as Harry Kane, Eric Dier and Jack Grealish while live.

And while playing EAFC 27 with other steamers such as IShowSpeed, who recently forced Alli to wear an Arsenal shirt on Instagram after losing a wager to the 21-year-old American.

It is a far cry from his heady days as a player, when Dele twice picked up the PFA Young Player of the Year award and starred for England on their way to the semi-finals of the 2018 World Cup.

During an interview in 2023 on The Overlap, he opened up about his harrowing past, having to smoke and sell drugs as young as seven years old and being hung over a bridge by a man from neighbouring estate when he was just 11.

This resulted in the midfielder turning to sleeping pills and alcohol to suppress his feelings and help him through his trauma.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino breaks down in TEARS as he speaks out on 'most difficult decision' to leave US for Man United after agreeing to replace Michael Carrick at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss, and admitted that he couldn’t turn down the ‘dream’ job of Manchester United head coach.

United confirmed that Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half-year contract to replace Michael Carrick, and will start work on Wednesday after staying on for a double-header against Haiti.

Flanked by US Soccer Federation bosses at the team’s headquarters in Georgia, an emotional Pochettino wiped away tears as he thanked the players and staff.

‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears as he began his farewell as US national team boss

Pochettino spoke at a USMNT press conference after his move to Man United was confirmed

‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'

The 54-year-old Argentine revealed that United first made contact on Sunday after a 4-4 draw in Carrick’s final game left the club in the relegation zone.

United are paying US Soccer more than £10million in compensation to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, and have allowed him to stay in charge for two more matches.

‘I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League,’ said the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton boss, whose first game in charge of United will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.

‘All of this was so quick because we arrived here last Friday and on Sunday afternoon this type of situation started to appear. There was some contact. When things became bigger, they are very sensitive.

‘We were very transparent with the federation and they understand the situation. The decision between US Soccer and Man United to agree to continue for these two games will not change our commitment.

‘That decision was between the three parties but, of course if Man United agreed different terms, I need to respect that.’

Pochettino, who will oversee his side's Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti over the next week, insisted it was the 'most difficult decision' to leave the USMNT

Meanwhile, Carrick issued a statement following his sacking on Thursday after 10 months in charge.

Posting on social media, he said: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘I want to say a big thank-you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

‘That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.’

RELIVE our live blog with WILL PICKWORTH as Mauricio Pochettino spoke for the first time since taking the Manchester United job when he faced questions at a United States national team press conference on Friday.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp reveals he confronted Germany star over controversial crown celebration with links to 'anti-LGBTQ+ group' - and promises he won't repeat it
Sports.content:
Germany manager Jurgen Klopp insists midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a controversial goal celebration after opposition from supporters.

Nmecha, a Christian player for Borussia Dortmund, was criticised last weekend for celebrating scoring by lowering an imaginary crown from his head onto the pitch.

The celebration - called 'The King's Return' - was popularised by an evangelical network of footballers called Ballers in God, which counts prominent Premier League players among its members. It is supposed to represent the idea of submission to God.

But an investigation by German outlets found that the campaign website for 'The King's Return' linked to a chat service run by an organisation called Groundwire, where counsellors shared anti-homosexual views and described abortion as 'Satan's Plan'. Daily Mail Sport encountered similar views when consulting the service.

Nmecha has maintained that his message was one of love, but after a huge outcry in Germany - and talks with Klopp and national team sporting director Rudi Voller - he will not adopt the celebration again.

Klopp said: 'It was a big ⁠issue. I saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time. But then it all kicked off.

Felix Nmecha has vowed not to repeat his 'King's Return' celebration after a huge outcry

He was called into a meeting with Jurgen Klopp and Germany's sporting director Rudi Voller for the celebration which is connected with evangelical Christian group Ballers in God

'As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

'I have known Felix Nmecha for a few months, and I can say that he is a very friendly young man, who is warm and open, and always spreads positive energy when he is with us.

'I confronted him with all the things you might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.

'For me ⁠the most important issue was settled. Then I said "how do we do it with the goal ⁠celebration?" He will not be celebrating like that.'

A vocal section of Dortmund fans opposed the club signing Nmecha from Wolfsburg in 2023 after he had shared anti-homosexual and anti-transgender posts.

Ballers in God was founded in 2015 by former Tottenham midfielder John Bostock and brings together a wide range of Christian players from across the pyramid with weekly sessions.

While the organisation does not hold an explicit stance on LGBTQ+ issues, their Instagram account did celebrate the end of the Rainbow Laces campaign in the Premier League last year.

In response to the Nmecha story, they wrote: 'We are encouraged by player-led movements such as The King's Return, where footballers themselves take the initiative to express their faith in Jesus.

Klopp says Nmecha told him he 'loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone'

'Our desire is not only to share our hope, but to demonstrate love and respect towards everyone, including those who do not share our beliefs.

'Our focus has always been, and will always be, to point people to Jesus with grace and love.'

Nmecha said: 'My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.'

Back at Dortmund, Nmecha, 26, still faces scrutiny. A supporters' group claimed that his celebration clashed with club values and he has been reprimanded by senior figures.

The club's president, Hans-Joachim Watzke, said: 'The fan department has every right to start a discussion like this. I was at their annual general meeting on Monday. It was clear that those who were bothered by parts of his celebration were in a significant majority. So you have to take it seriously and discuss it.

'If he scores a goal and points his index fingers upwards, everyone knows he wants to thank God. He is also welcome to make the sign of the cross.

'But placing the crown on the grass - that is, of course, somewhat linked to Ballers in God. I don’t even want to judge it. When I look at what they stand for, Borussia Dortmund’s code of core values and Ballers in God’s fundamental outlook are not entirely compatible. We don’t want that in our living room.

'I told him: "Felix, if you sense that it is dividing the fans, perhaps you will also realise that you shouldn’t do it any more." He wants to think about it. We had a wonderful conversation with him. We had a one-hour video call. That is where we are now, and he will think about it. I hope we can find a sensible solution.

'I like Felix Nmecha very much. We have a very, very good relationship and speak frequently. As a practising Catholic, I am the last person who would want to forbid someone from praying. That is not what this is about at all. It is legitimate, too. The only question we are discussing with him is the second part of his celebration.'

Sports.title: Now the Daily Mail bans F1: We boycott coverage after our reporter is barred from races - as decision is branded 'an abuse of power'
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail will boycott Formula One after motor racing correspondent Jonathan McEvoy was handed a draconian ban for the rest of the season by the sport’s governing body.

There will be no reporting on races or press conferences for the final three races of the 2026 season in the wake of the remarkable decision to revoke our reporter’s accreditation over an article criticising Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc.

McEvoy labelled the Monegasque racer a ‘sneaky little b*****d’ for his role in a contentious, opening lap collision with Scuderia teammate, Britain’s seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, at last month’s Mexican Grand Prix. The incident cost Ferrari a chance of a race victory.

McEvoy, who has covered nearly 400 races across 21 years of working for the Daily Mail, went on to reveal details of a tense post-race debrief between the drivers and Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur.

The FIA’s decision to withdraw McEvoy’s accreditation has been condemned by news industry leaders. Top drivers, past and present, as well as a host of other leading figures in the sport, have also offered their private support.

Andrew Moger, chief executive of the News Media Coalition (NMC), called on the FIA to ‘reinstate McEvoy so he can continue to do his professional best and rejoin the dedicated group of experienced journalists who serve F1, fans and the business of motor racing through their independent reporting including opinion-forming insights’.

Jonathan McEvoy has been handed a draconian ban for the rest of the season by the sport’s governing body

The NMC champions journalist access to major organised news and sports events around the world and Moger said the McEvoy case was alarming.

‘Like it or not, freedom of expression such as the ability to share viewpoints, and press freedom, remain vital to informed societies, debate and conversation - including about the behaviour of F1 drivers and evidently the sensitivity of teams’.

The Society of Editors also threw its support behind the Daily Mail, calling on the FIA to reverse its decision with immediate effect.

Chief executive Dawn Alford said: ’The FIA was wrong to withdraw Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation. He has covered Formula One for more than 20 years. The point of an opinion column is to give readers the considered view of someone who knows the sport. He should be free to write what he thinks, even when that makes for uncomfortable reading in the paddock.

’Accreditation gives journalists the access they need to do their jobs. Using it to punish a correspondent for what he writes is an abuse of that power. It sets a precedent that should concern every journalist covering Formula One and anyone who cares about independent sports reporting.

’Formula One fans want to know what is really going on in the sport. They rely on experienced reporters to ask awkward questions and tell them plainly what they make of the answers. That coverage suffers if journalists have to think about whether their next column might cost them their pass.

‘The FIA should reverse this decision immediately and reinstate Jonathan McEvoy’s accreditation in time for the next race.’

The Daily Telegraph described the ban as ‘the latest example of the FIA’s thin-skinned and overzealous policing of the media’.

In a stinging rebuke, McEvoy suggested Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur may be behind the decision

McEvoy, pictured with George Russell, has covered nearly 400 races in 21 years working for the Daily Mail

On Thursday, FIA general manager Alberto Villarreal wrote to McEvoy to inform him of the impending ban. The letter stated: ’The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship.

‘Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.’

The decision was labelled as ‘crazy’ by former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone, who added: ’I don’t know why the FIA would ever do that.

’Apart from the fact I like Jon, he is doing a fantastic job.

‘I look forward to reading what he’s writing. I don’t have to, it’s my choice to do that. I think it’s completely mad.’

Chris Dean, the Daily Mail’s head of sport, echoed those feelings in a strongly worded statement on Thursday.

He said: ’This is an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the Press.

’We are in dangerous territory when the FIA react in such a heavy-handed way to some mild and fair criticism of one driver.

’Jonathan McEvoy is a fearless and first-rate journalist who takes readers behind the curtain of F1’s shiny exterior. The FIA should reinstate his accreditation immediately.'

The FIA’s latest attack on press freedom comes after an incident at the Japanese Grand Prix in March involving Max Verstappen and the Guardian journalist Giles Richards.

The Dutchman refused to participate in a press conference until the reporter had left the room.

It came after the final race of the 2025 season in Abu Dhabi, when Richards quizzed Verstappen on whether he regretted his driving after a collision with title rival George Russell in an earlier race.

The incident cost Verstappen nine points and he went on to lose out in his quest for a fifth consecutive title to Lando Norris by two points.

Sports.title: Fighter who ambushed UFC star in bloody hotel brawl is punished: Abu Dhabi court dishes out six-month prison sentences and fines - including £61k for filming shocking attack
Sports.content:
Usman Nurmagomedov and his entourage have been swiftly punished with prison sentences and fines in Abu Dhabi after their shocking hotel attack.

Nurmagomedov set upon UFC star Merab Dvalishvili on Wednesday, slapping him in the lobby of Yas Hilton hotel in a revenge mission filmed by his friends.

The Georgian-American Dvalishvili then retaliated and fought back with his cameraman as the melee rapidly descended into complete mayhem. Dvalishvili was left bloodied and bruised and the attackers were quickly detained by the authorities.

In just two days, their punishments have been decided by the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, who published the findings on social media.

Six of the attackers were given six-month prison sentences and ordered to pay £61,000 each in fines. They will also be immediately deported when their sentences end.

They were described as having 'caused panic, disturbed public security and endangered lives'.

Two of Nurmagomedov's associates were fined £10,000 each for 'disturbing public security and assaulting others'.

Usman Nurmagomedov (left) was the one who initiated the brawl by slapping Merab Dvalishvili - his brother Umar (right) lost a title shot against the Georgian last year

The Abu Dhabi court shared this post online confirming the punishments for the attackers

And the other two members of the group who recorded the assault were given six-month sentences, £61,000 fines and confiscation of the devices used.

They were punished 'for violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl'.

Dvalishvili had been due to fight in a RAF wrestling event on Saturday. CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein released a statement confirming the fighter is back.

He said: 'I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support.

'We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us.'

Nurmagomedov and his team's violent ambush was four months in the making.

Back in July, Dvalishvili was competing in a RAF event in Georgia, which is a freestyle wrestling show the UFC allow their fighters to compete in outside of the day job.

While milling around at the event, a Dagestani wrestler and friend of Umar, Ahmed Gadzhimagomedov, confronted Dvalishvili about refusing to entertain a rematch of any kind with Umar.

UFC star Merab Dvalishvili was attacked in a five-star hotel in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday

'I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody (Gadzhimagomedov) came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand,' Dvalishvili told Ariel Helwani.

'And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realize, "Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him?"

'It’s between me and Umar… I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads.'

After Gadzhimagomedov squared up to him, Dvalishvili shoved him in the neck, shouting: 'What's your problem, b***h!'

The situation, unlike the hotel brawl that escalated into a complete bloodbath, was quickly defused and there was a child in close proximity.

Usman wanted to take revenge on behalf of fellow Dagestani Gadzhimagomedov and also his brother Umar, who lost against Dvalishvili in a title shot last year.

In the footage of the hotel attack, the group appeared to approach Dvalishvili, 35, from behind, before one man said a couple of words to him and slapped him in the face.

Dvalishvili was rocked, then kicked, and was held back by a man he appeared to be with.

He tried to fight back but a number of men overwhelmed him as his companion was attacked too. Eventually, the groups were separated, and Dvalishvili took to social media to respond to the incident.

The 35-year-old was blind sided while carrying out an interview

He said in a video, bloody and bruised as he received treatment: 'What a sneaky way guys. Just two of us, me and my friend, came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters are you guys? What kind of man does this? If you want to fight, let's do it the real way.

'You guys came when there was two of us, you were prepared. What the f***.'

His companion then added: 'From behind? You call yourselves men? You're a little b***h.'

Dvalishvili continued: 'You are sneaky guys. You are not real men. It shows your guys' character, what the f*** guys? If you want to fight, let's fight. We are fighters. I talk straight, but you guys came from behind. I don't know how many guys, all your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way, wow.

'I knew guys, I knew what kind of guys you were. Usman, Umar and his friends came sneaky from behind, so many guys. Wow. I am fine guys. All my friends and family, I am f***ing fine. I am a fighter. This is nothing for me, but it shows what kind of people you guys are. P***ys do this bro. We are warriors.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane reads letters from his kids: England captain close to tears as his four children write to him after he broke the Three Lions appearance record
Sports.content:
Harry Kane had to compose himself and hold back the tears while reading beautiful letters from his children after breaking the England appearance record.

The 33-year-old earned his 126th cap and scored in the 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday night, with the Wembley crowd celebrating his achievement and Ballon d'Or triumph.

And on the following morning, there was a surprise in store for the England skipper, who was visibly taken aback on camera when presented with letters from his four children, nine-year-old Ivy, eight-year-old Vivi, five-year-old Louis and three-year-old Henry, who he shares with wife Kate.

'Wow, that’s uh a bit of a surprise,' Kane said as he examined the letters and artwork. 'I think you guys are trying to make me cry on camera.'

He opened the first one before reading aloud: 'To Daddy, I love you very much and I want you to know that I’m very proud of you and also you are the best footballer in the world, the most kind Daddy in the world and the best striker in the world.

'I would like to celebrate you playing the most games for England by holiday together and eating ice cream.

Harry Kane was on the verge of tears as he read touching letters from his four children

'My favorite thing about you is you never give up and I love all things you do for us. Love Ivy.'

Dewy-eyed Kane then reflected: 'I wasn’t expecting this beautiful letter. Thank you Ivy. I love you. I've got one here from Vivian as well.'

'Dear Daddy, I’m so happy and proud of you. I love you because you are hard working and make the best fried eggs. I want to celebrate with you by going fishing, going down the water slides and having a cinema trip as well. Love from Vivi.'

Kane then said: 'Yeah, you’ve caught me by surprise here to be honest with you. I’m trying to just uh, stay strong for the camera. Thank you Vivi, love you.'

Then came the letters from Kane's two sons, Louis and Henry.

Louis' read: 'To Daddy, I love you so much because you train and work so hard. My favorite thing we do together is play football and cricket together. I love when you play England football because you score goals and we get to sing Vindaloo. I want to celebrate with you by making an ice cream house with sweets inside. Love Louis.'

'Thank you Louie, love you, boy. This last one is from Henry,' Kane said.

The short and sweet note from his youngest went: 'Daddy, you are the winner. Vindaloo! Love Henry.'

Kane walked onto the pitch with his children, (L-R) Henry, Ivy, Vivi, Louis on Thursday night

Kane showed the artwork and hand-written letters to the camera as he read them

Kane then pointed the endearing scribble to the camera, saying: 'He’s drawn me a lovely picture there. Love you, Henry. Thank you, beautiful messages from my wonderful family.'

Kane, who lives with his family in Bavaria and recently signed a new deal worth £400,000-a-week at Bayern Munich, brought the whole clan, including his parents, to Wembley for his big night on Thursday.

He walked out onto the hallowed turf with his four children, admired a gigantic tifo of himself in the crowd, posed for pictures with the gleaming Ballon d'Or trophy and was given a commemorative shirt by Prince William.

Kane is a devoted family man in addition to being the world's best footballer and took a moment to say a few words about his children at the Ballon d'Or ceremony last month.

He said: 'To Ivy, Vivienne, Louis and Henry. You're the reason I do this.

Prince William presented Kane with a commemorative framed shirt with 126 on the back

'I don't think you'll fully maybe appreciate bringing this trophy home. I'll bring a few others home, but this one is a special one, so I can't wait to see you and celebrate with you.

'I want to set a good example being a father but also being a professional and what it means to work hard, what it means to believe in yourself. I love you very much.'

Kane passed Peter Shilton as the record appearance-maker for England on Thursday and took his tally of goals for the national team to 92.

His penalty put England 2-1 up and they would not relinquish their lead. He'll next be in action against Spain on Sunday.

Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears and sobbed during a US Soccer press conference

Mauricio Pochettino has now been confirmed as the manager of Manchester United after the club parted ways with Michael Carrick

Mauricio Pochettino has been announced as the new Manchester United head coach. He will become the fourth permanent boss since Sir Jim Ratcliffe purchased his minority stake in the club in 2024 on 18 November.

Pochettino replaces Michael Carrick, who was sacked only a matter of months after being promoted from interim manager to permanent head coach. United took a long time to make their decision on Carrick. Still, after not being convinced by other candidates such as Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte, they have decided Pochettino is their choice.

The Argentine still has two matches to fulfil as head coach of the United States - a two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti - but after that, he will be in charge when United face Liverpool at Anfield after the international break.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s wife dragged into relegation sacrifice as couple went to extreme lengths
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s wife dragged into relegation sacrifice as couple went to extreme lengths

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United when the Premier League returns, with the club currently in the bottom three of the table

View 2 Images New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is not afraid to go to extreme lengths in a relegation fight. (Image: Tiziana FABI / AFP via Getty Images)

New Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, alongside his wife, have proven that he already has the head for a relegation fight, and is willing to go to extreme lengths to ensure his team survives. The Argentine has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract at Old Trafford, replacing Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



His first game in charge is on 22 November when United travel to take on rivals Liverpool. They go into the Premier League game in the relegation places, with some sensationally claiming they could be in for a fight to beat the drop this season.

‌



While the team will hope to be nowhere near the same position at the end of the season, nothing can be ruled out, given that United have recorded fewer wins than any other team in the league so far. The good news is that a relegation scrap is something Pochettino and his wife have experience with.

‌



Marcus Rashford causes issue as Man Utd set to trigger his team-mate's contract clause READ MORE :

In January 2009, Pochettino took charge of struggling Spanish side Espanyol. With just 10 weeks of the season left, the team were bottom of La Liga, eight points from safety.

It was widely believed that it would take a miracle for the team to escape the drop. So that’s what Pochettino searched for.

As reported by The Guardian at the time, Pochettino, his wife and his assistant manager packed their bags and hiked 12km to Montserrat. It was a pilgrimage to the religious mountain, which is slightly bigger than Mount Snowdon.

‌



View 2 Images Pochettino started his managerial career with Espanyol. (Image: MANUEL QUEIMADELOS/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



It is also home to the black virgin shrine, which was rescued from looting during the Spanish Civil War. Pochettino is said to have pleaded with the shrine to help his side pull off a miracle and survive relegation.

In their last 10 games of the season, Espanyol produced an incredible turnaround to haul themselves out of the relegation places. They won eight of those games, losing just once to Atletico Madrid, and drawing another.

‌



A 3-0 win over Malaga on the final day of the season saw them secure a 10th-place finish in La Liga. It is known as one of the great escapes in La Liga history and launched Pochettino’s managerial career.

The 54-year-old remained with the club until November 2012. He then made the move to the Premier League with Southampton three months later.

Article continues below

A successful five-and-a-half years with Tottenham was followed by spells with Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Most recently, he managed the USA national side and will take charge of his final two games over the international break before arriving at United.

Sports.title: Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison for Merab Dvalishvili attack
Sports.content:
Usman Nurmagomedov sentenced to six months in prison for Merab Dvalishvili attack

GRAPHIC CONTENT - Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face after he was attacked by Usman Nurmagomedov on Wednesday

View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili was slapped by Usman Nurmagomedov (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

Eight people have been sentenced to prison following Usman Nurmagomedov's attack on Merab Dvalishvili, according to reports.

‌



‌



On Wednesday, former UFC bantamweight champion Dvalishvili was left with a bloodied face falling a brawl with Nurmagomedov and his crew in at the Yas Hilton on Wednesday. The Georgian star was conducting an interview ahead of Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi - where he is due to face Marlon Moraes in a wrestling bout - when Nurmagomedov and a group of friends approached him from behind.

‌



A short exchange of words occurred before Nurmagomedov slapped Dvalishvili in the face, sparking an all-out brawl between the two sets of camps. Dvalishvili and his friend Saba Lazishvili were left severely injured following the physical altercation.

‌



On Friday morning, local reports stated that Nurmagomedov and his five associates were sentenced to six months in prison, slapped with a hefty 300,000 AED fine, and face deportation over the Abu Dhabi hotel attack.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

The two people who filmed the brawl were also sentenced to six months in prison along with a 300,000 AED fine, and order to be deported after serving the sentence for "violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl." Two others have also been fined for disturbing public security and assaulting others - ordered to pay 50,000 AED, but avoided jail time. Dvalishvili and Lazishvili were each fined 50,000 AED.

‌



Wrestling promotion RAF revealed on Friday that Dvalishvili has since been released from custody. Nurmagomedov was not due to feature on the RAF card over in Abu Dhabi, but was merely in attendance to support his older brother, Umar, who is expected to face UFC icon Urijah Faber.

On Friday, RAF CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein issued the following statement: “I am pleased to share that Merab Dvalishvili is back with us in Abu Dhabi. We would like to express our sincere appreciation to the relevant authorities in Abu Dhabi for their professionalism and support. We remain focused on moving forward and are pleased to have Merab back with us."

‌



Conor McGregor clears up retirement confusion ahead of final fight READ MORE :

Conor Benn told Conor McGregor fight would not last long READ MORE :

UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev, who trains with Nurmagomedov, was eager to break his silence and share his side of the story. “To those who are now condemning Usman and the guys, [and] they are writing insults to them, why were you silent when Merab hit a Dagestani wrestler for nothing and hurt his honor?” Makhachev wrote. “The man approached him to talk without malice. Merab started what happened today in his homeland by allowing himself to hit a guest and insulting his mother.”

Dvalishvili was quick to upload a statement to social media following the brawl. He wrote: "Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me - They kept kicking us when we were down like losers."

‌



WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT

4 View 4 Images The brawl broke out in a hotel lobby (Image: @ChampRDS/X) 4 View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili was left with a bloody face (Image: Instagram)

‌



The accompanying footage showed the Georgian bloody faced and receiving medical treatment, as he ranted: "What a sneaky way guys? Just two of us, me and my friend came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman Nurmagomedov and his friends came like snakes from behind. What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this, bro? If you want to talk fight, let's do it the real way, bro. You guys came from...There's just two of us and you guys were prepared, bro. What the f***?"

Dvalishvili then added: "We bleed, we fight, we war, but you guys are just sneaky guys, bro. You guys are not real men. That shows your guys' character, shows you guys aren't real men.

‌



"What the f*** guys? If you want to fight, fight. Let's f***ing fight. We are fighters, bro. I talk. I'm a real guy, I talk straight. But you guys came from behind bro. I don't know how many guys you was. All of your friends waiting for us in a sneaky way. Wow. I knew what kind of guys you are. I just came here in Abu Dhabi and Usman, Umar (Nurmagomedov's brother) and his friends came from behind and tried to beat us. So many guys. I'm fine guys. All my friends and family, I'm f***ing fine."

View 4 Images Merab Dvalishvili is supposed to wrestle on Saturday evening (Image: @ChampRDS/X)

‌



Dvalishvili has a long history with the Nurmagomedovs. Last year, the 35-year-old defeated Umar at UFC 311 by unanimous decision to defend the UFC bantamweight title. The rivalry ramped up even further a few months ago after Dvalishvili slapped Umar's friend, Akhmed Gadzhimagomedov, backstage after RAF Georgia. Dvalishvili, who had beaten Henry Cejudo in a freestyle wrestling match that evening, had shut down talks of a bout between himself and Umar.

Gadzhimagomedov then approached him to confront him about his comments, with Dvalishvili responding by slapping the Dagestani - leading to a similar scrap between camps. Speaking with Ariel Helwani, Dvalishvili explained his reasoning for the slap.

Article continues below

He said: "I was super relaxed, super chilled and then somebody came and grabbed my neck and pulled me over and started yelling at me in Russian language, which I hardly understand. And he mentioned Umar. It took me a couple of seconds to realise, 'Who is this guy to tell me what to talk about him? It's between me and Umar.' I have so much respect for all Dagestani people, especially fighters. The only guy who I don't like from Dagestan is Umar and his sneaky manager, Rizvan [Magomedov]. The guy who was helping Umar disrespect me on X and Threads."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino bursts into tears in first interview after getting Man Utd job

Mauricio Pochettino was announced as Manchester United's new manager on Friday, with the outgoing USMNT boss explained the decision in an emotional press conference hours later

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino became emotional during his press conference ahead of the USMNT's game against Haiti

Mauricio Pochettino was in tears during his first press conference since being unveiled as Manchester United's new head coach as he expressed how difficult it is to leave his role with the United States men's national team.

‌



‌



United confirmed that the 54-year-old had agreed to succeed Michael Carrick at Old Trafford on Friday afternoon, just hours before Pochettino was scheduled to address the United States media in a press conference ahead of their upcoming game against Haiti.

‌



Pochettino cut an emotional figure as he addressed his departure and spoke through tears before taking a moment to compose himself.

‌



He said: “A decision that in some part is a very sad decision and in another part that we are professional and are trying to find the next step, try to make your dreams come true and I think the most important thing is what we leave here. The moment that we shared together, all the things that we accomplished and put in place and the standard that we increase in that foundation.”

‌



Pochettino swiftly emerged as the leading candidate to replace Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday after overseeing just one win from 10 Premier League games this season.

Reports outlining that Pochettino and United were close to an agreement were rife prior to Carrick being officially removed from his post and the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager shed some light on the process, which includes an agreement that Pochettino will oversee the double-header against Haiti before starting his new role on November 18.

‌



“We were very transparent,” he said. “ We were talking with the federation. Yesterday when things were positive in the way that the agreement was, we had a meeting and I communicated to the player and the whole staff.

“ I think we will have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. Now I think it is better to talk about USA soccer and the national team. We have two games ahead and the focus is completely on this.”

Pochettino has agreed a two-and-a-half year contract to take charge at United, who came close to hiring him twice in the past.

Though Pochettino has made no secret of his desire for a Premier League return, he signed a contract extension with the USMNT until 2030 after guiding them to the last 16 of a home World Cup in the summer.

Asked why he signed an extension if he craved a return to Europe, Pochettino replied: “I think it's obvious, I never said that I wanted to go back. They know that there is not too many opportunities can happen in your career like the size of Manchester United. When that arrives it is difficult to turn down that situation.”

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's first job must be getting rid of Bruno Fernandes - he's trouble at Man Utd

If Mauricio Pochettino wants to succeed at Manchester United, he needs to be bold and kick troublemaker Bruno Fernandes to the curb

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino has a big Bruno Fernandes problem (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

When Mauricio Pochettino walks through the doors at Manchester United, his to-do list will stretch from Stretford all the way to Buenos Aires. But his first, most urgent task shouldn't require much deliberation.

‌



‌



He needs to call Bruno Fernandes into his office, shake his hand, and tell him to pack his bags for January.

‌



News that Fernandes has turned his nose up at United's latest contract offer this week has sparked an understandable flutter of anxiety within Old Trafford's leaking corridors. With his current deal expiring at the end of the season, albeit with a one-year extension option sitting in United's back pocket, the conventional wisdom says Pochettino must move heaven and earth to keep his captain sweet.

‌



But conventional wisdom at Manchester United has been dead wrong for over a decade. Fernandes isn't the solution to the club's malaise - he's one of its primary carriers.

Mauricio Pochettino's wife had brutal four word reaction after press conference READ MORE :

When will Mauricio Pochettino first take charge of Man Utd and his likely starting XI? READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Of course, the standard defence of the 32-year-old is always the same: Look at his goals and assists. This is the great Fernandes illusion - the soothing myth that because the numbers on his Wikipedia page look healthy, he must be some sort of lone genius propping up a crumbling empire. Take five minutes to actually watch him, though, and the whole thing unravels like a cheap suit.

‌



Strip away the penalty kicks - harvested with that little theatrical hop once the hard work has already been done - and the corners dutifully aimed at Casemiro's forehead, and what are you actually left with? A midfielder who pads his stats when the pressure is off, when the points are already in the bag, or when the stakes couldn't flatter him more.

For nearly seven years, Fernandes' gaudy chance-creation statistics have served as a convenient smokescreen, disguising a fair-weather talisman in a midfield that cannot keep the ball, control the tempo, or hold its shape against halfway-competent opposition.

‌



Worse still, when the roof is caving in, and United desperately need someone to grab a massive fixture by the scruff of the neck and twist it to his will, Fernandes simply evaporates. He doesn't boss big games - he merely attends them as an outraged spectator, hovering on the peripheries like a man furiously disputing an erroneous restaurant bill.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes behaviour on and off the pitch has sparked plenty of debate (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Another giant fly in the ointment is how wildly unsuited he is to the tactical regime about to arrive. Pochettino's entire managerial philosophy is built on relentless, lungs-on-fire pressing, synchronised sprinting, and ego-free collective graft. Asking Bruno Fernandes to function inside that kind of disciplined, high-velocity machine is like asking a grumpy cat to enjoy a bubble bath. He can't do it, and - most exhausting of all - he will spend 90 minutes moaning about being asked to try.

And that, really, is the rotting core of the whole enterprise. For all his padded goal contributions, Fernandes is a roaring net negative because of the thick atmospheric poison he pumps into the club. The signature arm-flapping, the theatrical scowls, the slumped shoulders of a wounded martyr. It isn't passion. It's performative con-artistry of the highest order.

‌



Every time Fernandes throws his hands to the heavens after a misplaced pass, he is cynically beaming a coded message to the Stretford End: Look at me. I'm the only one trying. These clowns around me are letting us all down. It's sneaky, deeply self-serving, and faintly villainous. While his team-mates absorb the brickbats raining down from the stands, the skipper stages a one-man pantomime of aggrieved perfection to keep his own halo polished.

We saw the mask slip entirely during his shabby little meltdown with Michael Carrick. Hooked off against Como after a poor performance, Fernandes didn't swallow his pride and take his seat on the bench like a grown-up. He threw his manager straight under the bus, openly slating Carrick's tactics in public with all the petulance of a toddler spitting out lukewarm broccoli.

‌



There was a nauseating whiff of late-stage Cristiano Ronaldo about the whole episode: Look at how I have suffered. I am the most important person in this building, so to hell with the manager, the squad, and the badge.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes could cause Mauricio Pochettino a big headache (Image: Omar Vega, Getty Images)

‌



And this, remember, is the man wearing the captain's armband at Manchester United. A club that has spent over a decade drowning in an excuse-making, accountability-free dressing room culture is being led by a chief whinger who actively models the exact behaviour that has ruined them. Instead of whipping slackers into shape, Fernandes legitimises sulking as a leadership style.

Pochettino's greatest trick as a manager has always been alchemy - welding a group of fresh, hungry players into a tight-knit unit where everyone pulls in the exact same direction. Keeping Fernandes around makes that impossible. You cannot build a church while the bell-ringer is setting fire to the pews.

‌



Fortunately, this contract standoff hands United and Pochettino a gift-wrapped escape hatch. With his current deal expiring in June, the temptation among the bean-counters might be to trigger that one-year extension option just to protect his transfer value.

But United must resist the urge. Extending his deal only drags out the soap opera, keeps his gargantuan wages on the books, and chains Pochettino to a mutinous skipper for another 18 months. It would be a triumph of accountancy over common sense.

‌



Instead, they must be ruthless. Stick him in the shop window and sell him in January while someone, perhaps in Saudi Arabia, is still willing to pay good money for him. Rip the armband off, hand it to someone whose first instinct in a crisis isn't to throw a strop, and let Pochettino stamp his authority on the place from day one.

United won't miss Fernandes half as much as the G/A fetishists and YouTube highlight-reel fans will claim. Football isn't played on paper or in Excel columns, and matches aren't won with hollow individual statistics.

Article continues below

Manchester United have spent far too long mistaking a noisy soloist for an orchestra. If Pochettino is to get this broken ensemble playing in harmony, his very first act must be to politely, but firmly, escort the soloist off stage.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first two January signings picked as Man Utd 'begin talks'
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's first two January signings picked as Man Utd 'begin talks'

Mauricio Pochettino has been announced as the next manager of Manchester United and he is reportedly targeting two new signings already

View 3 Images Head coach of the United States Mauricio Pochettino attends a training session one day ahead of an international friendly match against Canada at Allianz Field (Image: Getty)

Mauricio Pochettino has been formally confirmed as Manchester United manager and he's already reported to be considering January transfers. According to reports, the Argentine boss is planning a swoop for two players he's already well acquainted with.

‌



‌



Pochettino will succeed the departed Michael Carrick, whose troubled spell as United manager concluded on Thursday. United went into the November international break languishing in the relegation zone, having claimed victory in just one of their first 10 fixtures in the Premier League.

‌



In all competitions, Carrick's statistics weren't significantly better, with the club having secured a further two victories in the Champions League. A shift was required, and following a protracted procedure, INEOS ultimately dismissed Carrick.

‌



Before Carrick's exit was announced, the United hierarchy were understood to be progressing a deal for Pochettino behind the scenes. On Friday afternoon, Pochettino's hiring was made official. And with the January transfer window fast approaching, it's suggested he is already examining possible recruits.

Mauricio Pochettino faces immediate Man Utd problem already setting him up for failure READ MORE :

According to TeamTALK, two names that have already emerged are players Pochettino knows from his USMNT spell: Alex Freeman and Folarin Balogun.

View 3 Images (Image: GEOFFROY VAN DER HASSELT, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Regarding Balogun, it is understood that his representatives have informed United of the goal-hungry forward's desire to explore a potential transfer.

Balogun, who found himself at the centre of a contentious red card controversy during the recent World Cup, was caught up in an unsuccessful move to Everton this summer - a switch the player himself was far from enthusiastic about.

‌



The 25-year-old is now thought to be receptive to joining United, in part due to the prospect of linking up once more with manager Pochettino.

Meanwhile, the full-back position has been a persistent concern for United throughout the season, prompting interest in Villarreal defender Alex Freeman.

‌



Pochettino highly regards the 22-year-old and has firmly established himself as a key figure in the USA's starting line-up. He is versatile and can play at right-back or centre-back.

View 3 Images (Image: Europa Press Sports, Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



Before any of that, however, Pochettino will need to focus on getting the very best from the players already at his disposal. That challenge begins at Anfield following the international break, where United face fierce rivals Liverpool, before subsequent fixtures against Brentford and Sporting.

Speaking to Sky Sports News, United icon Gary Neville has backed Pochettino to succeed. He said: "I've always wanted Mauricio Pochettino as the manager at United.

Article continues below

"I've said it numerous times that I wanted him. I think he's a brilliant person. I think he understands the size of the club. He's just got to come in here and protect himself against actually the people that he's working with."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino named as new Man Utd boss with start date confirmed before Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has been formally announced as the next head coach of Manchester United, who have confirmed the outgoing United States men's national team boss will be in position to oversee their trip to Liverpool next Sunday.

Pochettino, 54, was swiftly identified as the preferred candidate to succeed United legend Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday. Carrick was axed after overseeing just one win from United's 10 Premier League games so far this season, a run which has seen them drop into the relegation zone.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager will oversee the USMNT's two fixtures against Haiti, the first of which is on Saturday, before officially starting his new role after signing a two-and-a-half year contract.

A statement confirming the news read: "Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

"The club has reached an agreement with the U.S. Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the U.S. Men’s National Team."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

United, who go on to reiterate Pochettino's reputation for adopting a "high-intensity, attacking style of football", have courted the Argentine previously and were close to making a move for him during his time at Tottenham before pivoting to Jose Mourinho.

Pochettino was also considered for the Old Trafford vacancy in 2022 following Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's departure; United instead chose to pursue a move for the then Ajax manager, Erik ten Hag.

Pochettino inherits a team low on confidence following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign.

Memories of Carrick engineering a third-placed finish after replacing Ruben Amorim in an interim capacity have evaporated, though there has been widespread sympathy for Carrick over the manner of his departure, with United's work to line up Pochettino as his successor largely played out in public before official confirmation of his own fate.

View 2 Images Pochettino will start work at United next week after overseeing two final USMNT games (Image: AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

A Manchester United statement confirming Carrick had been relieved of his duties read: "Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

"Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered."
