Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

In the second, victims from places such as Turbo, a town in Antioquia, and from Medellín were lured to Dabeiba and killed. In the third, bodies were hidden in municipal cemeteries, including Las Mercedes in Dabeiba and one in Ituango, another Antioquia town.

What the Sentence Requires

The five must live under restrictions on their freedom while they carry out nine restorative projects in Antioquia, Semana reported. The projects include rebuilding roads and bridges, humanitarian demining, memory work, searching for missing people and farm projects.

Martínez Vargas said the sanction “is not impunity” but the heart of the transitional-justice model born of the peace agreement, in Semana’s account (our translation). Their cooperation helped recover 77 bodies at Las Mercedes cemetery, and 18 have been identified.

What It Means for You

This is a human-rights ruling, not a market event, and it shows how the peace deal’s court punishes soldiers who confess: with supervised work for victims rather than jail. El Tiempo, a Bogotá daily, put the longest sanction at up to six and a half years.

Our earlier reports track the same court’s other cases. They include charges against 12 former officers over a Medellín operation and sanctions on seven former FARC leaders.

What Is Not Known

Colombian outlets call this the JEP’s third sentence, but El Espectador’s own text calls it the second restorative one, so we do not number it. We could not open the court’s own statement, and the sources we reviewed do not say whether the ruling can be appealed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who did Colombia’s peace court sentence on 13 November?

Five former army members found responsible for 18 criminal events with 35 victims in Dabeiba, Antioquia. All five had confessed to the court.

Will the five go to prison?

No. They receive restorative sentences of about five and a half to six and a half years, with restrictions on their freedom while they work on projects for victims.

What are “false positives” in Colombia?

Killings of civilians by soldiers who then presented the victims as guerrillas killed in combat. In El Espectador’s account, Magistrate Juan Ramón Martínez Vargas said the killers picked victims they thought no one would search for.

What did the cooperation help uncover?

They helped recover 77 victims’ bodies at Las Mercedes cemetery in Dabeiba. Eighteen of them have been identified.

World.title: Chile Deputies Send 2027 Budget to Senate
World.content:
Chile’s National Congress in Valparaíso, where the budget is debated. Photo: Carlos Figueroa Rojas, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

CHILE · BUDGET

Chile’s lower house finished voting on the 2027 national budget in the early hours of Friday 13 November 2026 and sent it to the Senate. The marathon session ran past midnight, and at least six ministry sections fell, several of them on tied or one-vote results.

For a US reader the clock matters more than any single line: Congress must pass a budget by Sunday 29 November, or the government’s original text becomes law. That sets up a short Senate fight over mining, education and interior funds.

Key Facts What Chile’s Chamber of Deputies finished voting the 2027 budget bill early Friday 13 November and sent it to the Senate.

Rejected At least six sections failed: Interior, Education, Mining, Government Secretariat, Women and Culture.

Security Public Security gets about 3.49 trillion pesos (about US$3.5 billion), 7% more than in 2026.

Deadline Congress must finish by Sunday 29 November, or the government’s original text applies.

Next The government can try to restore rejected funds in the Senate; any change returns to the Chamber.

Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 62.9 points (November 2026 edition).

What the Chamber of Deputies Decided

The Chamber of Deputies, Chile’s lower house, completed the vote before dawn on Friday, according to Pauta, a Chilean news site (13 November 2026). Deputies approved the Health section by 82 votes to 41 and restored money for the day-to-day costs of primary care.

The Public Security section, which funds the Carabineros national police, the investigative police and the prison service Gendarmería, comes to about 3.49 trillion pesos (about US$3.5 billion at about 995 pesos per dollar, in line with the 12 November close). That is 7% more than in 2026, and it includes Gendarmería for the first time because the prison service moved from the Justice Ministry.

Deputies also voted to raise funding for the Ricarte Soto Law, which pays for very costly diagnoses and treatments. The government filed a constitutional reservation, a formal objection, against that change.

Which Budgets Failed, and Why It Matters

At least six sections were rejected: Interior, Education, Mining, the Government Secretariat (the government spokesperson’s ministry), Women and Gender Equity, and Culture. Interior, Education and Mining fell after tied votes, while Women and Culture each lost by a single vote.

A rejected section is not deleted: it goes to the Senate, where the government can try to restore the money. Mining’s spending is the line US copper investors will watch, because Chile is the world’s largest copper producer, and we reported the Chamber’s general approval vote of 80 to 63 on 9 November.

What Happens Next in the Senate

The constitution gives Congress 60 days from filing to pass the budget, and this bill was filed on 30 September. DIPRES, Chile’s budget office, confirms that the president’s original text takes effect if Congress misses that limit, which falls on Sunday 29 November.

If the Senate approves changes, they must go back to the Chamber of Deputies, Pauta reported. The Chamber also rejected the article that lets the government borrow up to US$25 billion, El Periodista, a Chilean news site, reported, and the Senate can restore it too.

What It Means for You

For an investor or business with Chilean exposure, nothing is settled: the rejected lines can still be restored, and the final figures will come from the Senate and, if needed, a joint Chamber-Senate committee. The first Senate votes on Mining and Education will show how much of the Chamber’s pushback survives.

What Is Not Known

We could not confirm how the Senate will treat the rejected sections or whether the government will file amendments to restore them. The date of the Senate’s first vote on the bill was not confirmed in the sources we could open.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Chile’s Chamber of Deputies decide on 13 November?

It finished voting the 2027 budget bill in the early hours and sent it to the Senate. At least six ministry sections were rejected along the way.

Which budget sections were rejected?

Interior, Education, Mining, the Government Secretariat, Women and Gender Equity, and Culture. Interior, Education and Mining fell on tied votes.

When must Chile’s Congress pass the budget?

Within 60 days of filing. The bill was filed on 30 September, so the limit is Sunday 29 November, after which the president’s original text applies.

Does the rejection of a section cut that ministry’s money?

Not yet. The section moves to the Senate, where the government can try to restore the funds, and any change returns to the Chamber.

World.content:
The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi, file photo.

Sport: Abu Dhabi

Key Facts —Verdict. Abu Dhabi Criminal Court convicted 10 people; eight got six months in prison, two were fined. Merab Dvalishvili, a Georgian former UFC (Ultimate Fighting Championship) champion, is cleared to wrestle Brazil’s Marlon Moraes on 14 November. —As of. 13 November 2026, 18:30 GMT

Eight people were sentenced to six months in prison and deportation after a Yas Island lobby fight, while the Real American Freestyle (RAF) wrestling card goes ahead on Saturday.

What the Court Ruled

An Abu Dhabi court has convicted 10 people over a brawl at a hotel on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, reported to involve mixed martial arts (MMA) fighter Usman Nurmagomedov, his associates and Merab Dvalishvili. The Abu Dhabi Judicial Department, the emirate’s court authority, announced the verdicts on Friday 13 November 2026, as reported by UAE newspapers The National, Khaleej Times and Gulf News.

Six defendants received six months in prison and a Dh300,000 fine (about US$81,700) each. They will be deported after serving their sentences, for disturbing public security, causing panic and endangering lives.

Two more defendants were convicted of disturbing public security and assaulting others. Each was fined Dh50,000 (about US$13,600) and received no prison term.

The last two defendants also got six months, a Dh300,000 fine (about US$81,700) each and deportation, according to the statement as quoted by Khaleej Times. Their offence was “violating privacy by using information technology to film and publish footage of the brawl”, and their phones were confiscated and the footage ordered deleted.

In total, eight people were sentenced to prison. Dirham amounts here are converted at 3.6725 per US dollar, the official peg.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Abu Dhabi Email address Follow

What Happened in the Hotel

The fight took place on Wednesday 11 November 2026 in the hotel lobby, ahead of RAF Abu Dhabi. RAF, short for Real American Freestyle, is a freestyle wrestling league.

Abu Dhabi Police confirmed 10 arrests on 12 November, The National reported. Footage of the brawl was widely shared on social media.

Dvalishvili later posted: “Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend.” The National quoted the post and reported that both Georgians showed facial cuts.

A UAE flag display in Dubai, file photo. The brawl took place in Abu Dhabi.

Who Is and Is Not Named

Usman Nurmagomedov has been the lightweight champion of the Professional Fighters League (PFL), a US mixed martial arts promotion. Dvalishvili, 35, is a Georgian former bantamweight champion of the UFC, the Ultimate Fighting Championship, the sport’s biggest league.

Dvalishvili beat Usman’s brother Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC 311 in January 2025. The Judicial Department statement names no defendants.

The National says the two people fined are believed to be Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, his 21-year-old friend. Gulf News reports that the authorities have not publicly identified the convicted.

Khaleej Times adds that Abu Dhabi authorities have not directly linked the hotel incident to the UFC fighters. We therefore describe the people in the case only as defendants or convicted.

Why It Matters for Fight Fans

RAF announced late on Friday that Dvalishvili is cleared to wrestle his original opponent, the Brazilian Marlon Moraes, on Saturday 14 November at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Dvalishvili’s friend Saba Lazishvili will make his professional debut against UFC legend Urijah Faber, replacing Umar Nurmagomedov, The National reported.

What it means for you: Dvalishvili’s bout is still scheduled for Saturday, so fans who plan to watch can expect it to go ahead. For Brazilian fans, Moraes keeps his fight.

The case was heard in the United Arab Emirates, not Brazil. The charges cited public security and privacy offences, including filming and publishing footage of the fight.

What Is Not Known

The statement does not say which defendant received which sentence. Some outlets report that Usman Nurmagomedov is among the six jailed, while the statement itself names no one.

The statement does not set out any right to appeal. It also does not say when the deportations will take place.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people were convicted over the Abu Dhabi hotel brawl?

Ten people were convicted on Friday 13 November 2026. Eight received six months in prison, and two were fined Dh50,000 (about US$13,600) each, according to the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department.

Will Merab Dvalishvili fight on Saturday?

RAF announced late on Friday 13 November that Dvalishvili is cleared to wrestle Marlon Moraes at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on Saturday 14 November, as reported by The National.

Has Usman Nurmagomedov been sentenced to prison?

That is not officially confirmed. The court statement names no defendants, and outlets differ on whether Usman Nurmagomedov is among the six jailed.

The Brazilian chief of French benefits group Swile says the market grows through acquisitions, weeks after iFood agreed to buy rival Caju, though he named no target.

What the Swile CEO Said

Denis Tassitano, chief executive of Swile Brasil, the Brazilian arm of French benefits and meal-voucher group Swile, says the Brazilian benefits market grows through acquisitions. He says his company is not frightened by that.

He spoke in an interview published on Friday 13 November 2026. “The market moves through acquisitions,” Tassitano said, adding that many companies grow that way, that it is nothing new and that “we are not scared”.

He said Swile has an appetite for acquisitions, and that it is also growing its own marketing, sales and support teams. He named no target and gave no timetable, and Swile earlier bought the benefits company Vee Benefícios.

Tassitano was named head of Swile Brasil on 3 August 2026, succeeding Júlio Britto, the former chief executive. He previously spent about 15 years at software group SAP, latterly at SAP Concur, its travel and expense unit, for Latin America and the Caribbean.

He also said Swile plans to invest R$600 million (about US$106 million, at R$5.64 per US$, the spot rate on 13 November 2026) in Brazil through 2030. He presented as the company’s aim that the Brazilian operation should overtake Swile’s French operation in coming years.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Brazil 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 2 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

What iFood Bought

On Tuesday 20 October 2026, iFood announced that its iFood Benefícios arm is buying Caju. iFood is a Brazilian food-delivery app owned by Dutch group Prosus, and Caju is a Brazilian corporate-benefits startup.

iFood calls it the biggest merger and acquisition deal in its history, and the price was not disclosed. Caju has about 70,000 client companies and 1.3 million active users, according to company figures published on 20 October 2026.

iFood Benefícios has about 500,000 clients and 1.7 million active users. Completion depends on regulators including Cade, Brazil’s antitrust regulator, and until then the two companies stay independent.

Historic office buildings in central São Paulo, file photo.

Why Benefits Are Heating Up

Tassitano described a market that is consolidating, with larger groups buying smaller ones. He also pointed to changes in the rules of PAT, the Programa de Alimentação do Trabalhador, Brazil’s workers’ meal-benefit programme, as part of the context.

Those are his words, not a regulator’s finding. We have not independently assessed the rule changes he cited.

What It Means for You

For readers who follow Brazil’s consumer and financial technology sectors, the interview signals that Swile may pursue deals. That is a statement of intent by one executive, not a signed transaction, and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

For employers and staff who use meal cards, nothing changes today. iFood and Caju stay independent until regulators decide.

What Is Not Known

Tassitano did not say who Swile might buy, when, or at what price. It is also unknown whether Cade clears the iFood and Caju deal, and on what conditions.

The interview is one executive’s statement, not a company filing. Any later announcement will show whether Swile chooses purchases or organic growth.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the Swile Brazil CEO say about acquisitions?

Denis Tassitano said the market moves through acquisitions and that Swile is not scared of the trend. He said the company has an appetite for deals but named no target and gave no timetable.

What is iFood buying?

iFood announced on 20 October 2026 that its iFood Benefícios arm is buying Caju, a Brazilian corporate-benefits startup. The price was not disclosed, and completion depends on regulators including Cade.

How much does Swile plan to invest in Brazil?

Tassitano said Swile plans to invest R$600 million (about US$106 million) in Brazil through 2030. This is the company’s stated plan, not an audited commitment.

World.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Outlook, Teams and Health Services Worldwide
World.content:
Microsoft’s global outage ran into a second day Friday. Outlook email is still failing for many users, and parts of Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 tools only partly work. If your work or school email runs through Microsoft, this is what’s happening and what you can do.

The problems began late Thursday morning, Costa Rica time, when Microsoft opened an incident for users who couldn’t reach their Exchange Online mailboxes. At first the company said the problem was concentrated in the Americas. It later confirmed that users in any region could lose their connection to Microsoft 365.

Downdetector, which tracks outages, logged problems in 74 countries and territories. At Thursday’s peak it had more than 130,000 reports about Outlook alone, most of them from the United States. On Friday morning Microsoft said traffic was gradually coming back. The biggest improvements were in North America, with steady progress in much of Europe. The company still hasn’t said when everything will be fully restored.

Microsoft says Teams messaging, calls and meetings are mostly working. Teams calendars, meeting invitations and scheduling are still affected because they rely on the same email system. Some Outlook users still can’t sign in, and many messages are arriving hours late. Copilot users may get errors when they load a chat or ask for an answer. Planner, To Do and some SharePoint sharing features have also had problems.

Microsoft hasn’t named a root cause. It first blamed heavy load on part of its infrastructure in several regions. Later it said many servers had unexpectedly gone offline, which pushed their traffic onto the machines still running. Engineers stopped all deployments, moved traffic away from the affected systems and restarted servers. They’re also reviewing recent network configuration changes. Some servers brought back overnight failed again once traffic returned, and Microsoft said its early fixes had only marginal success.

Microsoft said it isn’t aware of any malicious activity. Executive vice president Charles Lamanna said the outage doesn’t appear to be a cyberattack. Many Costa Ricans remember the 2022 ransomware attacks that took down Finance Ministry systems and the Social Security System (CCSS). This is different: people can’t get into their accounts, but nothing Microsoft has said suggests customer data was exposed.

Health services abroad have been hit hard. In the United Kingdom, the National Health Service rescheduled some procedures after Teams went down, because it’s a key link between managers and health workers. The NHS also warned that some patients may struggle to get prescriptions, since pharmacies can’t reach doctors’ offices by email.

A UK union, the GMB, said ambulance services and medical centers saw a serious impact, although urgent care appeared unaffected. Japanese economy minister Ryosei Akazawa warned the impact was significant. New Zealand’s foreign ministry had trouble receiving email at its embassies and consulates.

In Australia, schools, courts and government offices began Friday without Outlook. The Euronext stock exchange told listed companies to use the phone, and Workhorse Group, a US company, postponed its quarterly results. No count of affected users in Costa Rica has been published, and no national institution has announced disruptions so far.

Still, Microsoft 365 is part of daily public life here. The Ministry of Public Education gives public school students and teachers institutional email and Microsoft Teams accounts. The Judiciary has made Teams its official platform for virtual hearings. If your email is down, check Microsoft’s official service page at status.cloud.microsoft before you assume the problem is on your end. Resetting your password or reinstalling Outlook won’t fix this.

A message that hasn’t arrived isn’t necessarily lost. Microsoft extended its delivery window to 48 hours, so delayed email is held and delivered instead of bounced back. If you’ve sent anything urgent since Thursday, call or use another channel to make sure it arrived. For urgent coordination, use Teams chat and calls, which mostly work. Double-check meeting times, though, because calendars may be out of sync.

Watch for scama since outages bring a wave of fake “support” emails and texts asking you to log in or reset your password. Don’t click links in those messages. Go to the status page directly. Microsoft said it will keep posting updates on its service status page until everything is restored. It’s the latest of several large cloud outages this year, and it shows how much work, school and public services depend on a few technology providers.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves to Dock Pay for Education Workers Who Joined Strike
World.content:
Costa Rica’s government is moving to dock a day’s pay from education workers who joined Wednesday’s march against cuts to public education, after the Ministry of Public Education (MEP) counted 36,994 staff absent from work. The figure, released by the ministry on Thursday, represents more than a third of the MEP payroll. The ministry said 175 school dining halls did not open and some 800 schools reported problems with cleaning or security during the protest.

President Laura Fernández declared the strike illegal at her weekly press conference on Wednesday. She said the government would deduct the day’s wages from those she described as vagabonds who had gone out to demand things that do not exist, and she called union leaders leeches.

Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez said the ministry had already coordinated with the Attorney General’s Office to ask a Labor Court to declare the strike illegal. The MEP sent its report to the Attorney General’s Office on Wednesday night, and a Labor Court will decide whether the walkout was lawful.

Costa Rican labor rules treat the loss of pay for days not worked separately from disciplinary sanctions. Sanctions require a court ruling that a strike was illegal. Thousands of teachers, university students and union members marched through downtown San José on Nov. 11 to demand more money for public education. Their demands included payment of seniority bonuses and pending salary increases, settlement of the state’s debt to the teachers’ pension board, known as Jupema, and changes to the transition to a single global salary scheme.

Marchers also rejected the proposed 2027 education budget, which equals 4.9% of gross domestic product. The Constitution sets 8% of GDP as the target for public education spending. The 2027 national budget includes a cut of 19.23 billion colones, about $42.9 million, to the MEP. Public universities joined the march to protest reductions to funds the government had agreed to return to them after the pandemic.

Sánchez rejected the unions’ arguments, saying the government had met and exceeded the agreements it reached two years ago. He pointed to an increase in the sector’s budget during a period of deflation and falling enrollment, without comparing that figure with GDP. The minister also criticized union proposals to raise the MEP budget from 2.8 trillion colones, about $6.2 billion, to nearly 5.8 trillion colones, about $12.9 billion. Fernández said she had held two working meetings with education union leaders during her first six months in office.

The National Association of Educators (ANDE) sent a statement on Thursday to Fernández and Sánchez objecting to the pay deduction and asked the president for a public apology. The Association of Secondary School Teachers (APSE), whose president is Dennis Solís Cruz, defended teachers’ participation and said that taking to the streets is a way to defend labor rights and public education.

The unions maintain that the strike was legal. Many teachers also responded on social media, posting messages about the demands of their work and rejecting the president’s description of them. The dispute comes as the 2027 national budget remains on hold. The Constitutional Chamber has barred lawmakers from holding the final vote on the spending plan before Nov. 29 while it reviews challenges tied to funding for the Judiciary and public universities.

The Labor Court will now decide whether the government can treat the walkout as illegal. The budget vote at the end of the month will set how much money public schools and universities receive in 2027.

World.title: Gas Cylinders Pulled in Costa Rica – Here’s How to Check Yours
World.content:
If your stove runs on a propane tank, the cylinder you swap at the corner store can be pulled from sale if inspectors find it unsafe, and thousands were this year. Costa Rica’s Public Services Regulatory Authority (ARESEP) destroyed 13,415 liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders between January and September 2026.

That is 302 more than the 13,113 it destroyed in the same months of 2025, an increase of 2.3%, according to ARESEP. About 37% of this year’s total, or 4,926 cylinders, were made of aluminum. Aluminum tanks get the closest look for a simple reason. Years of refills, transport and rough handling wear the metal down. Once the wall gets thinner than the safe minimum, the tank can no longer reliably hold the pressure inside it, and the risk of a leak or a rupture goes up.

ARESEP says worn aluminum cylinders are its first priority for removal. The numbers matter because so many homes depend on these tanks. About half of Costa Rican households use LPG, mostly for cooking, according to the regulator. The country used 481.4 million net liters (about 127.2 million US gallons) of LPG in 2025, 4.7% more than in 2024.

Here is how the checks work. ARESEP inspectors visit bottling plants and the shops that sell cylinders. They look at the tank and its valve, test for leaks and confirm that you get the amount of gas you pay for. When something is wrong, the regulator can block the sale and send the cylinder back to the bottler, which must either repair it or destroy it.

Every major brand had cylinders pulled. Data from ARESEP’s energy division show Supergas with 4,275 destroyed cylinders (32% of the total), Tomza with 3,853 (29%), Zeta with 2,780 (21%), Petrogas with 1,672 (12%) and Nanogas with 835 (6%). The regulator published raw counts, not rates, so the figures do not show how each company’s share compares with the number of cylinders it has in circulation.

You can do your own quick check when a delivery arrives or before you carry a tank out of the store. ARESEP recommends three things. First, make sure the cylinder has no dents, corrosion or signs of a leak. Second, check that the valve carries the bottler’s seal, which shows the tank was filled and closed at the plant. Third, look for a serial number and manufacture date you can read clearly, because those markings are how a cylinder’s age and history are tracked.

If a tank fails any of those checks, ask for a different one. You can also contact ARESEP on its toll-free line, 8000-273737, Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. If you ever smell gas at home, close the cylinder valve, open doors and windows, avoid switching lights or appliances on or off, and call 911 from outside.

Cooking gas is one more line in a household energy bill that has been under pressure this year. Fuel prices jumped in October, consumer prices rose for a second straight month, and the country paid $701 million more for imported fuel as diesel climbed. Electricity customers also face El Niño-related power costs spread across future bills.

For anyone who cooks with gas in Costa Rica, inspectors catch thousands of worn tanks a year, but a 30-second look at the tank, the seal and the markings is the easiest way to keep a worn one out of your kitchen.

World.title: Costa Rica Moves to Fire 36 Finance Ministry Workers Over Mouse-Jiggler App
World.content:
Costa Rica’s Finance Ministry is still working to fire 36 employees accused of installing a mouse-jiggler program to make it look as if they were working during remote-work shifts. The ministry will not yet say whether the software exposed any of its systems. The ministry announced the dismissal proceedings on Sept. 10.

Vice Minister of Revenue Víctor Carvajal said at the time that the program simulated mouse movement on institutional computers, so the employees appeared active and their screens did not lock during the workday. Carvajal said the 36 work in the ministry’s revenue, expenditure and administrative areas. He said the evidence pointed to possible job abandonment and that the employees would lose their telework arrangements while the dismissal process runs its course.

The program identified in the case is called Move Mouse. The ministry says it uses web-browsing controls and monitors the security of its equipment, yet the employees were able to install the program on government computers without authorization. Jeffrey Taylor, the ministry’s director of technology and digital innovation, said the ban on unauthorized software rests on the institution’s information-security and software-management policies, along with other general regulations. He did not specify which provisions apply or what sanctions they carry.

Asked whether the program led to data theft, infections or exposed credentials, Taylor said the state of the investigation did not allow the ministry to provide further information. He said the ministry took immediate steps to stop the installation and use of the software once the cases were identified. A technical team is now drafting a plan to tighten controls, he said.

The ministry oversees the country’s tax collection and holds tax records for individuals and businesses. In April 2022, a ransomware attack by the Conti group knocked its tax and customs systems offline for weeks. Costa Rica’s professional association for computing, the Colegio de Profesionales en Informática y Computación, said mouse-jiggler tools are not malicious in themselves and have legitimate uses. It warned, however, that keeping a session open with no one at the keyboard can expose information and systems to unauthorized access.

The association also cautioned that the mere presence of such a program on a computer does not prove misconduct. It said investigators should establish who installed it, who ran it and why, noting that the user account linked to an installation does not always identify the person responsible.

The dismissals must still clear administrative proceedings before they become final. The ministry, now headed by former President Rodrigo Chaves, has not named the employees.

World.title: Two Arrested in Killing of American Surfer Kurt Van Dyke in Costa Rica
World.content:
Costa Rican investigators have arrested two people in the February killing of Kurt Van Dyke. He was the 66-year-old American surfer and Puerto Viejo hotel owner found dead in his home near Cahuita on Valentine’s Day. The Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) detained a 31-year-old woman and a 34-year-old man today. The arrests came during three raids in the Guápiles area of Limón.

Both are suspects in an aggravated homicide investigation. Both were handed over to prosecutors, who will decide whether to seek charges or precautionary measures. Neither has been charged. Investigators now say the attack was not the random robbery it first appeared to be. According to the OIJ’s preliminary findings, the suspects allegedly planned the assault to obtain the PINs of bank cards linked to Van Dyke’s hotel.

The woman was in the home on the morning of Feb. 14 and was initially reported as a survivor of the attack. OIJ deputy director Vladimir Muñoz said she had a direct personal relationship with Van Dyke. Investigators allege she helped the attackers get into the house. Muñoz said Gutiérrez entered the home with two other men who have not yet been identified. According to his account, the group used violence to try to force Van Dyke to give up his card PINs. When that failed, Muñoz said, they beat and tortured him.

Van Dyke was found under a bed with apparent stab wounds and signs of asphyxia. The OIJ received the report at about 10:50 a.m. that Saturday. Investigators also allege that the group staged the theft of the woman’s car to hide her role. The vehicle was later found undamaged in the Atlantic region, which the OIJ considers evidence supporting her alleged participation.

Agents seized cell phones and a vehicle believed to have carried Gutiérrez and the two other men to the scene. Muñoz said two more people remain to be arrested in the case. Van Dyke grew up in Santa Cruz, California. He came to Costa Rica’s southern Caribbean in the 1980s, drawn by Salsa Brava, the powerful reef break off Puerto Viejo.

Known in surfing circles as “King,” he was a nephew of Hawaii big-wave pioneer Fred Van Dyke. For decades he ran Hotel Puerto Viejo, a regular stop for traveling surfers. His death drew international coverage. It also led the Costa Rican Hotel Chamber and local tourism leaders to voice concern about the region’s image. Tourism Minister William Rodríguez offered condolences at the time and said Costa Rica remains a safe destination.

The Public Ministry is expected to request precautionary measures in the coming days, which could include pretrial detention. The OIJ has not identified the two remaining suspects. Anyone with information can contact the agency’s confidential line at 800-8000-645.

World.title: 5 Costa Rica Parks With Closed Trails or New Rules This High Season
World.content:
High season is starting, and several of Costa Rica’s best-known national parks have a trail, an entrance or a whole sector closed. Others are open but are letting in fewer people under stricter rules. Here’s what’s shut, what’s open with conditions, and what to check before you buy a ticket.

Entry to most national parks is sold only online, and many parks close one day a week. Volcano parks can change their rules with little notice, so check the park’s official page the day before you go.

1. Marino Ballena National Park

The Piñuela sector closed on Monday, Nov. 9, and is expected to stay closed for six months because its facilities have deteriorated. You can’t walk in, and boats can’t drop off or pick up passengers there. The bathrooms and showers at Piñuela are also closed. The Uvita, Colonia and Ballena sectors stay open.

If your tour lands at Piñuela, ask your operator how the plan has changed.

2. Manuel Antonio National Park

The Punta Catedral trail is temporarily closed. It’s the loop over the headland between the park’s two main beaches, with lookouts over the Pacific. No reopening date has been given. The rest of the park is open Wednesday through Monday. It closes every Tuesday.

3. Poás Volcano National Park

Poás is open, but since Aug. 28 it has admitted about half as many people and you must wear a helmet. The rules followed a moderate eruption that threw rock from the crater. The park now admits 1,064 visitors a day, down from 2,052. Only two trails are open: the main trail to the crater lookout and the Sombrilla de Pobre trail. Up to 56 people at a time can stand at the lookout, for 20 minutes per group.

The limits stay in place until volcanic activity drops enough to lower the risk. Book early, because half the daily tickets means they sell out faster.

4. Rincón de la Vieja National Park

The trail to the active crater is still closed. It stays shut until activity drops enough for the climb to be considered safe. The volcano has been one of the country’s most active this year. Five districts of Upala and Liberia near the volcano have been under a yellow alert since Oct. 1.

The Las Pailas sector, with its mud pots and steam vents, is open Tuesday through Sunday, well below the summit.

5. Corcovado National Park

The Sirena, Los Patos and El Tigre sectors were closed to tourists through October for maintenance and the heaviest rains. Only San Pedrillo and La Leona stayed open.

Daily limits also apply. Sirena takes 366 visitors a day, San Pedrillo 120, and La Leona, Los Patos and El Tigre 80 each. Before you travel, confirm with your guide or lodge that your sector has reopened.

Playa Langosta, near Tamarindo

This isn’t a trail closure. Environmental authorities are investigating a die-off of fish, sharks, rays and birds in the San Francisco estuary at Playa Langosta. They have asked people not to alter the estuary’s mouth to the sea without permission.

The national park system has more than two dozen protected areas open to visitors, and most trails are running normally this season. Tickets, schedules and closures are posted on each park’s official page, and those pages are the most reliable guide to what’s open on the day you plan to go.

World.title: Four in Ten Costa Ricans Hold Back Opinions on Social Media Out of Fear
World.content:
Four in ten Costa Ricans say they have held back from sharing their opinions on social media for fear of the consequences, according to a national survey released yesterday by the University of Costa Rica (UCR). The fourth National Survey on Freedom of Expression and Trust in the Media found that 40.1% of respondents have stopped expressing their views online out of fear, down from 46.5% in 2025 and the lowest level since the survey began in 2023.

For the first time, a majority, 56.2%, said they had not held back, after that figure hovered around 48% in the three previous editions. The survey does not specify what respondents fear, whether criticism, harassment, consequences at work or something else. Women were more likely to stay silent. After controlling for age, education and political attitudes, researchers found that women were 10 percentage points more likely than men to say they avoid expressing opinions on social media.

The findings matter because social media has become the main way Costa Ricans follow national news. According to the survey, 70.7% regularly or always use social networks to stay informed, compared with 46.2% who often watch television newscasts. The gap between the two has widened since 2025, when social media first overtook television, and radio news now ranks last.

Perceptions of free speech in general also improved. The share of people who believe freedom of expression is at risk in Costa Rica fell to 54.7%, from 73.4% in 2025. This year’s edition is the first carried out since President Laura Fernández took office in May 2026. According to the survey, 60.1% now believe the government respects freedom of expression, the highest share recorded by the study.

Trust in the press rose sharply. For the first time since the survey began, a majority of respondents, 56.2%, said they trust the news media, up from 43.4% in 2025, 35.6% in 2024 and 32.6% in 2023. Trust in journalists themselves reached 71.5%, the highest in the survey’s four editions.

At the same time, 58.1% said working as a journalist in Costa Rica is dangerous, the highest share since the question was first asked and up from 48% in 2023. The finding comes amid broader scrutiny of press freedom in Costa Rica. The survey also points to the reach of misinformation. One in three respondents, 33.5%, admitted recently believing information that later turned out to be false, up from 28.1% in 2025. Facebook was the platform most often cited as the source, followed by TikTok and WhatsApp.

Looking back at the 2026 election campaign, 49% said they had come across false content about presidential candidates and 43% about the Supreme Elections Tribunal. The study was carried out by UCR’s Freedom of Expression and Right to Information Program (PROLEDI), together with the university’s Communication Research Center (CICOM) and Center for Political Research and Studies (CIEP).

Researchers interviewed 993 adults with mobile phones, selected at random, between Sept. 2 and 14, 2026. The maximum margin of error is 3.1 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. Taken together, the results show fewer Costa Ricans censoring themselves online than a year ago, while a substantial share still hesitate to speak freely in the digital spaces where most of the country now gets its news.

World.title: San Ramón Forests Hold Nearly Half of Costa Rica’s Bat Species
World.content:
The forests around San Ramón shelter at least 56 bat species, nearly half of all those recorded in Costa Rica, according to researchers at the University of Costa Rica (UCR) who are studying how these often-misunderstood mammals cope as their habitat is broken up by farms, pastures and towns.

The work is led by UCR’s Western Campus in San Ramón, where scientists and students are tracking how bats respond to changes in their surroundings and what that means for forests and farming. One study sampled seven sites in and around the Alberto Manuel Brenes Biological Reserve to examine how forest fragmentation and degradation affect bat populations. Researchers captured and studied 407 bats from 39 species, including 10 species that had never before been documented in the area.

Those new records helped raise the known total for the wider San Ramón region to at least 56 species. UCR researcher Daniel Zamora said the findings show the importance of protecting not only large, continuous forests but also the smaller patches of vegetation that link one habitat to another. Landscapes that mix farms, pastures, forest and homes, he said, can still support remarkable biodiversity.

One encouraging result was the abundance of fruit-eating bats. By dispersing seeds, they help plants spread and drive the natural regeneration of tropical forests. Other species eat insects, which could make them valuable to farmers. UCR graduate student Katherine Álvarez is studying whether insect-eating bats help control pests that attack potato crops in Cartago, with the aim of producing evidence that supports conservation and encourages growers to see bats as allies.

The university is also looking at how bats adapt to cities, including the role of protected green spaces in San Ramón and Liberia. Researchers are combining field surveys with acoustic monitoring, which records bats’ echolocation calls, to map where different species live and how they respond to changing environments. A recent urban wildlife survey in Heredia found similar surprises in city green spaces.

Other studies are examining parasites carried by bats, and a project on their anatomy and evolutionary relationships is planned for 2027. Alongside the science, the program runs environmental education activities aimed at dispelling myths about bats. Researchers work with students, community groups, landowners and conservation organizations to share what they find and build support for protecting the animals.

World.title: Four years after guilty pleas, sentencing delayed again for two men in killing of PC Osburne Martinez
World.content:
Four years after guilty pleas, sentencing delayed again for two men in killing of PC Osburne Martinez

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Tyrique Myles and Glen Lopez remain in custody awaiting sentencing, four years after pleading guilty to manslaughter in the fatal shooting of Police Constable Osburne Martinez. High Court Justice Nigel Pilgrim adjourned the case on November 11 to give Myles’ attorney more time to reach his character witnesses.

Defence attorney Norman Rodriguez told the court he intends to call witnesses on behalf of Myles, 26, but has been unable to contact them. Orson “OJ” Elrington, who represents Lopez, 29, said he would not call any character witnesses. The case is set to return to court on November 18.

Myles and Lopez pleaded guilty to manslaughter in November 2022. The terms discussed by the Crown and defence were 17½ years for Myles and 13 years for Lopez, but the court has yet to impose either sentence. An earlier sentencing hearing was adjourned because the agreed facts and formal plea agreement had not been filed.

Martinez, 27, was shot while responding to an armed robbery at the Belcove Hotel on Regent Street West in Belize City on November 2, 2018. He later died at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital. The third man charged in the case, Rayford Mejia, was convicted of murder after trial and sentenced to life in prison in 2023.

World.title: Sentencing delayed again for two police officers convicted of filming couple having sex
World.content:
Sentencing delayed again for two police officers convicted of filming couple having sex

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Sentencing has been delayed again for two police officers convicted of wilful oppression after recording a couple engaged in a sexual act and sharing the footage in a police WhatsApp group during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Police Corporal Jason Shaw and Police Constable Leslie Martinez, who were found guilty on July 17, 2026, appeared before High Court Justice Derick F. Sylvester on Friday, November 6, but their sentencing was further adjourned to allow arguments from the prosecution and defense.

The Crown is seeking custodial sentences for both officers, while their attorneys are urging the court to impose non-custodial penalties.

Justice Sylvester is expected to consider submissions from both sides, particularly because there is reportedly no directly comparable case to guide the court in determining an appropriate sentence.

The judge scheduled Monday, November 9, to hear the sentencing arguments.

The case stems from an incident on April 5, 2020, when the officers encountered a couple engaged in a sexual act inside an abandoned building in Belize City during the COVID-19 lockdown.

Prosecutors argued that the officers abused their authority by recording the couple and circulating the footage in a police WhatsApp group known as “Loyal Group.” The video subsequently went viral, causing humiliation and distress to the individuals involved.

A nine-member jury, comprising five women and four men, unanimously convicted Shaw and Martinez following a four-day retrial before Justice Sylvester in July.

The case had previously encountered several setbacks, including an aborted trial in June 2025 and a hung jury in October 2025.

A third officer, Police Constable Anthony Villamil, was initially charged alongside Shaw and Martinez but was later granted immunity in exchange for his testimony against them.

Shaw is represented by attorney Oscar Selgado, while Martinez is represented by attorney Leeroy Banner.

The officers remain awaiting sentencing as the court considers whether imprisonment or a non-custodial penalty is appropriate.

World.title: Two teenagers charged after police catch them riding stolen security guard’s motorcycle
World.content:
Two teenagers charged after police catch them riding stolen security guard’s motorcycle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two teenagers, ages 15 and 17, have been charged with theft after police allegedly caught them riding a motorcycle stolen from a security guard’s yard in the Vista Del Mar area of Ladyville.

The minors, a 15-year-old from Ladyville and a 17-year-old from Hattieville, were taken before the Belize Family Court on Thursday, November 5, following their detention earlier in the week.

According to police reports, the motorcycle, a black 2024 Lifan valued at $2,500, belongs to a 34-year-old Rangers Security guard who resides on Red Snapper Street in Vista Del Mar Phase 2.

The security guard reported that he had parked his motorcycle outside his home on the night of November 2, 2026, before going to sleep. He said he had kept the keys in his possession and had not authorized anyone to use the motorcycle.

Around 2:50 a.m. on November 3, he and his common-law wife were awakened by police officers knocking on their door. The officers asked whether he owned a motorcycle, prompting him to check his yard, where he discovered it was missing.

Police explained that while patrolling the Philip Goldson Highway, they spotted two young males riding a motorcycle without its lights on, heading from the Lord’s Bank junction toward the Burrell Boom junction.

Officers intercepted the teenagers, who allegedly admitted to taking the motorcycle from the security guard’s residence.

Police subsequently showed him a photograph of the recovered motorcycle, which he positively identified as his property. He later visited the Ladyville Police Station, where he formally identified the motorcycle and made a theft report.

Both teenagers were charged with theft in the presence of a Justice of the Peace before being taken to the Belize Family Court.

The case remains before the court.

World.title: New Micro Enterprise and Entrepreneurship program to provide tax relief to small businesses
World.content:
New Micro Enterprise and Entrepreneurship program to provide tax relief to small businesses

By Zoila Palma: Cabinet has approved the introduction of Micro Enterprise and Entrepreneurship legislation aimed at supporting the growth and development of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

The decision was made during Cabinet’s meeting on November 10, 2026.

Under the proposed legislation, a flat annual charge will be established for all micro enterprises.

Additionally, MSMEs approved under the MSME Fiscal Incentives Programme will be exempt from General Sales Tax (GST) on imports of equipment, packaging and labels, as well as industrial and agricultural inputs.

World.title: Attorney Norman Rodriguez says he received $800 not $1,200 and represented ‘Easy Glen’ until told to stop
World.content:
Attorney Norman Rodriguez says he received $800 not $1,200 and represented ‘Easy Glen’ until told to stop

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Attorney Norman Rodriguez has pushed back against Goldburn “Easy Glen” Adolphus’ claim that his aunt paid $1,200 for legal representation only for him to face his preliminary inquiry alone. Rodriguez said he received $800 and had already made several court appearances and prison visits on Adolphus’ behalf before being told his services were no longer needed.

Adolphus, 56, raised the complaint on November 10 after appearing without an attorney before the Chief Magistrate. At the end of the inquiry, the court committed him to stand trial in the January 2027 session of the High Court for the murder of Shaniele Faber. Rodriguez informed the court by letter that he no longer represented Adolphus.

In an interview, Rodriguez said he quoted $1,500 for the preliminary inquiry. He said Adolphus wanted the murder case to end at that stage, but he told him he could not promise that outcome because the prosecution’s statements appeared to contain enough evidence for the case to go to trial. Rodriguez said Adolphus later told him that his aunt would handle the matter.

Adolphus said he intends to take his complaint to the Bar Association and seek new legal representation. He has been on remand since his October 7, 2025 arraignment.

Faber, a 42-year-old school warden and mother of four, was found dead on October 4, 2025, by a man searching for bottles in a blue garbage drum at the corner of Amandala Drive and Cemetery Road in Belize City.

World.title: Department of Environment evaluates effectiveness of Belize’s Single-Use Plastics Regulations
World.content:
Department of Environment evaluates effectiveness of Belize’s Single-Use Plastics Regulations

By Zoila Palma: The Department of the Environment (DOE) is assessing the effectiveness of Belize’s Single-Use Plastics Initiative as part of ongoing efforts to reduce plastic pollution and minimize the harmful effects of disposable plastic and Styrofoam products on the environment.

The initiative, introduced by the Government of Belize, established restrictions on selected single-use plastic products through the Environmental Protection (Pollution from Plastics) Regulations.

The regulations introduced restrictions and prohibitions on specified products while establishing requirements for import permits, manufacturing licences, product registration, exemptions and conformity assessments.

They also provide enforcement mechanisms intended to ensure compliance and support the country’s transition toward reducing the use and circulation of certain plastic products.

To determine how effectively the initiative has been implemented and whether its intended objectives have been achieved, the DOE commissioned a consultancy to conduct an evaluation and assessment of the programme and its supporting regulations. The assessment examines the progress made since the introduction of the measures and identifies areas requiring improvement.

Today, the department presented the findings of the Evaluation and Assessment Report to key stakeholders through a hybrid meeting involving representatives from the manufacturing sector and importers. The engagement provided an opportunity for participants to discuss progress in implementing the regulations, challenges encountered by businesses in meeting regulatory requirements, and recommendations to strengthen enforcement and compliance.

The DOE emphasized that engaging stakeholders, particularly manufacturers and importers directly affected by the regulations, is essential to identifying practical solutions and improving the initiative’s overall effectiveness.

World.title: Belize Catholic Diocese reviews Father Edward Gallagher’s San Ignacio ministry after report he took a Belizean teenage boy to live with him in Northern Ireland
World.content:
Belize Catholic Diocese reviews Father Edward Gallagher’s San Ignacio ministry after report he took a Belizean teenage boy to live with him in Northern Ireland

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Roman Catholic Diocese of Belize City and Belmopan is reviewing records of Father Edward Gallagher’s ministry in San Ignacio, Cayo, following his guilty plea to 109 sex offences in Northern Ireland. The review comes amid reports that a Belizean teenage boy accompanied Gallagher back to Northern Ireland after his missionary assignment and lived with him there.

In a statement dated November 12, the Belize diocese said the Diocese of Derry sent Gallagher to Belize, where he served in San Ignacio from approximately 1999 to 2004. The Belize diocese said it had received no complaints or allegations of abuse against him but was reviewing its records. It said anyone who comes forward will be treated with respect and confidentiality and offered pastoral support.

As Breaking Belize News previously reported, The Irish News reported that the teenager is believed to have lived with Gallagher for several months in a parish house in County Tyrone. The Diocese of Derry told the newspaper it had no knowledge or record of the reported arrangement. The report did not allege that Gallagher abused the teenager, and the Belize diocese did not address the reported arrangement in its statement.

Gallagher, 59, pleaded guilty at Londonderry Crown Court on October 5. The offences date from June 2023 to April 2025, nearly two decades after his time in Belize, and include attempting to communicate sexually with children and possessing indecent images of children. He remains in custody pending sentencing on December 9.

Derry Bishop Michael Router said Gallagher was suspended from ministry after his arrest and that he was petitioning the Vatican to dismiss him from the priesthood.

World.title: Corozal Sustainable Future Initiative urges motorists to slow down for wildlife crossing on Sarteneja road
World.content:
Corozal Sustainable Future Initiative urges motorists to slow down for wildlife crossing on Sarteneja road

By Zoila Palma: The Corozal Sustainable Future Initiative (CSFI) is urging motorists to slow down and remain alert for wildlife crossing roads, following the discovery of a dead Northern Tamandua along the Sarteneja Road on Thursday morning.

CSFI Rangers recovered the animal from the roadway after it was suspected to have been struck by a vehicle.

CSFI warned that roadkill remains a serious threat to Belize’s wildlife, particularly in areas where roads pass through natural habitats. It reminded motorists that animals frequently cross these roadways and may be difficult to spot, especially during periods of reduced visibility.

CSFI is encouraging drivers travelling through forested areas to reduce their speed, remain vigilant and watch for wildlife, particularly during early morning and nighttime hours.

World.title: JC’s Walker Cup ban overturned, school instead placed on probation
World.content:
Jamone Lyle (second right) and his Jamaica College teammates celebrate a goal in their Walker Cup semi-final against Mona High on Saturday, October 10, 2026. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

Jamaica College (JC) have now been placed on a two-year probation by the Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) Appeals Board for using an ineligible player during the ongoing schoolboy football season, replacing an earlier decision that would have barred the school from next year’s Walker Cup competition.

The latest ruling, announced in an ISSA press release, follows a meeting of the Appeals Board last Friday to review Jamaica College’s appeal against decisions made by the association’s Disciplinary Committee and subsequently upheld by its Executive Committee.

The Appeals Board set aside the decision that JC would not be invited to participate in the 2027 Walker Cup and instead placed the school on two years’ probation, effective November 6, 2026.

However, the board dismissed the other two aspects of the school’s appeal, leaving intact the sanctions imposed in relation to player Jamone Lyle.

The decision to forfeit all points earned from matches in which Lyle participated was upheld, as was his one-year suspension from ISSA competitions.

Under the terms of the suspension, Lyle may become eligible to participate in ISSA competitions after serving the period, provided he remains a student in good standing and has relinquished his professional status in accordance with FIFA guidelines.

Both decisions were originally taken by ISSA’s Executive Committee on October 18, 2026.

The latest ruling therefore allows Jamaica College to remain eligible for consideration for the 2027 Walker Cup, but the school will now serve another two-year probation, having just completed a previous two-year probation for another matter.

ISSA Competitions Officer Ewan Scott, who signed the release, noted that the association’s rules state that decisions of the Appeals Board are binding on all concerned.

World.title: Nine years on, CRH to open renovated A&E department
World.content:
ST JAMES, Jamaica — The newly rebuilt Accident and Emergency (A&E) Department at the Cornwall Regional Hospital (CRH) is set to be opened on Friday, nine years after the department along with the rest of the hospital was shuttered after noxious fumes made the condition untenable for staff and patients.

The project faced notable delays over the period, but the A&E department, which is currently housed at the Mount Salem Health Centre, will finally return to the main building.

It has been described as at least twice the size of the previous area and will include operating theatres to make it one of the most modern A&Es in Jamaica.

It follows the opening of the Administration department at the CRH building in April 2025.

World.title: WATCH: ‘No hit in 20 years!’ McKenzie takes aim at Beenie Man
World.content:
West Kingston Member of Parliament Desmond McKenzie has declared that Beenie Man’s Weh di money deh? that was released as a single earlier this month will not sell.

“You have a certain deejay, for the last 20 years him can’t make a number one hit song, and all of a sudden … left the shores of Jamaica and gone out deh and talk about ‘Weh di money deh’,” McKenzie said.

“Dat deh record nah sell at all, nobody nah buy it,” added McKenzie who is also Deputy Leader of the governing Jamaica Labour Party (JLP).

He was speaking Thursday night at the annual West Kingston Constituency Conference inside the Edward Seaga Auditorium at the Tivoli Gardens High School.

His remark is the latest salvo in a dispute that erupted in October when Beenie Man, during an interview with British broadcaster ITV News, questioned how millions of dollars in donations to the Jamaican Government intended for Hurricane Melissa victims was distributed.

READ: ‘You don’t see where the money go’: Beenie Man criticises Gov’t hurricane relief spending

“This is nothing new that the Government get the money, the Government distribute the money the wrong way. The people who supposed to get the money haven’t been getting any,” Beenie Man claimed.

His remarks have met with pushback from members of the Government including Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness. But, when it was thought that the matter was settled, Beenie Man released Weh di money deh? And McKenzie ripped into him Thursday night.

Suggesting that Beenie Man was seeking relevance, he said, “Yuh have a certain DJ, fi di last 20 years him caw mek a number one hit song. And all of a sudden, him caw mek it locally caw him nah say nutten. [So] him lef di shores of Jamaica an gone out deh go talk about ‘weh di money deh…government hold on pon di money”.

The deputy leader of the JLP told the conference that, “We’re at a point in the country’s history where what matters more is substance than fluff. And what we have is a government of performance”.

He admitted that like any other government, the Holness-led Administration would have got some things wrong. “We would not be the only government in the world that makes mistakes but we admit to our faults and we do what is necessary to correct our mistakes,” he said.

-Lynford Simpson

World.title: Toll rebels being barred
World.content:
The Caymanas toll plaza where motorists enter and exit the Edward Seaga Highway. (Photo: Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited)

Unruly motorists have pushed the operators of the Edward Seaga Highway (or T3 leg of Highway 2000) to develop a blacklist system that flags vehicles linked to toll road violations and restrict them from accessing the motorway.

According to the Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited (JNSHCL), developer and operator of the 66.13-kilometre road which has six toll plazas and one local head office operating on a 24/7 basis, the violations include tailgating through the barrier, forcing the barrier, and stealing or swapping toll cards to avoid payment. Verbal abuse or violent threats against staff will also result in blacklisting. Blacklisted vehicles are prohibited from entering the highway and once identified will be turned away.

According to the operators, those responsible will bear full legal responsibility under applicable law for any resulting harm, disruption or consequences to the highway and the travelling public.

Trudy-Ann Williams, deputy commercial and compliance manager for the JNSHCL, told the

Jamaica Observer that a pilot of the feature was conducted last month and full roll-out is slated for the end of this month.

“We had security on the ground, personnel from the Jamaica Constabulary who were willing to assist us once we were able to identify these motorists, to escort them from the toll lane

— if it is that they became boisterous

— or just simply to provide further information to them about the reason they were placed on the blacklist,” Williams told the Observer.

She said the operators have developed a working list based on past violations committed by operators of private and public passenger vehicles.

“The numbers fluctuate. Right now I think we have over 50 licence plates; it’s not an extensive list and the list is updated as time goes by, as we do more research, so the list will change if a motorist comes forward and clears themselves; they will be removed and the list updated,” she told the Observer.

Williams said an individual who, for example, was blacklisted because they did not pay the toll can clear themselves by coming forward to pay the relevant sum.

Explaining how the debarring feature works, Williams said, “Once a motorist who is on the blacklist approaches the toll lane, their licence plate will be detected by our new QR code system and an alert will go off, meaning an alarm, and they will be barred and not allowed to enter the highway. Once they are discovered we will alert the motorist that they are on the blacklist and that they should remove themselves from the toll lane,” Williams said.

“There is a flashing light, there is an alarm and the barrier will not open,” she said, adding that motorists who wish to be clear about their status can contact JNSHCL through its general office or customer service lines (1-876-803-5075 or 1-888-429-5674), respectively.

“We also will make a list available through our website where they can search to confirm whether or not they are on the blacklist. However, their full details will not be available on the website because we do not want to disclose sensitive details to just about anyone who has access, so they will still have to call to clarify the reason they are blacklisted,” Williams outlined.

She also emphasised that individuals who are involved in altercations with toll booth staff are only blacklisted after thorough investigations.

“There are different reasons why motorists might become blacklisted; it might not only be for toll evasion, even through toll evasion is the number one reason. If we have persons who have violated or abused the toll in any way, including being overly rude or violent toward our staff, they can also be placed on the blacklist. There are not a lot of those persons; however, we would just like persons to bear in mind that we are non-tolerant of our staff members being abused in any way,” she pointed out.

“If it is that someone thinks it was unfair of us to have blacklisted them for that reason, we would have ensured that we did our due diligence before adding them to that list, which includes gathering relevant evidence… for any of those violations. We have evidence, and that is how we determine if the vehicle will be blacklisted. We are not taking it lightly or trying to just build a list on a whim; it is all evidence-based,” Williams said.

In the meantime, she said in addition to the blacklist feature, the JNSHCL is introducing a new way to access the toll road via the QR code or cardless system, effectively phasing out the use of toll cards.

“Persons will be able to access the toll road without taking a toll card and, instead, will use their cellphone to scan a QR code. The cellphone, if it has data or even if it doesn’t have data, we will provide free Wi-Fi at our toll plazas; they can connect or use their data, scan the QR code app or feature on their phone, and that will generate a journey code. Once that information is captured, then they are allowed access to the motorway and then when they get to the exit the information, in most cases, will automatically populate. If it is, that it is not automatically populated, then they can show the QR code on their phone or scan another at the exit. The payment is normal, you can pay via cash or debit card,” Williams explained.

“For persons who are not so familiar or tech-savvy, we are trying to ensure that we do some more public education campaigns. We will have persons at the entrance who can show them how to access the feature and to give further instructions. We will ensure that this happens for a period of at least 10 days once the feature has been launched,” she assured.

Toll evasion in Jamaica is a criminal offence under the Toll Roads Act, resulting in fines up to $10,000 or 30 days’ imprisonment per count for non-payment. Authorities, including TransJamaican Highway

— concessionaires for the tolled motorway running between Portmore and Kingston, and Kingston and Manchester

— use surveillance and police enforcement to target offenders, especially those tailgating or using stolen tags, which can lead to higher penalties.

World.title: Bell in hot water
World.content:
BELL... the Integrity Commission found that he attended deliberations on his wife’s application to the municipal corporation without withdrawing or recusing himself from the Commercial Services Committee

Councillor Ian Bell (People’s National Party, Beecher Town Division) is facing a two-month expulsion from the St Ann Municipal Corporation, removal from two key committees, and a formal reprimand following an Integrity Commission investigation which found that he failed to withdraw from discussions concerning his wife’s application for space at the Ocho Rios Transportation Centre.

St Ann’s Bay Mayor Michael Belnavis announced the proposed disciplinary measures during Thursday’s monthly council meeting, saying a notice of motion for Bell’s expulsion would be brought before the council later that day.

Belnavis said the corporation would also seek Bell’s immediate removal from the Commercial Services Committee, which considers applications and matters relating to the corporation’s commercial activities, and the Planning Committee.

According to the mayor, the proposed two-month expulsion is being pursued under section 44(1) of the Local Governance Act, 2016, on the grounds that Bell brought the corporation into disrepute.

The measures follow an investigation into the circumstances surrounding an application made by Bell’s wife, businesswoman Shirlyn Campbell-Bell, to rent a section of the transportation centre to operate a gaming lounge.

The Integrity Commission found that Bell, who was a member of the Commercial Services Committee, attended deliberations on his wife’s application without withdrawing or recusing himself. The commission said this breached the conflict-of-interest standards expected of elected officials under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Development’s Councillor’s Handbook.

The Integrity Commission recommended that Bell be formally reprimanded for failing to withdraw from the committee’s consideration of the application, despite his personal interest in the matter and his knowledge of the proper procedure.

“The purpose is to protect the integrity of the committee and ensure that its membership can carry out its responsibilities without any unresolved concern regarding this matter. In addition, mandatory refresher training will be required for all members of council. That training must strengthen members’ understanding of the conflicts of interest, disclosure, recusal, ethnic decision-making, statutory obligations and good governance,” Belnavis announced on Thursday.

“We must ensure that members understand not only the procedures but their personal responsibility to uphold them. We cannot allow uncertainty, silence or conflicting interpretations of procedures to compromise the work of this corporation,” he added.

He also noted that the corporation will introduce stricter procedures requiring councillors to formally declare conflicts of interest, with every departure from and return to committee meetings duly recorded in the minutes.

“Conflicts must be declared in writing. Every withdrawal and return must be recorded in the minutes. The clerk to the committee must provide guidance whenever conflict arises and the presiding chair must confirm that the matter can properly proceed before discussion or decision-making begins,” he said.

The Integrity Commission report traced the matter to March 31, 2023, when Campbell-Bell applied to rent space at the transportation centre to place a 40-foot container for a gaming lounge.

The investigation found that the application was delivered to the corporation by Bell rather than being submitted through its Registry Department, as required under the established procedure. It also found that Campbell-Bell’s married name was omitted from the application.

Although the corporation sent her correspondence in May 2023 indicating that the request had been approved, the commission found that the required approval process had not been completed.

The report also found that the structure was built without the necessary building and planning permits, in breach of the Building Act, 2018. It said there was no evidence of a lease agreement between Campbell-Bell and the corporation, or that the application had been referred to the Ministry of Local Government for the minister’s approval.

The commission further found that the gaming lounge had operated since 2023 without paying user fees to the corporation, and that the corporation had made no attempt to collect those fees.

The investigation also examined whether Bell had declared his relationship with the applicant. While six councillors told investigators that he had disclosed that Campbell-Bell was his wife, they could not identify the specific meeting at which this was done. The commission said it was therefore unable to definitively conclude that he had made the declaration.

However, it found that Bell remained present when the application was considered and that the evidence suggested he did not recuse himself from the meeting.

Belnavis said the corporation would now examine the status of the building and take the necessary steps through the relevant legal and technical processes.

“The Integrity Commission’s report indicates that the required building plans were not submitted to the relevant agencies before construction commenced. The existence of the structure does not, in itself, constitute lawful approval,” he said.

The mayor said the corporation would also consider the requirements of section 49 of the Local Government Act, which deals with the sale or lease of land vested in a municipal corporation and requires ministerial approval.

The Integrity Commission recommended that the corporation assess and recover all outstanding fees relating to the business and enforce the relevant laws and policies concerning Campbell-Bell’s occupation of the property.

It also recommended that the corporation strengthen its conflict of interest procedures and consider disciplinary action against Bell, including a formal reprimand.

Belnavis said the measures were intended to ensure that the commission’s findings led to changes in how the corporation manages its commercial properties and conducts its affairs.

World.title: Complex Ricki’s Loving You embraces healing
World.content:
Complex Ricki.

Recording artiste Complex Ricki is encouraging listeners to embrace healing and second chances in love with her latest single, Loving You, released on November 6 through VPAL Music, the distribution arm of VP Records.

The track explores the emotional journey of moving beyond past disappointments, rediscovering one’s worth and finding the courage to pursue meaningful relationships.

For Complex Ricki, the song represents a celebration of personal growth and the possibilities that come with allowing oneself to love again.

“Loving You is about healing, embracing second chances, and finding happiness again. I want people to know that no matter what they’ve been through, they deserve genuine love,” she shared.

Through reflective lyrics, the entertainer addresses the importance of emotional maturity, commitment, and self-discovery, while highlighting the reassurance that comes with finding a relationship built on mutual understanding.

Rather than allowing previous experiences to dictate her outlook on romance, Complex Ricki uses the single to promote a renewed sense of confidence and optimism.

The song also touches on the importance of recognising one’s value and refusing to settle for relationships that do not contribute positively to personal development.

Beyond its romantic message, Loving You encourages listeners to acknowledge their individual progress and remain receptive to new experiences, even after navigating difficult circumstances.

The release adds to Complex Ricki’s growing musical catalogue as she continues to use relatable themes and personal experiences to connect with audiences.

With Loving You, the singer hopes to resonate with individuals who have experienced heartbreak but remain hopeful about finding genuine affection and happiness.

The single is available on all major digital streaming platforms through VPAL Music.

World.title: Everything Fresh eyes bigger slice of Bahamas
World.content:
GRANT...demand is exciting; we have concluded negotiations with RIU and increased volumes on that side in Jamaica

EVERYTHING Fresh Group Limited is eyeing further expansion in The Bahamas, targeting mom-and-pop shops and smaller retailers as it seeks to build its presence beyond the hotel sector. The food distributor, which entered the market in 2018, currently serves close to 50 customers and is pursuing proposals that could significantly improve the profitability of its Bahamian operation.

In an interview with the Jamaica Observer following the company’s annual general meeting at the AC Hotel on Wednesday, General Manager Nicola Maitland said some of the proposals were awaiting approval.

“If we get the approval, within as early as two years we can be very profitable,” she said.

The company is targeting 10 per cent growth in The Bahamas operation by the end of its 2026 financial year. While pursuing growth overseas, Everything Fresh is also adjusting its Jamaican operation following Hurricane Melissa in 2025, which disrupted hotel operations and affected its traditional business model.

Maitland acknowledged that the company had not returned to its pre-hurricane position, particularly as it continues to address outstanding receivables from hotel customers.

“We’re not where we used to be, but we are working with the hotel privately regarding the receivables; however, we are not held fast on a strategy; we are taking multiple options,” she said.

One of those measures has been to increase the company’s exposure to the retail market locally. Although Everything Fresh previously supplied supermarkets and other retailers, it has since increased its presence in that market as it seeks to diversify its customer base and reduce its dependence on hotel business.

“We always supplied retail; however, we have increased our footprint, and we continue to bring in more SKUs based on the demands,” Maitland said.

The company is also introducing products aimed at consumers seeking more affordable alternatives, as it targets the down trend market. This includes a new margarine line, which was introduced in October. To support the expansion of its customer base, Everything Fresh is investing in its distribution infrastructure, including improvements to its Bog Walk facility in St Catherine. The warehouse serves as a central distribution hub for its hotel business and is being expanded to accommodate additional storage and freezer capacity. The company is also increasing its delivery fleet, with additional trucks expected to come on stream in 2027 and 2028.

“We have a lot more trucks coming in for 2027/2028 so we can deliver more products and reduce our delivery times to our customers,” Group Chief Financial Officer Errol Grant said during the AGM.
