World.title: Man Utd name Pochettino as new manager
World.content:
London – Manchester United named Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager on Friday following the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

The club issued a statement saying the USA coach, who has extensive experience in the Premier League, would take charge from November 18 following two matches against Haiti.

“The club has reached an agreement with the US soccer federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US men’s national team,” United said.

“The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

“Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues.”

Pochettino, who led the United States to the last-16 of the World Cup on home soil earlier this year, has previously managed in the English top flight with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

He has a huge job on his hands at United, who have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign.

The 20-time English champions are in the relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far.

“The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career,” Pochettino said in a statement released by US Soccer.

“We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.”

US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said the 54-year-old had left a “lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture”.

United’s next game is at the home of fierce rivals Liverpool on November 22.

World.title: Iraq to close Mandali border crossing with Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has announced the temporary closure of the Mandali border crossing with Iran, as Baghdad is under increased US pressure to limit trade channels with Tehran amid the continuing US-Iran dispute.

The crossing, in Iraq’s eastern Diyala region, is set to shut on Friday, November 13, for maintenance and technology improvements.

Iraq’s Border Ports Authority said that the work is meant to enhance operations ahead of the rainy season but did not say when the crossing will reopen.

The decision came after Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein announced that Washington had urged the closing of practically all border crossings with Iran, leaving just two open.

Hussein admitted that such limitations might have a considerable impact on Iraq’s economy, considering the extensive commerce between the two nations.

The statement comes after another incident involving Iranian aviation, in which Iraqi officials denied permission for an airplane carrying Iran’s national football team to land at Basra International Airport on November 10.

The plane returned to Iran, and the players continued their trek to Iraq by road.

The denial reportedly stemmed from US restrictions on Iranian airlines.

Baghdad has also increased its inspection of border operations and smuggling networks, as it faces pressure to put Iran-backed armed organizations under state control.

Groups like Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba continue to wield considerable power in Iraq, hampering the government’s attempts to keep the nation out of the larger regional struggle.

At the same time, Iraq reopened the Sheeb border crossing with Iran in Maysan province on November 10, after many weeks of shutdown for security and technological upgrades.

The reopening reveals that Baghdad has not implemented a complete blockade of its border with Iran.

The events reflect Iraq’s increasingly strained relationship with Washington and Tehran, as the government works to bolster national security, comply with international sanctions, and safeguard its economic interests.

As the US-Iran war continues, Baghdad is under increasing pressure to display stronger control over its borders, airspace, and armed groups while preserving vital commerce with its eastern neighbor.

World.title: Spinneys opens second Iraq branch at Baghdad’s Iraq Gate Residential Complex
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Spinneys, an international grocery chain, has launched its second branch in Baghdad, increasing its presence in Iraq with a new location at the Iraq Gate Residential Complex in the Mansour area.

The 700-square-meter grocery serves inhabitants of the complex, which has around 4,800 residential homes.

The supermarket is intended to serve as a neighborhood shopping attraction, selling groceries, fresh organic produce, bakery goods, dairy, deli items, and common home necessities.

The new facility also provides grocery delivery services, enabling consumers to have their purchases delivered straight to their homes.

The launch follows Spinneys’ introduction into the Iraqi market and is part of the company’s ambition to grow its supermarket network in Baghdad and across the nation.

Spinneys opened its first Iraqi branch at Iraq Mall in Baghdad earlier in 2026. The flagship supermarket covers more than 7,000 square metres, making it considerably larger than the new residential-focused location.

Spinneys’ activities in Iraq are overseen by Gray Mackenzie Retail Lebanon (GMRL), a retail firm founded in 1996 that manages the Spinneys supermarket brand in Lebanon and has expanded into the Iraqi market.

The Iraq Gate location features a smaller residential-focused supermarket concept, intended to enable quick shopping for residents inside the development rather than operating as a huge independent retail attraction.

The launch is another step in Spinneys’ development in Iraq, as multinational supermarket operators increase their presence in Baghdad’s retail sector.

World.title: Silicon Valley insiders nervously eye Nvidia scandal fallout
World.content:
San Francisco – Hours after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, shocked tech insiders at a conference in San Francisco saw his departure as troubling for the business but were uncertain over how heavy the impact would be.

Many were still processing the spectacular departure of the rockstar CEO, who came to embody the global boom for AI chips but fell from grace after revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, one reportedly with a Chinese spy.

“It’s a blow to I think everything and pretty much every player in (the) space, except direct competitors,” Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi said in onstage remarks.

“The culture of the company is a lot… the personality of the CEO that is there for a long time,” Ghodsi said.

A lot now “depends on who the next CEO is,” he added.

Nvidia’s board has appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to replace Huang on an interim basis, but it remains unclear who will take over in the long term.

Investors had begun taking a dimmer view of the company even before news of the scandal broke.

Nvidia’s shares have lost 13 percent of their value since Monday, and are down more than 26 percent over the past month.

One venture capitalist told AFP that the fallout from Huang’s infidelities was accelerating a correction that had already been underway.

– Show must go on –

Others were more sanguine about the industry’s prospects.

“We’re very sad to see Jensen go,” Asher Spector, the founder of an artificial intelligence startup called Flapping Airplanes, said onstage at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit.

“That said, Nvidia has been a great partner,” Spector said, adding: “We’re very optimistic.”

A lighthearted note came from an arcade game in the style of “Mortal Kombat”, which pitted tech CEOs like Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and even disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes against each other.

Other major tech companies, including Microsoft, Uber and Apple, have survived and even thrived after the departure of era-defining executives.

Still, some attendees noted that Huang’s downfall might leave competing AI chip designers circling for a chance to grab a piece of Nvidia’s market share.

“It was kind of unimaginable to us that there would be a world where Nvidia wouldn’t be the biggest player a few years from now,” Robert Wachen, the co-founder of AI computing startup Etched, said.

“But now you see there’s probably a pretty big opening” for other players in the sector, Wachen said.

– Open-model guru –

Huang’s exit has particularly rattled the open software community.

The former Nvidia chief advocated for an ecosystem that includes so-called open models, which users can download and customize to varying degrees.

That differs from leading model developers like OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, and Anthropic, which crafts Claude, both of which push for closed models.

Huang was “the leader of the pack” for open models and his departure does “create a lot of uncertainty,” Igor Babuschkin, the CEO of a startup called River AI, said.

He also led Nvidia to provide billions in financing commitments to other companies, notably a more than $100 billion data center for OpenAI, which sparked concerns about circular dealmaking and a growing tech bubble.

“Will circular deals face greater scrutiny and a reality check? Very likely,” Hivemind Capital partner Emmanuel Vallod told AFP via email.

“But does that mean the music is about to stop? I very much doubt it.”

World.title: Iraq orders only national flag at government buildings amid crackdown on militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is said to have instructed ministries, government agencies, and public institutions to show only the Iraqi national flag, with other flags prohibited from flying at official sites.

The decision comes as Baghdad steps up attempts to reinforce state authority and limit the influence of armed factions, especially those with strong links to Iran.

Iran-backed militias, such as Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, have maintained a visible presence in Iraq, with their flags and insignia seen at public meetings, roadblocks, and other armed group sites.

The alleged limitation would highlight the contrast between Iraqi state institutions and political or military groups, stressing that government buildings should represent the nation rather than specific factions.

Since entering office in May 2026, Al-Zaidi has progressively opposed militia authority, pushing for firearms to be solely controlled by the state and warning that armed organizations who refuse to comply might face legal penalties.

The government has also taken action against alleged militia-related business interests, including the cancelation of contracts at Mosul International Airport.

The moves have heightened tensions with Kataib Hezbollah and other Iran-aligned militias who oppose Baghdad’s disarmament initiatives.

The restrictions come amid ongoing regional instability in the aftermath of the US-Iran war earlier this year, which has exposed Iraq to assaults and raised pressure on the government to prevent armed groups from pulling the nation into the fight.

For Baghdad, limiting flags at official buildings would be a symbolic step toward bolstering national sovereignty. The greater question is whether the administration can transform such efforts into effective control of armed groups and their weaponry.

World.title: Iraq offers condolences to UAE after Fujairah road accident kills 14
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has sent its condolences to the United Arab Emirates after a tragic traffic accident in Fujairah that killed 14 people and wounded 30 others.

Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a statement on November 12 expressing sorrow to the UAE government, its people, and the families of those killed, confirming Baghdad’s support for the nation in the aftermath of the tragedy.

According to the UAE’s Emirates News Agency (WAM), the accident happened soon before midnight on November 11 on Sheik Khalifa bin Zayed Road, near Fujairah’s entrance.

Fujairah Police reported that a truck driver lost control and struck another car before flipping and colliding with many automobiles stuck in sluggish traffic.

A fire then broke out, spreading to surrounding automobiles.

According to UAE media outlets, the collision included 23 cars, five of which were trucks, and was one of the country’s bloodiest in recent years.

Emergency responders, including police, ambulance personnel, and Civil Defense teams, were sent to put out the fire, rescue casualties, and take the wounded to hospitals.

Fujairah Police stated that 15 wounded individuals had been released from the hospital, while another 15 were still receiving medical attention.

Authorities reportedly indicated that the dead were Emirati and international nationals, with DNA tests underway to identify some of those slain.

World.title: Microsoft battling to fix global Outlook outage
World.content:
Washington – Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.

The hours-long disruption, which Microsoft attributed to “elevated load” on its infrastructure, has hit email as well as products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Outlook.

“We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they’re not taking as expected,” Microsoft said on X.

“We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity,” the tech giant added, without saying when service was expected to be fully restored.

The disruption went global within an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.

A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

One of the impacted countries was New Zealand, where the foreign ministry sent a notice saying its “ability to receive emails has been affected by the global Microsoft outage. This also impacts all New Zealand Embassies, Consulates and Representative Offices around the world.”

Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports “in the Americas,” but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected “Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.”

Microsoft 365 is the company’s cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.

“We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors,” the company wrote on X.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” it added.

Downdetector, which tracks online outages, showed a sharp decline around 0450 GMT in users’ reports of disruptions in Washington and Hong Kong.

Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.

In one update shortly after 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT), Microsoft said it was “observing limited recovery” as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.

“As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect,” the company added.

World.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
World.content:
Houston – Elon Musk’s SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking “catch” of the spaceship following a day in orbit.

A successful capture of the Starship upper stage would mark a significant milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable spacecraft that can drastically reduce mission costs and make frequent travel possible.

“If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket,” SpaceX said.

For the 15th Starship test flight Friday, SpaceX aims to recover both stages of the massive 124-meter (407-foot) launch vehicle.

The company has caught the booster, dubbed Super Heavy, on three previous occasions, with the first stage descending vertically back to the launch site shortly after blastoff and nestling into mechanical “chopstick” arms.

It will now attempt to do the same with the spaceship. Some versions of the vessel are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while others will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.

A spacecraft that can be fully reused is the “Holy Grail” of the space industry, said Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“No one’s really been able to do that so far,” he said. “People have been trying to do that since the (NASA) space shuttle. But the space shuttle ended up being kind of a compromise because a lot of the vehicle wasn’t reusable.”

Reusing the Starship spacecraft would require the vessel to withstand the extreme heat of reentering Earth’s atmosphere and then return to service without extensive refurbishment.

– Refueling challenge –

Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which are regularly employed to launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.

The Starship project, however, has been plagued by years-long delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges — even as NASA is counting on the spaceship to serve as a lunar lander for its Artemis program.

Other technical challenges include transferring fuel to Starship in orbit — a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.

Following SpaceX’s high-profile stock market debut in June, the company carried out the first orbital flight of Starship in September, though the mission was cut short due to an engine issue.

It is also investing heavily in additional launch sites for its mega-rocket in Louisiana and Florida.

– Complex capture –

Friday’s launch is scheduled to take place at SpaceX’s “Starbase” in southern Texas at 4:45 pm (2245 GMT).

Following liftoff and the mid-air separation of the two stages, SpaceX plans to bring Super Heavy back to Earth six and a half minutes later, catching it at the launch site on the Gulf of Mexico coastline.

The spaceship will continue to reach Earth’s orbit, where it will deploy 26 satellites into Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation that has become a major revenue stream for SpaceX.

It will then circle the planet 14 times, before returning 22 hours later and — SpaceX hopes — descending safely into the chopstick arms.

This capture attempt is more complex than that of the booster, as the spaceship will be descending much faster and from a much greater altitude.

SpaceX has said it would proceed with these maneuvers only if conditions are optimal, and in the past has made last-minute changes to test flights under Musk’s “fail fast” strategy of learning through crashes, explosions and other mishaps.

As of late Thursday, the US Federal Aviation Administration had not yet given its final approval for the test flight.

World.title: Searches continue for Kulgam terrorists
World.content:
Security forces continued Friday massive cordon and search operations to track down terrorists

SRINAGAR: Security forces continued Friday massive cordon and search operations to track down terrorists who shot and injured three CRPF personnel in south Kashmirâs Kulgam district two days ago.Around 200 alleged overground workers have been picked up but all have been released after questioning, a senior police officer said.CRPF chief Gyanendra Pratap Singh visited Kulgam on Friday and reviewed the situation after Wednesdayâs strike that ended a long lull in attacks on security forces in the valley. An NIA team surveyed the attack site in Akhran area.Two of the wounded CRPF personnel have been discharged after treatment. The third, who underwent surgery for bullet wounds in his abdomen and spine, remains at an army hospital in Srinagar.

World.title: Search operations continue in J&K for killers of 2 SPOs
World.content:
JAMMU: Massive search operations continued across the treacherous Dachchan-Marwah forests of Kishtwar and adjoining areas in J&K after the security forces recovered bullet-riddled bodies of two special police officers (SPOs) a day after they went missing.

Bodies of the slain SPOs, identified as Rashpal Kumar, 45 and Bobby Chand, 57 were recovered Thursday approximately 2-3 km from the site from where they reportedly went missing.

Leader of opposition in the state, Sunil Sharma, said remnants of the terror-supporting ecosystem were still active in the region despite sustained pressure from security forces.

Meanwhile, reports circulating on social media suggested that Kishtwar police have issued posters of three wanted terrorists and announced a cash reward of Rs 30 lakh for information leading to their arrest, but there was no official confirmation yet.

NEW DELHI: Centre has made weekly stock declarations mandatory for all pulses by stockists, millers, wholesalers, retailers and large chain retailers, in a move to prevent artificial price rises and curb hoarding. The declarations will have to be uploaded every Friday onto a dedicated portal of the consumer affairs department.The move comes amid a sharp rise in pulse prices despite comfortable supply and record buffer stocks. This comes a week after the food department made weekly stock declarations mandatory for six varieties of rice.Consumer affairs secretary Nidhi Khare said the weekly reporting requirement was aimed at checking sharp price spikes, artificial supply constraints, speculative stock accumulation, hoarding and profiteering. The department has also written to states and UTs, asking them to closely monitor pulse prices and take action against hoarding and black marketing.The department has warned that misreporting of stocks will be viewed seriously and urged traders and millers to rationalise margins and pass on the benefits of favourable supply conditions to consumers.Officials said that the department, in a meeting with millers, has flagged that retail prices of some varieties of pulses were rising despite a decline or minor increase in wholesale prices, robust availability and imports.âSo, the increase is likely due to some artificial reasons, including hoarding,â said an official.Govt data show that the average retail prices of tur and gram (chana) stood at Rs 135 and Rs 95 per kg respectively on Friday, registering an increase of 19.5% and 10% from a year ago. Retail inflation in the pulses category rose to 8.7% in Oct, against a deflation of 1.7% in April 2026.Khare said chana production stood at 12.6 million tonne in the 2025-26 crop year, the second highest in five years, while mandi arrivals remained comparable with previous years. Imports of yellow peas, used as a substitute for chana, have also been higher than in previous years. In such a condition, there is no reason for any increase in retail prices.As per official assessment, stocks held by large retailers, dealers, importers, millers, stockists and traders declined from 5.9 million tonne on July 3 to 5.4 million tonne on Nov 6. The Centreâs buffer stock of pulses has touched a record 3.8 million tonne, above the norm of 3.5 million tonne.

World.title: 'Visa matters are sovereign': MEA responds after 115 foreign speakers denied nod for Congress event
World.content:
Political backlash

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday defended India's visa decisions, saying these are "sovereign functions" of every government. The response came amid allegations that more than 100 foreign speakers invited to the Congress-organised Bharat Summit in Hyderabad were denied entry into India or had their visas cancelled."I would like to say, and all of you are aware, that visa matters are sovereign functions of any country or any government. So that is what I have to say," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said during his the bi-weekly media briefing.The MEA's response came amid allegations by Congress leaders that several foreign delegates who had received prior clearance from the ministry were subsequently denied entry into India or had their visas revoked. The opposition has alleged that the decisions were taken following instructions from the Union ministry of home affairs (MHA).The two-day Bharat Summit 2026 is being held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14, bringing together around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries. Organised by the Congress and the Telangana government, the summit features discussions on global geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.The controversy has particularly brought Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng into focus, after she claimed that her Indian visa was cancelled shortly before her scheduled departure for Hyderabad, where she was due to participate in a panel discussion on media and press freedom at the Bharat Summit.In a post on X, Lyng said she had received a visa from the Indian embassy in Norway and was scheduled to travel to Hyderabad on Friday. However, she alleged that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to leave for the airport, citing "orders from above" in the ministry of home affairs.Lyng's case has also drawn attention because of her earlier interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to Oslo in May. The Norwegian journalist had questioned PM Modi on press freedom and his reluctance to take questions from journalists during the visit.The reported visa cancellations have triggered a political row, with opposition leaders questioning the government's decision and alleging that foreign journalists and speakers were being prevented from attending the international gathering.Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing him of having a dictatorial mindset over the alleged restrictions on foreign journalists attending the Bharat Summit.In a post on X, Reddy alleged that some journalists were stopped from entering India by the ministry of home Affairs despite having received visas. Questioning the reported action, he said, "Is asking Modi ji a question a crime? It is journalists' responsibility to ask questions. Whether to answer them is up to Modi ji."Defending the summit, Reddy said the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026 aimed to attract investments and generate employment for skilled and unskilled youth, while showcasing Hyderabad's cultural and technological development to representatives from 70 countries.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor also criticised the reported visa cancellations, describing them as a "disappointing footnote" to the Bharat Summit."It is completely unclear under what provision of law the government has taken such a drastic step," he said, adding that reversing the decision was impossible as the conference was scheduled to conclude the following day.Tharoor further criticised the development, saying, "What a shame that a proud democracy has become so insecure that it must stifle any voices it fears will be critical!"Meanwhile, former foreign secretary Kanwal Sibal took a contrasting position, criticising the Norwegian side over the controversy and calling its conduct "unacceptable".In a post on X, Sibal said, "The Norwegians are being very presumptuous. Trying to put us on the mat."Suggesting a tougher response, he added, "Our answer to this should be to tighten up grant of visas to Norwegian journalists."The BJP, meanwhile, defended the visa cancellations, branding the gathering an "Anti-Bharat Summit" and accusing the Congress of bringing together radical Left and anti-India groups.

World.title: Bengaluru researchers develop chip that could help make 6G networks faster
World.content:
BENGALURU: As the world prepares for the next generation of wireless communication, researchers are working on a problem that could determine how fast future networks become: how to keep signals strong as they travel through increasingly compact devices.

A team from Bengaluruâs Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) has developed a silicon chip that could help solve this problem. The chip allows high-frequency signals to pass through deliberately created barriers and sharp turns without losing much of their strength, while carrying data at speeds of up to 100 gigabits per second.

The development could contribute to building smaller and more efficient circuits for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks, which are expected to use terahertz waves to transmit large amounts of data.



Terahertz waves occupy a part of the electromagnetic spectrum between microwaves and infrared light. They can carry much more information than the frequencies used by today's wireless networks. But working with these waves presents a challenge. When they encounter bends, junctions or obstacles inside a circuit, some of their energy can scatter or bounce back, weakening the signal.

The JNCASR team found a way to overcome this using a specially designed silicon structure.





They arranged tiny triangular holes in the silicon in a pattern that allows terahertz signals to travel along a defined path. By changing the sizes of these holes over a short section, they created a barrier that the signals could cross with very little loss.

In their experiments, a single barrier reduced the signal by just 1-2%, while two barriers placed one after another resulted in a loss of only 2-3%. In conventional circuits, similar obstacles can significantly weaken signals.

Researchers tested the technology in three different chip designs, including one that routed signals through four sharp bends and another that split a signal into two pathways. The devices were tested at frequencies between 310 and 360 gigahertz.

In data transmission experiments, one of the devices achieved speeds of 100 gigabits per second using a technique that allows information to be encoded through changes in a signal's strength and phase.

At this speed, a 5GB high-definition film could theoretically be transferred in less than half a second.

âShowing that terahertz waves can cross a barrier created simply by changing the hole geometry, while carrying 100 gigabits per second, suggests that this effect can become a useful design tool for terahertz chips,â said Abhishek Kumar, assistant professor at JNCASR, who led the study.

The team included Samina Mulla and Sangram Kumar Sadhu as joint first authors, along with collaborators from research institutions in India, Singapore and France.

An important aspect of the work is that the chip is made using high-resistivity silicon, a material compatible with established semiconductor manufacturing processes. This could make it easier to translate the research into practical devices.

The findings, published in the journal Advanced Materials, could help develop compact circuits capable of directing and splitting terahertz signals on a single chip. Researchers now plan to explore ways of controlling the barriers using electrical, thermal or mechanical changes, potentially allowing signals to be redirected between different paths when required.

World.title: Delhi ministers order 50% staff to work from home as air quality worsens
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday directed 50 per cent of the workforce in his departments to work from home amid worsening air quality in the nation capital, news agency PTI reported citing official sources

Under the Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan, the Commission for Air Quality Management has asked the Delhi government and other NCR state governments s to consider allowing public, municipal and private offices to operate with 50 per cent staff strength, with the remaining employees working from home.

"Going by CAQM guidelines on air quality, heads of departments are free to take decisions regarding allowing work from home. Essential services will not be covered in this," a government official said.

Transport minister Pankaj Singh has also directed departments under his charge, including health and family welfare and information technology, to adopt work-from-home arrangements.

According to the PTI report, the Centre is also likely to allow its employees to work from home under the revised GRAP schedule.

Delhi's air quality remained in the very poor category on Friday, with the AQI recorded at 373 at 4 pm. A thick blanket of smog enveloped the city, reducing visibility and leaving many residents complaining of breathing difficulties.

World.title: BPCL says E20 petrol samples across 27 states pass quality test, clarifies viral test image
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited on Friday said all E20 petrol samples tested across 27 states and Union Territories were found to be within the prescribed ethanol content range of 19-21%.

The clarification came amid concerns triggered by a photograph shared during the company's consumer awareness initiative in Karnataka, which showed an ethanol separation test being conducted at one of its fuel stations.

In a statement, BPCL said the quality monitoring exercise was carried out by oil marketing companies in coordination with the Centre for High Technology. The company tested 280 samples as part of the exercise.



BPCL said its officers had been conducting demonstrations across Karnataka to address consumer queries about E20 petrol and explain the testing procedure.

The test involves mixing 100 ml of E20 Ethanol Blended Motor Spirit (EBMS) with 30 ml of water to separate ethanol from petrol.

"The mixture initially appears hazy or milky, which is normal during the process. It takes time for the ethanol-water and petrol layers to separate completely," the company said.





Explaining the photograph that triggered concerns, BPCL said it was inadvertently captured and shared before the separation process was complete, showing an intermediate stage of the test rather than the final reading.

"The image therefore reflected an intermediate stage of the test and not the final reading," BPCL said.

The company added that the officer concerned promptly removed the post after realising that it could be misinterpreted.

It maintained that the sample tested was within the prescribed specifications.

BPCL said the quality of E20 petrol supplied through its retail outlets was monitored through established quality assurance mechanisms in accordance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specifications under IS 17021.

World.title: From Australian chana to Canadian masoor: NITI Aayog flags India's food import dependence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India may not yet be fully secure in meeting its food requirements, with heavy dependence on imports for essential commodities such as edible oils and pulses,

vice-chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri said on Friday.

Speaking at an event in Delhi, Lahiri said India imports more than half of its edible oil requirements and relies on other countries for several pulses.

He questioned whether the country was sufficiently prepared to deal with disruptions in global supplies and sudden price increases.

"We are talking about Viksit Krishi in Viksit Bharat in 2047. As we move towards Viksit Bharat at 2047, are we secure regarding our food supply across the various products? Perhaps not as yet," he said.



Lahiri said he was surprised to learn that chana (gram) consumed in India comes from Australia, while masoor dal is imported from Australia and Canada. Some pulses also come from Myanmar, African countries and Russia, according to news agency PTI.

"Now you can ask what is wrong with India importing edible oils or oil seeds from Indonesia, Malaysia, Argentina, Brazil, Russia, and Ukraine, and pulses from Australia, Canada, Myanmar, Africa, and Russia," Lahiri said.





"The problem is, first, the issue of vulnerability to global supply disruptions or price shocks," he added.

India meets more than half of its edible oil demand through imports. These imports are estimated at 17 million metric tonnes, worth around $20 billion, Lahiri said.

India is also the world's largest producer and consumer of pulses, accounting for nearly a fourth of global consumption. The country consumes around 25-27 million tonnes of pulses every year.

"For our dal-chawal or dal-roti, we require pulses and edible oils. Any disruption of supply of these essential commodities or price shock can assume the gravity of a strategic disaster," he said.

Lahiri said reducing dependence on imports would require greater focus on domestic production of pulses and edible oils. He pointed to the need to diversify crops and reduce the dominance of wheat and paddy in Indian agriculture.

World.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election plea against Udhayanidhi’s win from Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni
World.content:
The Madras High Court on Friday (November 13, 2026) refused to reject an election petition filed by P. Milany of Theni district, challenging the victory of Leader of the Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin from the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni Assembly constituency in the 2026 general elections.

Justice G. Arul Murugan dismissed two applications filed by the LoP urging the court to reject the election petition and strike off substantial pleadings made by the election petitioner. The judge decided to proceed with the trial and directed the applicant to file his reply statement by December 11, 2026.

He disagreed with Mr. Udhayanidhi that the day of declaration of election result must also be taken into account while calculating the limitation period of 45 days for filing an election petition and therefore, the present election petition must be dismissed for having been filed on the 46th day.

The judge said, a three-judge Bench of the Supreme Court in Tarun Prasad Chatterjee versus Dinanath Sharma (2000) had categorically held that Section 9 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 would apply to election petitions too and so the day of declaration of result must be excluded while calculating the limitation period.

Though Mr. Udhayanidhi’s counsel relied upon a subsequent decision of the Supreme Court in Youaraj Rai versus Chander Bahadur Karki (2006), Justice Murugan said, such reliance was “misplaced” since the applicability of Section 9 of the General Clauses Act was not an issue that had to be decided in the case.

The judge further held that the other grounds raised by the election petitioner were triable issues which could not be decided without letting in evidence and therefore, the LOP had not made out a case either for striking out the pleadings or for rejecting the election petition at the threshold.

The applicant was declared elected on securing 62,992 votes as against his nearest rival candidate D. Selvam of the TVK, who had garnered 55,852 votes. However, the election petition was filed by another candidate, Mr. Milany, who too had contested from the constituency as an Independent and secured 30 votes.

The election petitioner had challenged the victory of Mr. Udhayanidhi on grounds such as alleged suppression of his assets in the election affidavit, improper acceptance of his nomination form due to certain discrepancies in the attestation made by a notary public and so on.

Though the LoP denied all charges levelled against him by the election petitioner, the judge said, the veracity of the allegations could be ascertained only after a full fledged trial. The judge said, the pleadings in the election petition could not be termed as “unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous or vexatious” in order to strike them off.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government would implement the Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024 and initiate the provision of clearances to industries in real time based on self-certification to encourage investors, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has said, adding that the proposed law would be passed in the coming session of the Legislative Assembly.

Addressing the media after the valedictory of the 31st CII Partnership Summit here on Friday, Mr. Naidu said there was a pressing need for good governance and that investors needed to be reassured about the safety of their investments in the event of a regime change. This was “keeping in view the ruin caused between 2019 and 2024”, which aggravated the impact of State bifurcation.

The government would be liberal in facilitating businesses, but not be lenient in ensuring accountability for the support being availed, Mr. Naidu said, noting that while mobilising investments with due sense of urgency, it was ensuring that they would take tangible shape as per the committed timelines.

Besides, the compliance burden was being reduced to make doing business far more easier. Due focus was being laid on making the agriculture sector resilient, as the government could not afford to lay the whole emphasis on the industrial sector only. Both sectors are crucial to increase the Gross State Domestic Product, he said.

The Chief Minister said that the State attracted investments of nearly ₹9.88 lakh crore through 303 MoUs during the current edition of the CII Partnership Summit and that they have the potential to generate approximately 3,49 lakh jobs across sectors. The cumulative investments that were tied up since June 2024 has reached ₹32.49 lakh crore.

“Andhra Pradesh is hogging the limelight, with its distinct advantages for investors and the potential of the three economic regions of Amaravati, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam,” he said.

The government was extending all possible support for businesses in emerging sectors to thrive, and a priority has been accorded to development of the space sector around India’s only spaceport at Sriharikota, he said.

Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu; MPs T. Krishna Prasad and M. Sribharat; Ministers T.G. Bharat, K. Atchannaidu, P. Narayana, Kollu Ravindra, Kondapalli Srinivas, Kolusu Parthasarathy and Satya Kumar Yadav were present.

World.title: Take steps to control inflation, Anbumani Ramadoss tells State govt.
World.content:
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Friday criticised the State Government for achieving the “highest inflation of 7.29% in October” among all other States in India as per the Statistics released by the Union Government.

In a statement, he said the poor and middle class families are facing severe hardship due to rising prices of essential food commodities, including rice, pulses and edible oils.

“While the national inflation rate has increased to 6.09%, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India’s tolerance limit of 6%, Tamil Nadu’s inflation rate is 1.20 percentage points higher. The statistics also reveal that rural populations have been more severely affected by inflation than their urban counterparts,” he said.

Dr. Anbumani further said prices of essential commodities, particularly rice, have increased to unaffordable levels in Tamil Nadu compared to other states and said that sharp increase in rice prices have resulted in rise in inflation.

“The government has failed to take any meaningful action. The scheme to supply onions at subsidised rates through ration shops has failed. Similarly, the government’s announcement that fine-quality rice would be supplied at Rs.30 per kg failed to receive public support because the rice distributed was merely polished ration-shop rice. These failures have contributed to Tamil Nadu’s inflation reaching such a high level,” he said.

Dr. Anbumani added that people cannot be expected to withstand further increase in prices of essential commodities when per capita income in Tamil Nadu has been declining.

World.title: Fee reimbursement dues pushing students into distress in Andhra, says Jagan
World.content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy held Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh responsible for a student's attempt to end life at a private engineering college in Chittoor district, alleging that the government's failure to clear fee reimbursement dues was pushing students into distress.

In a post on X on Friday, Mr. Jagan said students had taken to the streets, alleging that non-payment of college fees had driven a student to resort to the extreme step. He claimed that similar incidents had occurred at the same college in the past.

Accusing the government of being indifferent to students' plights, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy demanded that the Chief Minister stop diverting attention from the issue and take responsibility.

He alleged that the coalition government had weakened the Vidya Deevena and Vasathi Deevena schemes introduced during the YSRCP’s tenure to support students from economically weaker sections in pursuing higher education.

Putting the dues under the two schemes at ₹12,400 crore, Mr. Jagan said 13 quarters of Vidya Deevena payments, amounting to ₹9,100 crore at ₹700 crore per quarter, would be due by the end of the academic year. Another ₹3,300 crore was pending under Vasathi Deevena for April 2024, 2025 and 2026.

He said the government had paid only ₹2,800 crore in two instalments, leaving more than ₹9,600 crore unpaid.

He alleged that colleges were pressuring students to pay fees and threatening to prevent them from appearing for examinations or to withhold certificates. Some students had discontinued their education or taken up jobs, while others were facing severe distress, he said.

Mr. Jagan demanded that the Chief Minister relieve Mr. Lokesh of the HRD portfolio, clear the arrears immediately and ensure that colleges did not put pressure on students.

World.title: Madurai jewellery heist: quantum of lost valuables decreases to 10 kg gold, 1 kg diamond
World.content:
A day after representatives of a Tanishq showroom in Madurai complained that 15 kg gold and 3 kg diamond ornaments had been stolen in a heist, they informed the police on Friday that only 10 kg gold and 1 kg diamond ornaments had been looted.

The new estimate had been arrived at based on further assessment of the valuables left on display and those retrieved intact from the showroom, Commissioner of Police S. Rajendiran told The Hindu.

Around 42 kg jewellery, including diamonds, were on display on the first floor of the newly-inaugurated showroom on Bypass Road.

The police suspect that the lone burglar may have decided to steal only as much as he could carry, considering the difficulty in climbing to the top of the lift shaft through which he had entered the premises.

The burglar had meticulously accomplished his stealth task by sneaking into the tall building and coming out with the valuables without having not been noticed by anyone.

They also suspect that he may have studied the topography of the building.

Earlier attempt

CCTV footage had also shown the masked man climbing onto the terrace using a scaffolding on the night of November 5. The Commissioner said it may have been a failed burglary attempt.

City police are leaving no stone unturned as they have got very little clue except the CCTV footage of the lone burglar collecting the jewellery inside the showroom. The police could not identify him as he had covered his face and had also left no fingerprints by wearing gloves.

The police have not ruled out the possibility of an inside job. Special teams are interrogating the employees of the showroom and those involved in its construction, interior design and installation of the lift.

“As of now, we have kept our options open,” said Commissioner of Police, S. Rajendiran.

“Only an abled body with good recce of the showroom, could have succeeded in such a crime,” said a senior police officer. The burglar had spent some one hour in the early hours of Thursday for his completing his task.

Security lapses

Mr. Rajendiran said certain lapses in the security arrangements, including the failure to switch on the anti-burglary alarm on Wednesday night and to check CCTV footage, and negligence on the part of the security personnel had gone in favour of the burglar.

World.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
World.content:
Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.

The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Also Read | Why climate finance remains a recurring flashpoint at UN summits

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.

Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”

Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.

For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.

Meanwhile, defence spending has climbed significantly.

The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Also Read | UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards

COP31 seeking implementation, not new targets

As they ​respond to the contemporary mood, host country Turkiye and lead negotiator Australia have emphasised making previous pledges work, rather than securing a new headline target at the conference, which continues until the end of next week.

“COP31 must respond to ⁠the global moment and send a clear message to accelerate implementation,” Australia’s COP31 negotiating president Chris Bowen said. He also said finance must be “faster, simpler and fairer”.

Analysis by previous COP host Brazil published earlier this week found that $137 billion was mobilised in 2024, a slight increase on 2023, but that ‌direct aid and future commitments to multilateral funds were lower.

Current trends suggested provision would fall $840 billion short of the $1.3 trillion goal, it said.

“Geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal space in many developing countries and the high cost of capital where it is most needed are among the obstacles,” the report said.

By way of solutions, it urged measures such as risk-sharing and clearer links between national plans and budgets.

Some smaller nations have taken novel steps to find cash and to spur richer nations to match it.

The Solomon Islands pledged $400,000 from its own pocket on Thursday (November 13, 2026), saying it was determined to show leadership and calling on rich countries to do the same.

The Bahamas committed $75 million to protect and restore its seagrass meadows, which ‌store carbon, to try to persuade investors to fund verified carbon projects.

The Hindu Editorial | New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals

Unclogging the system to get money flowing

Both public and private funding provide climate finance grants, loans, ​aid and investment in measures ranging from renewable energy to flood defences.

Multilateral development banks are a conduit for finance that leverages capital provided by shareholder countries to increase lending power and they say they are delivering. Their lending reached record ⁠levels in 2025, according to the European Investment Bank.

But, they could do more, according to Washington-based think tank the Center for Global Development and recipients ⁠of the finance have said the development banks should make access easier.

Addressing that, a group of multilateral funds told the COP31 talks they would rely more on one another’s assessments in co-financed operations rather than having to go through multiple overlapping processes.

For private investors, ‌the most obvious issue is the risk of investing in an instrument that does not guarantee returns.

Given how unforthcoming the world’s richer governments have been, the private sector is ever more important.

“Our clients see opportunities in the energy transition, but they need reliable ​power, predictable costs and confidence in customer demand before they invest,” HSBC Chief Sustainability Officer Julian Wentzel said. “COP31 needs to help create that confidence.”

World.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
World.content:
The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.

At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.

The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Recovery underway: Microsoft

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Around 8 p.m. IST on Friday (November 13, 2026), Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform at Microsoft, said, "We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure. We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward."

The company said it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the disruption and promised that it would publish a detailed report on the root cause and corrective measures after services were restored.

Public services hit

In some countries, government services were affected by the outage.

Singapore’s Government Technology Agency and Japanese Ministries reported email disruptions, according to local media reports and official notices.

In Britain, Rachel Harrison of the GMB Union said National Health Service staff handling emergency calls could not refer to patient details as they normally would, creating a “massive backlog”. Britain’s National Pharmacy Association said the outage delayed prescriptions, AFP reported.

What industry leaders say

Sai Rahul Poruri, CEO of FOSS United, said India should reduce dependence on external technology providers. He called for a more diverse provider ecosystem, citing Germany’s approach of allowing individual regions to choose their email providers, many of which use free and open-source software.

Sambratha Shetty, chief operating officer of Synergia Foundation, said disruption could delay client deliveries and expose IT firms and global capability centres in Bengaluru to service-level agreement penalties. She called for backup channels, multiple providers, and tested continuity plans.

Ben Mudie, field chief technology officer for APAC at cybersecurity firm Tenable, warned that employees could turn to personal email accounts and unauthorised file-sharing services when workplace systems become unavailable, potentially exposing sensitive company information.

World.title: Modi comes to aid of elderly woman who felt unwell at Mysuru event
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi personally came to the aid of an elderly woman who felt unwell during the inauguration of the COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru on Friday.

The woman, Prema Simbaiah, former president of Nanjangud Town Municipality and a BJP worker, appeared to feel dizzy and was on the verge of collapsing. Noticing her condition, Mr. Modi went up to her and ensured that she received immediate attention. She was given juice to help her recover.

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman was also present at the event.

Mysuru district BJP president Subbanna later visited Ms. Simbaiah at her residence to enquire about her health. He said she was doing well.

Thanking Mr. Modi for coming to her aid, Ms. Simbaiah said she had felt uncomfortable as she had not had lunch before arriving at the venue. She expressed her gratitude to the Prime Minister for providing her with juice and ensuring that she recovered.

World.title: President House says matters related to provinces did not come under discussion during Zardari, Naqvi meeting
World.content:
The President House on Friday refuted media reports about yesterday’s meeting between President Asif Ali Zardari and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, saying that discussions focused on national security and regional situation.

The clarification comes after several media reports emerged claiming that Naqvi and the president had discussed the formation of new provinces during a meeting in Nawabshah on Thursday night. No official handout was issued about the meeting.

“There is no truth to media reports suggesting that matters concerning the provinces were discussed during the interior minister’s meeting with the president,” the President House said in a statement.

“Matters concerning national security and the regional situation were discussed during the meeting. However, no discussion took place on matters related to provinces,” the statement added.

The security czar has whipped up a political storm over the past few months since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Earlier this week, Naqvi reaffirmed his stance on the creation of new provinces or administrative units. He suggested that political parties should hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on this matter, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate.

However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move for new provinces.

In September, the Sindh Assembly adopted a resolution rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units , with the CM Murad declaring that “there will be no compromise on Sindh’s geographical unity”.

Meanwhile, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has called for a “full stop” on the debate surrounding new provinces and also a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”.

In his remarks on Thursday, Naqvi contended that he and Bilawal were “nearly on the same page”.

“He [Bilawal] said that political matters are about to be reset, while my suggestion is that overall matters are about to be reset,” Naqvi said.

World.title: Petrol price cut by by Rs2; high-speed diesel price remains unchanged
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs2 per litre, marking its ninth consecutive decrease, while the high-speed diesel rate was unchanged at Rs360 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs330 per litre from Nov 14 (Saturday) to Nov 16 (Monday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Turkiye, Qatar sign defence agreement: Turkish presidency
World.content:
Turkiye and Qatar signed a defence agreement on Friday that President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said would further strengthen ties between the regional allies, his office said.

The announcement came after Erdogan met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul.

Qatar’s ruler travelled to Istanbul after attending the United Nations COP31 climate summit in southern Turkiye.

“A mutual defence agreement signed by Turkiye and Qatar today will add a new dimension to the brotherly ties between the two countries,” Erdogan said during the meeting, according to a statement from his office.

The statement gave no further details about the contents of the agreement.

Erdogan also said Turkiye and Qatar would expand cooperation in the defence industry. The two countries would continue working together “to prevent a renewed outbreak of war in the Gulf region and to promote dialogue and peace”, he said.

The leaders also discussed Israel’s attacks on Gaza and the humanitarian situation in the Palestinian territory, efforts towards normalisation in Syria and the latest developments in Libya, the statement added.

According to a joint communique issued by Qatar’s foreign ministry following a session of the Supreme Strategic Committee between Qatar and Turkiye, the agreement aims to strengthen collective defence, promote regional security and stability, and present “a unified stance in confronting any external armed attack targeting either party or both of them”.

As per the statement, the two sides reiterated that the agreement reflected their “shared vision of contributing to a more secure and stable regional order”.

In August, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Makkah, bringing together the Sunni Muslim US allies at a time of conflict across the region.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement last week, clearing the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which has been struggling to fend off attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

Under the agreement, signed by the three regional powers in August, an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.

World.title: Pakistan aiming to become competitive destination for long-term investment, CDF Munir tells minerals moot
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Friday that Pakistan was aiming to become a competitive destination for long-term mineral investment.

He made the remarks while addressing the participants of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 in Islamabad, according to state-run Radio Pakistan. Delegations, exhibitors and attendees have arrived from across the world to attend the event.

As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.

On Friday, CDF Munir said all possible measures were being taken to ensure the security of the entire mining ecosystem. He said mines and miners, investments, industries, projects and all associated people would be provided adequate protection, the Radio Pakistan report said.

He added that harnessing Pakistan’s mineral wealth was a collective national objective. He also emphasised that the country’s goal was not merely to export raw materials but to develop the entire value chain, including refining and manufacturing, it added.

CDF Munir also said that Pakistan sought to foster long-term partnerships that created sustainable economic value for the country and its partners.

“He stressed that mineral development must benefit local communities, adding that people living in mineral-rich areas should witness tangible improvements in their lives,” the report said. He also emphasised that Pakistan must move from potential to productivity, from promises to action and from raw exports to value-added growth.

PM expresses hope for Pakistan’s economy

Addressing the same event, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed the hope that Pakistan could become the world’s sixth-largest economy “earlier than 2050”.

In his remarks, he recalled a Goldman Sachs assessment, which had projected Pakistan to become the sixth-largest economy in the world by 2075 and said: “I would like to make a small amendment here — instead of 2075, it will be earlier than 2050.”

He commended the hard work of the petroleum minister in organising the forum and specially acknowledged CDF Munir and his team, saying that his invaluable support and untiring efforts had “placed Pakistan’s mines and minerals agenda at the heart of our economic vision”.

The premier highlighted that the production of copper and gold at Reko Diq on the Tethyan copper belt was expected to commence in 2028 after having stalled for about two decades.

He renewed a commitment he made at last year’s forum to end the practice of shipping Pakistan’s minerals out of the country in raw form, saying, “That day is not far away when this will come to a grinding halt.”

Instead of simply extracting and exporting raw minerals, he expressed his desire for Reko Diq and every project along the Tethyan belt to establish “refineries, smelters, cable and conductor factories — the industries that will connect Pakistan with the rest of the world”.

He called on the investors present to “mine in Pakistan, process in Pakistan, manufacture in Pakistan, and then export to the rest of the world”, terming it a “win-win partnership” for everyone.

Regarding Pakistan’s efforts to meet investor expectations, PM Shehbaz highlighted that the country was simplifying procedures, “eliminating red tape, cutting inordinate delays and ensuring complete transparency in awarding licences and contracts”.

He added that through digitisation of records and the National Minerals Data Centre, investors would be able to know what was beneath the ground before committing “a single dime or yuan” to projects.

The prime minister stressed that the federal and provincial governments would work in a unified fashion to provide “all necessary support” to investors to promote their business in the country.

He acknowledged that the safety and protection of manpower, assets and supply routes was “the paramount responsibility” of the government and expressed his commitment to fulfilling it.

“Your safety is our safety and your protection is our protection.”

PM Shehbaz underscored the need for the cooperation of local communities as well as the availability of reliable infrastructure, power, water, roads, rail and communications to help investments thrive.

He also declared, “If any file gets stuck due to bureaucratic delays or cumbersome procedures, bring it straight to me. I will personally ensure that it moves at lightning speed.”

The premier highlighted the country’s youth population as its “real wealth”. He urged investors to build skilled training centres and vocational institutes so that these young people could become skilled professionals, innovators and entrepreneurs.

“Every investment in mining must translate into local jobs, local businesses, local contractors; into schools, clinics, clean drinking water, and above all for a better life for the communities where these investments are being undertaken,” he stressed.

He added that his government and the provinces would work alongside the investors to ensure that those living nearest to these sites would be the main beneficiaries of these economic activities.

The premier also underscored the need for responsible mining in line with international standards, saying that “development and environmental protection must go hand in hand”. He said the mining projects would be carried out with “state-of-the-art” technology while protecting Pakistan’s water, land and the health and safety of workers.

In this regard, he said, he had directed “every relevant ministry and department” to provide a responsible point of contact to investors with the authority to resolve their issues without any delay, enabling speedy implementation of their plans.

He reiterated that the government and all institutions “will stand with you like a rock at every step”, inviting investors to visit Pakistan and promising that “we will roll out the red carpet for you”.

“Together, we will turn Pakistan’s mineral wealth into mutually beneficial economic cooperation, industrial growth and shared prosperity,” he said.

‘Mineral exploration increasingly focused on strategic resources’

Earlier in the day, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik addressed the forum and stated that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were increasingly focused on minerals that were of strategic importance to global investors.

In continuation of the pitch, Malik told the investors that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were being complemented with “modern geochemical and geophysical surveys, exploratory drilling, and upgrading of our geoscience advanced research laboratories with sophisticated analytical technologies”.

Here, he particularly mentioned the exploration of copper and gold in Chagai and western Balochistan to lithium, tin and tungsten in Gilgit-Baltistan and antimony and base metals in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

He said Pakistan had been exporting raw ore and importing the finished products to meet its requirements for a long time.

“We are now advancing copper smelting to capture more of the value chain from the mine to the finished metal,” he added.

The minister said Pakistan was also strengthening the scientific foundation of its mineral sector through the Geological Survey of Pakistan.

“The government’s accelerated geological mapping programme, including detailed surveys at a scale of 1:50,000, is helping identify mineral prospects across the country.”

The minister further said that through international technical cooperation, including the UK Pakistan Geoscience Capacity Building Programme, “we are strengthening expertise in digital mapping, airborne surveys and mineral assessment”.

“We are also digitising decades of geological information to give investors greater access to reliable data, reduce exploration uncertainty, and enable informed investment decisions,” he continued.

The petroleum minister highlighted that discovering a mineral deposit was only the initial stage and a commercially viable mine required electricity, water, roads, railways and access to international markets.

“That is why infrastructure development is aligned with our mineral ambitions,” he explained. In this context, he described the planned upgrade of the Rohri-Nokundi railway corridor, connectivity to Port Qasim and the development of supporting infrastructure around Reko Diq as “important steps” towards connecting Pakistan’s mineral-rich regions with the global markets.

He said, “Our objective is very clear: to build not just individual mines, but an integrated, competitive and sustainable mineral industry.

“Where it is commercially and technically viable, we want investment to support processing, refining, downstream industry, technology transfer and integration into the global value chains.

“We want this industry to build Pakistani capability as it grows through technical skills, vocational training, engineering services, a stronger base for Pakistani suppliers and real career opportunities for young people, including women entering the sector for the first time.”

But, he contended, none of this would hold together without the communities in our producing regions. “Projects that earn the trust of the communities around them are, in our experience, the projects that actually get built and sustained.”

World.title: Barrick Mining expresses interest in mineral processing industries in Karachi, Gwadar
World.content:
The delegation from the Barrick Mining Corporation on Friday expressed strong interest in investing in the establishment of mineral processing industries in Karachi and Gwadar.

The development came as the delegation, led by Chairman John Thornton, held a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said on X.

According to the PMO, the visiting delegation described the decision by the prime minister and the government to hold a minerals conference as an important step towards mineral development in Pakistan.

“The delegation expressed strong interest in investing in the establishment of mineral processing industries in Karachi and Gwadar,” the statement added.

It quoted the premier as saying that Pakistan was a country rich in natural resources and mineral wealth. He said that harnessing these resources to develop the province and improve the prosperity of its people was the government’s top priority.

“Major projects such as Reko Diq will create new opportunities for employment, skills development and economic growth for the people of Balochistan,” PM Shehbaz said.

Pakistan was committed to putting its vast mineral resources to use and creating new opportunities for global investment, he added.

The prime minister further said that the Reko Diq project was an important milestone for investment in Pakistan’s mineral sector and was of key importance to the country’s economic future.

“The success of the Reko Diq project will set a benchmark for future mineral investment in Pakistan,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that to develop the mineral sector, the government of Pakistan was creating a favourable environment based on “trade, investment, infrastructure and modern technology”.
